18.34: The master became very angry. He handed the slave over to some men to punish him until he paid back everything he owed.
18.35: My heavenly Father will treat you the same way if each of you does not forgive his brother or sister from his heart. "

19.1: When Jesus finished saying these words, he left the Galilee. He went to the part of Judea which is on the other side of the Jordan River.
19.2: Large crowds followed him. Jesus healed some of them there.
19.3: Some Pharisees came to Jesus. They were testing him with this question: " Is it all right for a man to divorce his wife for any reason? "
19.4: Jesus answered, " You have read this: 'In the beginning, when God created people, he made them male and female. '
19.5: He said, 'A man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife. The husband and wife will become one flesh. '
19.6: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Man must not separate what God has joined together. "
19.7: The Pharisees said to Jesus, " Then why did Moses give this command: 'A man who divorces his wife must give her divorce papers. '? "
19.8: Jesus said to them, " Your hearts were hard so Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but it was not like that from the very beginning.
19.9: I am telling you, unless her sexual sin is the reason, if a man divorces his wife and marries another woman, he is committing unlawful sexual intercourse. "
19.10: Jesus' students said to him, " If this is the true relationship between a husband and his wife, it would be better not to marry! "
19.11: But Jesus said to them, " Not everyone can accept this teaching - only those to whom it has been given.
19.12: There are some men who cannot have sexual relations; they were born like this. Others were made that way by man. And some did this to themselves because of the kingdom of heaven. Let the person who is able to accept it accept it. "
19.13: Then some people brought their small children to Jesus, so that he could put his hands on them and pray. But his students told the people not to do this.
19.14: Jesus said, " Let the little children come to me. Don't stop them because the kingdom of heaven belongs to people who are like these children. "
19.15: Then Jesus placed his hands on them. Later he left there.
19.16: A man came to Jesus and asked, " Teacher, what good thing must I do to get eternal life? "
19.17: Jesus said to him, " Why are you asking me about goodness? God is the only One who is good. Since you want to enter eternal life, obey the commands of God. "
19.18: The man said to Jesus, " Which commands? " Jesus said, " 'You must not commit murder. ' 'You must not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. ' 'You must not steal. ' 'You must not lie. '
19.19: 'You must honor and obey your father and your mother. ' 'You must give yourself to other people, for their good, expecting nothing in return, the same way you give to yourself. ' "
19.20: However, the young man said to Jesus, " But I have obeyed all these things! What do I still need to do? "
19.21: Jesus answered him, " If you want to be all that God wants you to be, go sell everything you have and give the money to the poor people. Then you will have a treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me! "
19.22: When the young man heard these words, he went away sad because he owned many things and he wanted to keep them.
19.23: Jesus said this to his students, " I am telling you the truth: it will be hard for a person with lots of money to enter the kingdom of heaven!
19.24: I am telling you again: it will be easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. "
19.25: When Jesus' students heard this, they were very surprised. They asked, " Then who can be saved? "
19.26: Jesus looked into their eyes and said, " For men, this is impossible but for God, all things are possible! "
19.27: Then Peter answered Jesus, " Look, we have left everything and followed you! What will there be for us? "
19.28: Jesus said to them, " I am telling you the truth: you have followed me. At the time when things will be made right, when I sit on my glorious throne, you will also sit on twelve thrones. You will judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
19.29: Every person who has left his home, brothers, sisters, father, mother, children, or fields, because of my name, will receive many rewards and, after that person dies, he will receive eternal life with God.
19.30: Many people who seem as if they are not important now will be important at that time. Those who seem important now will not be important then. "

20.1: " The kingdom of heaven is like the man who owned some land. He went out early in the morning to hire some workers for his vineyard.
20.2: He agreed to pay them one silver coin per day. Then he sent them into his vineyard.
20.3: At about nine o'clock in the morning, he went out again and saw some men standing around in the marketplace. They were not working.
20.4: He said to them, 'You go into my vineyard, too. I will pay you whatever is fair. '
20.5: So they went. In the same way, the owner went out about noon and again around three o'clock in the afternoon.
20.6: About five o'clock in the afternoon, he went out and found some more men standing around. He asked them, 'Why have you been standing around here all day long? Why weren't you working? '
20.7: They answered him, 'Because no one hired us. ' He said to them, 'You go into my vineyard, too. '
20.8: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his manager. 'Call the workers and give them their pay. ' He began paying the ones who had come to work last before the ones who came first.
20.9: The men who came to work at five o'clock received one silver coin each!
20.10: The men who came to work first thought they would be paid more than a silver coin, but they also received only one silver coin.
20.11: They took the money, but they began to complain against the owner of the farm.
20.12: They said, 'The men who came last worked only one hour. You are paying them the same amount as us! We did most of the work all day long - and it was hot, too! '
20.13: But the owner said to one, 'Friend, I was not unfair to you. You agreed to work for me for one silver coin.
20.14: Take this coin. It belongs to you. Go! I want to give to this man who came to work last the same amount that I gave to you.
20.15: It is not wrong for me to do what I desire with what is mine! Do you have a jealous eye because I am generous? '
20.16: The people who seem as though they are not important now will be important later. Those who seem important now will not be important then. "
20.17: Jesus was ready to go up to Jerusalem. Along the road, he took the twelve students aside. He said to them,
20.18: " Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem. The most important priests and the teachers of the law will turn against me. They will condemn me to death.
20.19: Then they will give me to non - Jewish men who will laugh at me, beat me with whips, and nail me to a stake. However, I will rise from death on the third day. "
20.20: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee, Jacob and John, came to Jesus with her sons. She bowed down and asked him for something.
20.21: Jesus said to her, " What do you want? " She said to him, " Promise me that these two sons of mine will sit on thrones in your kingdom, one at your right side and one at your left side. "
20.22: Jesus answered them, " You don't know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup of suffering which I am about to drink? " They said to Jesus, " We are able. "
20.23: Jesus said to them, " Yes, you will drink from the cup of suffering which I will drink, but the privilege of sitting at my right side or my left side is not mine to give. Instead, those places belong to those for whom my Father prepared them. "
20.24: When the other ten delegates heard about this, they were very angry with the two brothers.
20.25: Jesus called for them and said, " You know that the rulers of the world lord it over their people. Important men use their authority over them,
20.26: but you must not think that way. Instead, if one of you wants to be great, that person should be your servant.
20.27: If one of you wants to be important, he should be your slave.
20.28: I did not come to be served. Instead, I came to serve and to give my life to pay the price for many people's sins. "
20.29: As they were coming out of Jericho, a large crowd was following Jesus.
20.30: Two blind men were sitting beside the road. When these men heard that Jesus was passing by, they shouted, " Lord! Son of David! Please help us! "
20.31: Some of the people told them to be quiet. But they shouted even louder, " Lord! Son of David! Please help us! "
20.32: Jesus stopped there and called for them. He asked, " What do you want me to do for you? "
20.33: They answered, " Lord, heal us! Let us be able to see again! "
20.34: Jesus felt sorry for them so he touched their eyes. Immediately the men were able to see again. They followed Jesus.

21.1: When they came near Jerusalem, they went into the town of Bethphage on the Hill of Olives. Then Jesus sent two of his students on ahead.
21.2: He said to them, " Go into the village just ahead of you. You will soon find a donkey tied up. A young donkey will be with her. Untie them and bring them to me.
21.3: And if anyone says anything to you, say, 'The Lord needs them. ' Then he will send them right away. "
21.4: This took place to make what God said through the prophet come true:
21.5: " Tell this to the city of Jerusalem: 'Listen! Your King is coming to you. He is gentle; he is riding on a donkey, even upon a young donkey, born of a work animal. ' "
21.6: The two students went into town. They did exactly as Jesus told them.
21.7: They brought the mother donkey and her young colt. They put their robes on top of the colt. Jesus took his seat upon the robes.
21.8: A very large crowd spread their robes on the road for Jesus. Other people began to cut down branches from trees and to spread them on the road.
21.9: The crowds were shouting. Some people were in front of Jesus and some were behind him. They said, " Hosanna to the son of David! Give praise to this one who is coming with the authority of the Lord God. Hosanna to God! "
21.10: When Jesus came into Jerusalem, the whole city was excited, asking, " Who is this man? "
21.11: The crowds continued to say, " He is Jesus, the prophet from the town of Nazareth in the Galilee. "
21.12: Jesus went into the courtyard of God's temple. He threw out all the people who were selling and buying things there. He turned the money - exchangers' tables upside down. He also turned over the chairs of the people who were selling pigeons.
21.13: Jesus said to them, " It is written, 'My house will be called the place for praying. ' but you have changed it into a hiding place for thieves! "
21.14: Blind people and crippled people came to Jesus in the temple courtyard. He healed them.
21.15: The most important priests and teachers of the law became very angry. They saw the amazing things which Jesus did. They saw children crying out in the temple courtyard, " Hosanna to the son of David! "
21.16: The most important priests and teachers of the law asked Jesus, " Do you hear what they are saying? " Jesus answered them, " Yes! Have you not read this: 'I will make praise complete by using the words of small children and babies. ' "
21.17: Then Jesus left them and went outside of Jerusalem to the town of Bethany where he spent the night.
21.18: Early the next morning, when Jesus was going back into Jerusalem, he was hungry.
21.19: He saw a fig tree next to the road. He went to it but found no fruit on it - only leaves. Then Jesus spoke to the tree, " May no fruit ever come from you! " The fig tree soon dried up.
21.20: When Jesus' students saw this, they were amazed. They asked, " How could the fig tree dry up so quickly? "
21.21: Jesus answered them, " I am telling you the truth: if you have faith and don't doubt, you will be able to perform this too! You can even say to this mountain, 'Pick yourself up and throw yourself into the sea! ' and it will happen.
21.22: If you believe, then you will receive everything you ask for in prayer. "
21.23: Jesus went into the temple courtyard. He was teaching the people. The most important priests and some of the Jewish elders came to him. They asked, " What sort of authority do you have to do these things? Who gave you this authority? "
21.24: Jesus answered them, " I will ask you a question too. If you answer me, I will tell you what sort of authority I have to do these things:
21.25: Where did John's immersion come from? Was it from God or from man? " They began thinking to themselves: " If we say, 'From God', then he will say this to us: 'Why didn't you believe John? '
21.26: But if we say, 'From man', we are afraid of the people - all of them thought of John as a prophet. "
21.27: They answered Jesus, " We don't know. " Jesus said to them, " Then I am not telling you what sort of authority I have to do these things. "
21.28: Jesus said to them " What do you think? A man had two sons. The man came to the first son and said, 'Son, go work in the vineyard today. '
21.29: He answered, 'Yes sir, ' but he did not go. Then the man went to the second son and said the same thing. The son answered, 'I don't want to! ' but later he changed his mind and went. Which of the two sons did what their father wanted? " The Jewish leaders answered, " The second one. " Jesus said to them, " I am telling you the truth: the tax collectors and prostitutes will go into the kingdom of God before you ever do!
21.32: John came to you preaching the way of being made right but you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. You saw this but you did not change your mind later to believe what John was saying. "
21.33: " Listen to another story: there was a man who owned some land. He planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a hole for the wine press, and built a lookout tower. Then he rented the land to some farmers and went away on a trip.
21.34: When harvest time was near, he sent his slaves to the farmers to receive his part of the grapes.
21.35: But the farmers grabbed his slaves. They beat one and killed another. They threw stones at another slave until he died.
21.36: Again the owner sent slaves, more than before, but they did the same thing to those slaves.
21.37: " Finally, the owner sent his son to them, thinking, 'They will respect my son. '
21.38: But when the farmers saw the son, they thought to themselves, 'When the owner dies, his son will own the vineyard. Come, let us kill him and we will get his field! '
21.39: So they took the son, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
21.40: When the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers? "
21.41: The Jewish leaders answered Jesus, " He will kill those evil men! After that he will give the field to some other farmers who will share the fruits with him at harvest time. "
21.42: Jesus said to them, " You have read this in the Scriptures: 'The stone that the builders did not want will become the cornerstone. The Lord God makes this happen. It is a wonderful thing for us to see. '
21.43: This is why I am telling you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will make it produce fruit.
21.44: Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken. If that stone falls on you, it will crush you! "
21.45: When the most important priests and the Pharisees heard these stories, they knew that he was talking about them.
21.46: They wanted to arrest Jesus, but they were afraid of what the crowds might do to them because the people believed that Jesus was a prophet.

22.1: Again Jesus used an example to answer them:
22.2: " The kingdom of heaven is like a king who gave a wedding party for his son.
22.3: The king sent his slaves to invite the guests to the wedding party, but the guests didn't want to come.
22.4: Again, the king sent more slaves saying, 'Tell the guests, " Look, I have prepared the dinner - the steers and fattened calves have been killed - everything is ready! " '
22.5: However, the guests didn't care. They left. One went to his field. One went to his business.
22.6: The others grabbed the king's slaves, insulted them, and killed them.
22.7: The king was very angry. He sent his army to destroy those murderers and to burn their city.
22.8: Then the king said to his slaves, 'The wedding party is still ready, but the guests were not worthy enough to come.
22.9: So go to the street corners and invite whomever you can find to the wedding party. '
22.10: Those slaves went out to the streets and gathered up everyone they could find, good people and bad people. Then the wedding hall was filled with guests.
22.11: The king entered and looked at the guests. He saw a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes.
22.12: The king said to him, 'Friend, how did you get in here without being dressed for the wedding? ' The man had nothing to say.
22.13: Then the king said to the slaves, 'Tie his hands and feet and throw him outside in the dark. In that place there will be screaming and grinding of teeth. '
22.14: Many people are invited, but few people are chosen. "
22.15: Then the Pharisees came. They had made a plan to trap Jesus with a question.
22.16: The Pharisees sent some of their students and the students of Herod Antipas to him. They said, " Teacher, we know that you are true and you teach God's true way. It does not matter to you what people think. You don't pay attention to how important someone is.
22.17: So tell us, what do you think? Is it right that we should pay taxes to Caesar? Yes or no? "
22.18: But Jesus knew their evil plan. He said, " You hypocrites! Why are you trying to trap me?
22.19: Show me the coin for the tax. " They brought a silver coin.
22.20: Jesus said to them, " Whose name and picture is on it? "
22.21: They answered, " Caesar's ". Jesus said to them, " Then give to Caesar the things which are Caesar's and give to God the things which belong to God. "
22.22: When they heard this, they were amazed. They left him and went away.
22.23: That same day some Sadducees came to Jesus. ( Sadducees believed that no one will rise from death. ) They asked Jesus,
22.24: " Teacher, Moses said that if someone has no children and he dies, his brother must marry the widow. Then they will have children for the dead brother.
22.25: There were seven brothers among us. The first one got married, but died. He left his wife with no children.
22.26: In the same way the second brother, the third brother - all seven brothers - died without having children.
22.27: Last of all, the woman died.
22.28: All seven men had married her. So when this woman rises from death, whose wife will she be? "
22.29: Jesus answered them, " You are wrong. You don't know the Scriptures or God's power.
22.30: When people rise from death, they don't marry one another. Instead, they are like angels in heaven.
22.31: Do people rise from death? I know you have read what God said to Moses:
22.32: 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. ' God is not a God of dead people; He is the God of people who are alive! "
22.33: When the crowds heard this, they were very surprised at his teaching.
22.34: When the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
22.35: One of them, an expert on the law of Moses, tried to trap Jesus. He asked,
22.36: " Teacher, what is the most important command in the law? "
22.37: Jesus answered him, " 'You must give yourself to the Lord your God, for His good, expecting nothing in return, with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. '
22.38: This is the most important command.
22.39: The second most important command is like it: 'You must give yourself to your neighbor, for his good, expecting nothing in return, the same way you give to yourself. '
22.40: These two commands are the foundation of the whole law and the prophets. "
22.41: When some Pharisees gathered, Jesus asked them,
22.42: " What do you think about the Messiah? Whose son is he? " They answered Jesus, " David's son. "
22.43: Jesus asked them, " Then why did the Spirit ( through David ) call the Messiah 'Lord'? David wrote:
22.44: 'The Lord God said to my Lord: Sit at My right side until I put your enemies under your feet. '
22.45: Since David called him 'Lord', how could Messiah be David's son? "
22.46: No one was able to answer Jesus. From that time on, no one dared to ask him any more trick questions.

23.1: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his students.
23.2: He said, " The teachers of the law and the Pharisees sit on Moses' seat of authority.
23.3: Therefore, do everything they tell you. Obey them. But don't act as they do because they say one thing and do another.
23.4: They bind heavy loads and put them on people's shoulders, but they don't want to lift a finger to help move them.
23.5: Everything they do, they do so that people will notice them. They show off their phylacteries and they make their tassels long.
23.6: They like to have the best seats at the dinners and the most important seats in the houses of worship.
23.7: They like the greetings of respect which people give them in the marketplaces. They like people to call them, 'Master'.
23.8: You should not be called 'Master' because there is only one teacher for you. You are all brothers.
23.9: On earth you should not be called 'Father' because you have only one Father - the heavenly Father.
23.10: You should not be called 'Leader' because the Messiah is your only Leader.
23.11: The most important one among you will be your slave.
23.12: Every person who acts as though he is important will be made ashamed, but every person who truly humbles himself will be made important.
23.13: " It will be horrible for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees. You hypocrites! You shut the door to the kingdom of heaven in people's faces! You will not go in and you stop those who are trying to get in.
23.14: It will be horrible for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees. You are hypocrites, because you rob widows' houses while you make long prayers for a show. You will receive greater condemnation.
23.15: It will be horrible for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees. You hypocrites! You travel all over the world to make one convert. And when you convert him, you make him twice as much a child of hell as you are!
23.16: " It will be horrible for you, you blind guides who say, 'It is not important if someone makes a vow to God by the temple sanctuary. But if someone makes a vow to God by the gold in the temple sanctuary, he is guilty! '
23.17: You are foolish and blind! What is more important? The gold or the temple sanctuary which makes the gold holy?
23.18: You also say, 'If someone vows to God by the altar, it does not matter. But if someone vows to God by the gift on the altar, he is guilty! '
23.19: You blind men! Which is more important? The gift or the altar which makes the gift holy?
23.20: The person who vows to God by the altar vows to God by the altar and everything on the altar.
23.21: The person who vows to God by the temple sanctuary vows by the sanctuary and by the One who dwells there.
23.22: The person who vows to God by heaven vows to God by God's throne and the One who sits upon it.
23.23: " It will be horrible for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees. You hypocrites! It is true that you give God ten percent of everything you have. You even give Him ten percent of your spices - mint, dill, and cumin. But you forget about more important things in the law: being fair to other people, giving mercy, and faith. You should always tithe, but you must remember to do the more important things too.
23.24: You blind guides! You strain out the gnat, but you swallow the camel!
23.25: " It will be horrible for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees. You hypocrites! You wash the outside of the cup or the bowl. But inside, there are the things you got by cheating other people and pleasing yourselves.
23.26: Blind Pharisees! Make the inside of the cup clean first, so that the outside of it will be clean too.
23.27: " It will be horrible for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees. You hypocrites! You are like tombs which have been painted white. They seem to be very beautiful outside, but inside they are full of all kinds of filth and the bones of dead people.
23.28: You are the same way. Outside you seem good to people, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and sin.
23.29: " It will be horrible for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees. You hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets. You make the graves of good people beautiful.
23.30: You claim, 'If we had lived in the time of our ancestors, we would not have helped them kill the prophets. '
23.31: So you are admitting you are the sons of the men who murdered the prophets!
23.32: You are finishing what your ancestors started.
23.33: You snakes! You are from a family of poisonous snakes! How will you escape the judgment of hell?
23.34: Look! I am sending you prophets, wise men, and teachers of the law. You will kill some of them and you will nail others to crosses. You will whip some of them in your houses of worship. You will chase them from town to town.
23.35: You will have to answer for the death of every good person who has been killed on earth. You will have to answer for all the spilled blood from the murder of Abel to the murder of Zechariah, the son of Barachiah. You murdered Zechariah between the temple sanctuary and the altar.
23.36: " I am telling you the truth: all these things will happen to the people of this generation!
23.37: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets. God sent you His men, but you stoned them to death. I have often wanted to gather up your people, as a hen gathers up her baby chicks under her wings, but you refused.
23.38: Listen! Your house is completely abandoned.
23.39: I tell you, you will never see me again until you say, 'Praise to the one who is coming with the authority of the Lord God. ' "

24.1: Jesus left the temple courtyard. While he was walking away, his students came to him to show him the beautiful things of the temple area.
24.2: Jesus said to them, " Do you see all these things? I am telling you the truth: everything you see here will be destroyed. No stone will stay on top of another. Everything will be completely destroyed! "
24.3: While Jesus was sitting on Olive Hillside, his students came to him alone. They asked, " Tell us, when will these things happen? How will we know when it is the time for you to return? When will the end of the age be? "
24.4: Jesus answered them, " Be careful! Don't let anyone fool you.
24.5: Many people will come to you using my name. They will say, 'I am the Messiah! ' And they will fool many people.
24.6: You will hear about wars and wars that are about to begin. Be sure that you don't get upset. These things must happen, but the end will come later.
24.7: One country will fight against another country. Kingdoms will fight against other kingdoms. There will not be enough food to eat. Everywhere there will be earthquakes,
24.8: but all these things are only the beginning of the pain.
24.9: Then they will hand you over to some men for torturing. They will kill you. All people will hate you because of my name.
24.10: Then many people will feel discouraged; they will turn against one another. They will hate each other.
24.11: Many false prophets will appear. They will fool many people.
24.12: Because the influence of sin will be so strong, the giving of self to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return of many people, will grow cold.
24.13: But the person who endures until the end will be saved.
24.14: This Good News about the kingdom will be preached in the whole world so that all nations may hear the truth. And then the end will come.
24.15: " When you see what God talked about through Daniel the prophet - 'The Abomination of Desolation' - standing in the holy place ( let the reader note the meaning ),
24.16: then those people who are in Judea must run away to the mountains.
24.17: The person who is on top of his house must not come down to carry things in the house away with him.
24.18: The person who is in the field must not turn back to get his robe.
24.19: At that time it will be horrible for pregnant women and nursing mothers.
24.20: Pray that the time when you escape will not be during winter or on a Sabbath day.
24.21: There will be great suffering. Never has there been such suffering since the beginning of the world until the present time and there will never be such suffering in the future.
24.22: If that period of time were to last any longer, then no one would be left alive. But those times will be cut short because of the people chosen by God.
24.23: " At that time if someone says to you, 'Look, here is the Messiah! ' or, 'There he is! ' don't believe him.
24.24: False messiahs and false prophets will appear. They will perform such great proofs and miracles to fool people - even God's chosen people, if that were possible.
24.25: Listen! I am telling you ahead of time.
24.26: If they say this to you, 'Look, he is in the desert! ' don't go out there! or, 'He is in secret rooms! ' don't believe them!
24.27: " I will return. On the day when I come, I will shine, as lightning flashes across the sky, from the east to the west.
24.28: People can always know where a dead body is - they can see the vultures gathering.
24.29: Soon after the trouble of those times, 'The sun will become dark. The light of the moon will not be seen The stars will fall from the sky. The powers in the universe will be moved. '
24.30: Then my sign will appear in the sky - all men on earth will see me coming on the clouds with power and great glory; they will mourn.
24.31: I will use a loud trumpet to send out my angels. From all directions the angels will gather together my chosen people.
24.32: " Learn from the story about the fig tree: when its branches start to become soft and green, and new leaves begin to grow, you know that summer is near.
24.33: In the same way, when you see all these things happening, you will know that the time is very, very near.
24.34: I am telling you the truth: all these things will happen in this generation.
24.35: The world will be destroyed, but my words will never be destroyed!
24.36: No one knows when that exact time will be. The angels of heaven do not know it. The Son doesn't know it. Only the heavenly Father knows.
24.37: " When I come, it will be just as it was in Noah's time.
24.38: People were eating, drinking, getting married, giving their daughters away in marriage - even on the day when Noah entered the ark.
24.39: The people did not know the truth until the flood came and swept them all away. That is how it will be when I come.
24.40: At that time there will be two men in the field; one will be taken and one will be left.
24.41: Two women will be grinding grain; one will be taken and the other will be left.
24.42: So watch! You don't know on what day your Lord is coming.
24.43: Know this: if a homeowner knew what time of night a robber was coming, he would watch for the robber and not let him break into his house.
24.44: This is why you must be ready. I will come at a time when you are not expecting me.
24.45: " Who is the wise and trusted slave? Who is the slave whom the master can choose to take care of the master's family and the other slaves by giving them food at the right time?
24.46: When the master comes and finds that slave doing the work he gave him, that slave will be very happy.
24.47: I am telling you the truth: the master will choose that slave to take care of everything which the master owns.
24.48: However, if that slave thinks his master will not come back soon,
24.49: then he may begin to beat the other slaves. That slave may also eat all the food and get drunk with other men.
24.50: Then the master of that slave will come when that slave is not ready, at a time when that slave is not expecting him.
24.51: Then the master will punish that slave and send him away. This is what the master does to all the slaves he cannot trust. In that place there will be screaming and grinding of teeth. "

25.1: Jesus said, " At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins. They took their lamps and went out to meet the groom.
25.2: Five of them were foolish and five were wise.
25.3: The foolish ones took their lamps, but they did not take extra oil with them.
25.4: The wise virgins took extra oil in their jars with their lamps.
25.5: The groom was late. All of the virgins became sleepy. They fell asleep.
25.6: About midnight there was a shout: 'Look, the groom! Go out and meet him! '
25.7: Then all ten virgins got up and prepared their lamps.
25.8: But the foolish virgins said to the wise virgins, 'Give us some of your oil because our lamps have almost gone out. '
25.9: The wise virgins answered, 'No! There would not be enough for all of us. Instead, go to the store and buy some more oil. '
25.10: While these virgins were gone to buy some more oil, the groom came. The wise virgins, who were ready, went inside with him to the wedding party. And the door was shut.
25.11: Later, the other virgins came and said, 'Master, master, open the door for us! '
25.12: But the Master answered, 'I am telling you the truth: I don't know you. '
25.13: So watch! You don't know the day or the exact hour when I will come. "
25.14: " The kingdom of heaven will be like a man leaving on a trip. He called his slaves and turned his property over to them.
25.15: He gave five talents to one, two talents to one, and one talent to another. Each man received what he was able to manage. Then the man went on the trip.
25.16: The man with five talents went out immediately and earned five more talents.
25.17: In the same way the man with two talents earned two more talents.
25.18: But the man with one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and buried his master's money.
25.19: After a long time, the master of those slaves came back. He made them give an account.
25.20: The man who had received five talents came and brought five more talents, saying, 'Master, you turned five talents over to me but, look, I earned five more talents! '
25.21: His master said to him, 'Fine! You are a good and faithful slave. I see that I can trust you with small things. Therefore I will put you in charge of important things. Come and share your master's happiness. '
25.22: The man with two talents came and said, 'Master, you turned two talents over to me but, look, I have earned two more talents! '
25.23: His master said to him, 'Fine! You are a good and faithful slave. I see that I can trust you with small things. Therefore I will put you in charge of important things. Come and share your master's happiness. '
25.24: Then the man who had received one talent came. He said, 'Master, I knew you were a hard man. You take money which you didn't earn and you gather food which you didn't grow.
25.25: So I was afraid. I went off and hid your talent in the ground. Look, here is your talent. '
25.26: His master answered, 'You evil, lazy slave! You knew that I take money which I didn't earn and gather food which I didn't grow.
25.27: Therefore you should have put my money in the bank. Then when I returned, I could have my money, with interest too.
25.28: Take the talent away from him and give it to the man who has ten talents.
25.29: The person who uses what he has will get more, but the person who doesn't use what he has will have everything taken away from him.
25.30: Throw this useless slave outside into the dark. In that place there will be screaming and grinding of teeth. '
25.31: " When I come with my glory and all my angels, then I will sit on my glorious throne.
25.32: All the people in the world will be gathered in front of me. I will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
25.33: I will put the sheep on the right side and the goats on the left side.
25.34: Then I will say to the people on the right side, 'You are blessed by my Father. Come, take what belongs to you - the kingdom which was prepared for you since the beginning of the world.
25.35: I was hungry and you gave me something to eat. I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink. I was a stranger and you took me into your home.
25.36: I had no clothes, so you gave me some clothes. I was sick and you took care of me. I was in jail and you came to visit me. '
25.37: Then the people made right will answer him, 'Lord, when did we see you? When did we feed you when you were hungry? When did we give you something to drink when you were thirsty?
25.38: When did we see you as a stranger and take you into our homes? When did you need clothes and we gave you some clothes?
25.39: When were you sick or in jail? When did we come to you? '
25.40: I will answer them, 'I am telling you the truth: since you treated some of my so - called " unimportant " brothers this way, you did it to me! '
25.41: " Then I will say to the people on the left side, 'Go away from me into eternal fire. You are condemned! The fire has been prepared for the devil and his angels.
25.42: I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat. I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink.
25.43: I was a stranger and you didn't take me into your homes. I had no clothes and you didn't give me any. I was sick; I was in jail, but you didn't take care of me. '
25.44: Then they will answer, 'Lord, when did we see you? When were you hungry, thirsty, a stranger, without clothes, sick, or in jail and we didn't help you? '
25.45: Then I will answer them, 'I am telling you the truth: since you didn't treat one of these so - called " unimportant " people with kindness, you didn't do it to me, either. '
25.46: Then these people will go off into eternal punishment, but the people made right will go into eternal life. "

26.1: When Jesus finished saying all these things, he said this to his students,
26.2: " You know that the day after tomorrow is the beginning of the Passover. I will be handed over to be nailed to a cross. "
26.3: Then the most important priests and the Jewish elders of the people gathered together at the high priest's house. His name was Caiaphas.
26.4: They planned to use a trick to arrest Jesus and kill him,
26.5: but they said, " Let us not do it during the Festival, so that there will be no trouble among the people. "
26.6: Jesus was in the town of Bethany in Simon's house. ( Simon had been a leper. )
26.7: A woman came to Jesus. She had an alabaster jar of some very expensive perfume. While Jesus was at the table, she poured it on his head.
26.8: When Jesus' students saw this, they became very angry. They asked, " Why waste this?
26.9: This could have been sold for a lot of money and given to poor people! "
26.10: Knowing what they were saying, Jesus said to them, " Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a good thing to me.
26.11: You will always have poor people with you, but you will not always have me!
26.12: When she put this perfume on my body, she did it for when I will be buried.
26.13: I am telling you the truth: the Good News will be preached in the whole world. Wherever they tell it, what she did will be mentioned to remember her. "
26.14: Then one of the twelve delegates, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the most important priests.
26.15: He said, " If I were to hand Jesus over to you, what would you pay me? " They agreed with him on the price - 30 silver coins.
26.16: From that time on, Judas was looking for the best time to give Jesus to them.
26.17: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, Jesus' students came to him. They asked, " Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal? "
26.18: Jesus answered, " Go into the city to the host. Tell him, 'The Teacher says, " My time is near. My students and I will have the Passover meal with you. " '
26.19: Jesus' students did exactly as Jesus told them. They prepared the Passover meal.
26.20: When evening came, Jesus sat down at the table with his twelve students.
26.21: While they were eating, Jesus said, " I am telling you the truth: one of you will turn against me! "
26.22: They began to feel very sad. Each one of them said to Jesus, " Lord, I am not the one, am I? "
26.23: Jesus answered, " The person who has dipped his hand in the same dinner bowl with me will turn against me.
26.24: I will die just as it is written about me. But how horrible it will be for that man who turns against me. It would be better if that man had never been born! "
26.25: Judas ( the one who turned against him ) answered, " Master, I am not the one, am I? " Jesus answered Judas, " Yes, you are. "
26.26: While they were eating, Jesus took bread and gave thanks. He broke off some of the bread and gave it to his students. He said, " Take it and eat it. This bread is my body. "
26.27: Then he took a cup. He gave thanks to God for it and gave it to them. He said, " All of you, drink from it.
26.28: This is my blood which I am pouring out for many people for the forgiveness of sins. It shows the new covenant which God has set up with men.
26.29: I tell you, from now on I will never drink this fruit of the vine again until the day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom. "
26.30: Then they sang a song of praise and went out to the Hill of Olives.
26.31: Then Jesus said to them, " Tonight all of you will be ashamed of me. This is written: 'I will strike the shepherd and the flock of sheep will be scattered. '
26.32: However, after I rise from death, I will go ahead of you to the Galilee. "
26.33: Peter answered him, " Everyone else may be ashamed of you, but I will never be ashamed of you! "
26.34: Jesus said to Peter, " I tell you the truth: before the rooster crows in the morning, you will say you don't even know me three different times! "
26.35: Peter answered him, " Even if I must die with you, I will always be loyal to you. " All of Jesus' students said the same thing.
26.36: Then Jesus and his students went to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to them, " Sit here while I go over there and pray. "
26.37: He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him. He began to feel sad and depressed.
26.38: Then he said to them, " My soul is full of sorrow; I am going to die. Stay here and be watchful with me. "
26.39: Then Jesus went forward a short distance and bowed down to pray. He said, " My Father, if it is possible, take this cup of suffering away from me - but what You want is more important than what I want. "
26.40: Then Jesus came to his students. He found them sleeping. He asked Peter, " Were you not strong enough to stay awake with me for just one hour?
26.41: Watch and pray for strength against temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak. "
26.42: Jesus went away the second time. He prayed, " My Father, if this must happen and I must drink the cup of suffering, if this is what You want, let it be. "
26.43: Again Jesus came and found them sleeping. Their eyes were very tired.
26.44: He left them again. The third time he prayed the same prayer.
26.45: Then Jesus came to his students and asked them, " Are you still sleeping and resting? Listen, the time has come - I am now being handed over into the hands of sinful men.
26.46: Get up, we must go. Look! The one who turned against me is near! "
26.47: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve delegates, came. There was a large crowd with him. They had come from the most important priests and the elders of the Jewish people. They had sticks and swords.
26.48: Judas had given them the signal to arrest the one he would give the kiss of friendship.
26.49: Judas went immediately to Jesus and said, " Greetings, Master! " Then Judas gave him the kiss of friendship.
26.50: But Jesus said to him, " Friend, do what you came for! " Then the men who came with Judas reached out and took hold of Jesus.
26.51: Suddenly one of the men with Jesus reached for his sword and pulled it out. He struck the high priest's slave, cutting off his ear.
26.52: Then Jesus said, " Put your sword back in its place! Everyone who uses violence will be violently destroyed.
26.53: Don't you think I could call on my Father for help? He would bring more than twelve legions of angels here!
26.54: But how could the Scriptures come true if this did not happen? "
26.55: At that moment Jesus said this to the crowd: " Why did you come out here to get me with swords and sticks? Do you think I am a criminal? I was sitting in the temple courtyard every day teaching. You did not arrest me there.
26.56: All this happened to make the writings of the prophets come true. " Then all of Jesus' students left him. They ran away.
26.57: After they arrested Jesus, they brought him to Caiaphas, the high priest. The teachers of the law and the Jewish elders were gathered there.
26.58: Peter was following Jesus but he did not come near Jesus. He came as far as the high priest's courtyard. Later he went inside. He was sitting with the guards. He wanted to see what would happen.
26.59: The most important priests and the whole Jewish Council were trying to find some men who would give false evidence against Jesus so that they could put him to death.
26.60: But they did not find many people to come forward to tell lies. Finally, two men came forward.
26.61: They claimed, " This man said, 'I am able to destroy God's temple sanctuary and build it again in three days! ' "
26.62: The high priest stood up and asked Jesus, " Will you give no answer to what they say against you - is it true? "
26.63: Jesus continued to be silent. The high priest said to him, " By the living God, I hereby force you: you must answer! Tell us if you are the Messiah, the Son of God! "
26.64: Jesus said to him, " Yes, I am. " Nevertheless, I tell you, from now on, you will see me: sitting at the right side of God. I will be coming on the clouds of the sky. "
26.65: Then the high priest ripped his clothes and he cried out, " He has said an evil thing! Why do we need any more witnesses? Listen, you have just heard him say this evil thing!
26.66: What do you think? " They answered, " He is guilty! He must die! "
26.67: Then they spit in Jesus' face. They hit him with their fists. Some of them slapped him.
26.68: They said, " Prophesy for us, you Messiah! Let God tell you which one of us hit you! "
26.69: Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came to him. She said, " You too were with Jesus, the one from the Galilee! "
26.70: But in front of everyone Peter said that this was not true. He said, " I don't know what you're talking about! "
26.71: Later, Peter went out to the gate. Another girl saw him. She said to the men there, " This man was with Jesus from Nazareth! "
26.72: Again Peter denied it. This time he said, " I swear, I don't know the man! "
26.73: After a little while, the men who were standing there came to Peter and said, " Surely you are one of Jesus' community! It is clear that you have a Galilean accent! "
26.74: Peter began to curse and swear, " I don't know the man! " Immediately the rooster crowed.
26.75: Then Peter remembered that Jesus had said, " Before the rooster crows, you will say, three different times, that you don't even know me. " Peter went outside and cried bitterly.

27.1: It was early in the morning. The most important priests and the Jewish elders of the people made the decision to put Jesus to death.
27.2: They tied him up. Then they brought him and handed him over to Pilate, the Governor.
27.3: Judas, the one who turned against Jesus, saw that Jesus had been condemned. Judas changed his mind and brought back the 30 silver coins to the most important priests and the Jewish elders.
27.4: He said, " I have done wrong! I handed over an innocent man to die! " They answered, " We don't care! That's your problem! "
27.5: Then Judas threw the silver coins toward the temple sanctuary and left. He went off and killed himself by hanging.
27.6: The priests picked up the coins and said, " Since this is blood money, it would not be right to put this into the treasury. "
27.7: So they decided to use it to buy a potter's field for burying strangers.
27.8: Today that field is called Field of Blood.
27.9: Then what God had said through Jeremiah the prophet came true: " They took 30 silver coins. This was the value that the sons of Israel put on him.
27.10: They used the money to buy the potter's field, as the Lord God ordered me. "
27.11: Jesus stood before the governor. The governor asked him, " Are you the King of the Jews? " Jesus answered, " Yes. "
27.12: The most important priests and the Jewish elders accused Jesus, but Jesus gave no answer.
27.13: Then Pilate said to him, " Don't you hear how many charges they are bringing against you? "
27.14: But Jesus didn't even say a word. The governor was very surprised.
27.15: Every year at the Passover Feast, the governor always set one prisoner free, whomever the people wanted.
27.16: This time they had a well - known prisoner named Jesus Barabbas.
27.17: Therefore, when the people gathered, Pilate said to them, " Who do you want me to set free? Jesus Barabbas or the Jesus who is called Messiah? "
27.18: ( Pilate knew that they had handed Jesus over to him because of jealousy. )
27.19: While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent a message to him. It said, " Have nothing to do with this innocent man! Last night in a dream I suffered many things because of him! "
27.20: The most important priests and the Jewish elders persuaded the crowds to ask Pilate for Barabbas. They wanted to destroy Jesus.
27.21: The governor asked them, " Which of the two men do you want me to set free? " They answered, " Barabbas! "
27.22: Pilate asked them, " What should I do with Jesus, the one who is called Messiah? " They all answered, " Nail him to a cross! "
27.23: But Pilate asked, " Why? What crime has Jesus done? " But they continued yelling even more, " Nail him to a cross! "
27.24: Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere - only more trouble. He took some water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. He said, " I am not responsible for this man's death - you are! "
27.25: The whole crowd answered, " We accept that responsibility for us and for our children! "
27.26: Then he set Barabbas free for them. After beating Jesus with whips, Pilate handed him over to be nailed to the cross.
27.27: The governor's soldiers took Jesus to the Roman fortress. The whole group gathered around Jesus.
27.28: They took off his clothes and dressed him with a long red robe.
27.29: They used thorny branches to make a crown. Then they put it on his head. They put a stick in his right hand. They kneeled down before him and made fun of him, saying, " Hail, King of the Jews! "
27.30: They spit on him. They took the stick and began to hit him on the head.
27.31: When they finished making fun of him, they took off the long robe and dressed him with his own clothes. Then they led him away to nail him to the cross.
27.32: As they were going out of Jerusalem, they found a man from the city of Cyrene. His name was Simon. They forced him to carry Jesus' cross.
27.33: They came to a place called Golgatha. ( This means 'The Place of the Skull'. )
27.34: They gave Jesus some wine. ( A drug for pain was mixed with it. ) When he had tasted it, he refused to drink it.
27.35: Then they nailed him to the cross. The soldiers gambled to see who would get Jesus' clothes.
27.37: At the top of the stake they wrote the reason for his punishment in these words: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
27.38: Along with Jesus, two criminals were nailed to crosses. One was on his right side; the other was on his left.
27.39: The people who were passing by shook their heads and said terrible things to Jesus.
27.40: They said, " You are the one who was going to destroy the temple sanctuary and build it again in three days! Since you are the Son of God, save yourself! Come down from the cross! "
27.41: In the same way the most important priests, the teachers of the law, and the Jewish elders made fun of Jesus. They continued to say,
27.42: " He saved other people but he cannot save himself! He is the King of Israel; let him come down from the cross now! Then we will believe in him!
27.43: He trusts in God; let God rescue him now if He wants him. Jesus did say, 'I am the Son of God. ' "
27.44: Even the criminals who were nailed to the other crosses did the same thing - they kept insulting Jesus.
27.45: There was darkness over the whole land from noon until three o'clock in the afternoon.
27.46: At about three o'clock, Jesus shouted this loudly: " Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? " ( This means: " My God, my God, why did you abandon me? " )
27.47: Some of the men standing there heard this. They said, " This man is calling for Elijah. "
27.48: One of them quickly ran and got a sponge. He soaked it in some sour wine. Then he put it on the end of a long stick and gave Jesus a drink.
27.49: The other men said, " Leave him alone. Let's see if Elijah will come and save him! "
27.50: Again Jesus cried out very loudly. Then he died.
27.51: The curtain in the temple sanctuary was split into two parts - from the top to the bottom. The earth shook. Large rocks broke apart.
27.52: ( Tombs were opened. After Jesus rose from the grave, many saints who had died were raised from death too. They left their tombs and went into Jerusalem and appeared to many people. )
27.54: There was a Roman army officer and some of his men guarding Jesus. When they saw the earthquake and the other things that happened, they were very frightened. They said, " This man really was God's Son. "
27.55: There were many women there. They had helped Jesus and followed him from the Galilee. They were far away, watching.
27.56: Some of them were: Mary ( from the town of Magdal ), Mary ( the mother of Jacob and Joseph ), the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
27.57: Since it was getting late, a rich man named Joseph from the town of Aramathea ( He was also a student of Jesus. )
27.58: came to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate gave an order to give the body to him.
27.59: So Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean sheet.
27.60: Then he put Jesus' body into his own new tomb which he had cut out of solid rock. He rolled a large stone to cover the door of the tomb. Then Joseph left.
27.61: Mary ( the one from Magdal ) and the other Mary were there. They were sitting in front of the grave.
27.62: That day was called Preparation Day. The next day the most important priests and the Pharisees had a meeting with Pilate.
27.63: They said, " Sir, we remember what that liar said while he was still alive: 'After three days I will rise from death. '
27.64: So give an order to make the grave secure until the third day. Otherwise, his students might come, steal him, and tell the people: 'Jesus came back to life! ' Then this last lie will be even worse than the first lie. "
27.65: Pilate said to them, " You have a guard. Go and make it as secure as you know how. "
27.66: So they went and sealed the grave. They put a seal on the stone and they stationed a guard.

28.1: After the Sabbath day, when the first day of the week morning was dawning, Mary ( the one from Magdal ) and the other Mary were on their way to look at the grave.
28.2: Suddenly there was a great earthquake. An angel of the Lord came down from heaven. He went to the large stone and rolled it away. Then the angel sat on top of it.
28.3: His appearance was shining like lightning. His clothes were as white as snow.
28.4: The men who were guarding the tomb acted as if they were dead men; they trembled with fear.
28.5: The angel said to the women, " Don't be afraid. I know you are looking for Jesus who was nailed to the cross.
28.6: He is not here! He is raised from death, just as he said. Come, look at the place where he lay.
28.7: Go quickly and tell his students: 'Jesus has been raised from death! Listen, he will go ahead of you to the Galilee. You will see him there. Remember, I told you. ' "
28.8: The women left the tomb quickly. They were afraid, yet very happy. They ran to tell Jesus' students.
28.9: Suddenly, Jesus met them. He gave them his greetings! They went to him, held onto his feet, and worshipped him.
28.10: Then Jesus said to them, " Don't be afraid. Go tell my brothers that they must leave for the Galilee. They will see me there. "
28.11: While the women were going, some of the guards went into Jerusalem. They told the most important priests everything which had happened.
28.12: The priests had a meeting with the Jewish elders. They decided to give the soldiers some money to lie.
28.13: They said to the soldiers, " Say this: 'While we were sleeping, the students of Jesus came at night and stole his body. '
28.14: If the governor hears about this, we will make him believe us. We will fix it; don't worry. "
28.15: So the soldiers took the money and did as they were told. This rumor has spread among Jewish people until this very day.
28.16: The eleven students went to a hillside in the Galilee where Jesus had told them to meet him.
28.17: When they saw him, they worshipped him, but some had doubts.
28.18: Jesus came to them and said, " All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
28.19: Therefore when you've gone out, make students for me from all nations. Immerse them by the authority of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
28.20: Teach them to obey everything I commanded you. Remember, I will always be with you - even until the end of time! "

1.1: This is how the Good News about Jesus Christ, God's Son, began:
1.2: It was like what Isaiah, the prophet, wrote: " Listen! I am sending My messenger to go ahead of you. He will prepare the way for you. "
1.3: " There is a voice crying, out in the desert: 'Prepare the Lord's way. Make His paths straight. ' "
1.4: In the desert, John was immersing people. He was preaching this message: " Change your hearts and be immersed for the forgiveness of sins! "
1.5: Everyone in Jerusalem and from the region of Judea was going out to John. They were admitting that they had sinned. Then he was immersing them in the Jordan River.
1.6: John always wore clothes made of camel hair. He had a leather belt around his waist. He ate grasshoppers and wild honey.
1.7: His message was, " There is one coming later who is more important than I am. I'm not worthy to bend down and untie his shoelace.
1.8: I have immersed you with water; he will immerse you in the Holy Spirit. "
1.9: At that time, Jesus came from the town of Nazareth in the Galilee; John immersed him in the Jordan River.
1.10: Suddenly, as Jesus was coming up from the water, he saw the sky separate. The Spirit was like a dove coming down to Jesus.
1.11: A Voice came from heaven, saying, " You are My Son, and I give Myself to you, for your good, expecting nothing in return. I am very pleased with you! "
1.12: At once the Spirit sent Jesus into the desert.
1.13: Satan was tempting Jesus for 40 days in the desert. Jesus was with the wild animals, but the angels were helping him.
1.14: After John was arrested, Jesus went to the Galilee. He was preaching the Good News about the kingdom of God:
1.15: " The time is ripe. The kingdom of God is very near! Change your hearts and believe in the Good News! "
1.16: While Jesus was walking beside Lake Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, his brother. They were fishermen. They were throwing their nets into the lake.
1.17: Jesus said to them, " Follow me and I will make you fishermen — of people. "
1.18: Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
1.19: Jesus went a little farther and saw Jacob and his brother, John. They were in a boat preparing their nets. They were sons of Zebedee.
1.20: Immediately Jesus invited them too. They left their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired workers. And they followed Jesus.
1.21: They went into the town of Capernaum. On the Sabbath day when Jesus went into the house of worship, he began to teach the people right away.
1.22: They were amazed at what he taught. Jesus was teaching them as one with authority — not as the teachers of the law.
1.23: There was a man in their house of worship with an evil spirit. Suddenly, he shouted,
1.24: " Jesus of Nazareth! What do you want with us? Did you come here to destroy us? I know who you are — the Holy One of God! "
1.25: But Jesus stopped the evil spirit. Jesus said, " Stop talking and come out of the man! "
1.26: The evil spirit jerked the man around. He shouted loudly and came out of the man.
1.27: The people were shocked. They started asking one another, " What is this? A new teaching? With authority, Jesus commands evil spirits and they obey him. "
1.28: And so the news about Jesus went out quickly to the whole area in the Galilee.
1.29: After Jesus left the house of worship, he went into Simon and Andrew's house with Jacob and John.
1.30: Simon's mother - in - law was very sick with a fever. They talked to Jesus about her.
1.31: He went to her, took her hand, and raised her up. The fever left her and she began to serve them.
1.32: When it was late, after the sun had gone down, they brought to Jesus all the sick people and people with demons.
1.33: The whole town was gathered at the door.
1.34: Jesus healed the people who had many types of diseases. He also threw out many demons. He would not allow the demons to talk because the demons knew who he was.
1.35: While it was still dark the next morning, Jesus got up and went out to a place where people did not live. There he was praying to God.
1.36: Simon and the men with him searched for Jesus.
1.37: They found him and said to him, " Everyone is looking for you. "
1.38: Jesus said to them, " We must go to other villages near here. I must preach there too. This is why I came. "
1.39: Jesus went everywhere in the Galilee, preaching in their houses of worship and throwing out demons.
1.40: A man with leprosy came to Jesus. He bowed down and begged Jesus saying, " You can heal me if you want to. "
1.41: He felt sorry for him. So he reached out and touched the man. Jesus said to the man, " I do want to heal you — be healed! "
1.42: Immediately the leprosy left him; he was healed.
1.43: Jesus sent him away at once. He gave him a strong warning,
1.44: " Don't tell anyone about what happened, but go show yourself to the priest. Then give a gift to God because you have been healed. This is what the law of Moses commands. This will prove to the priests that you are healed. "
1.45: But the man went out and began to tell all about it. He spread the news so far that Jesus was no longer able to go into a town openly. Instead, Jesus stayed out in places where people did not live. From everywhere the people were coming to him.

2.1: A few days later, Jesus went back to the town of Capernaum. The people heard this: " He's home! "
2.2: So many people gathered that there was no room — not even at the door. Jesus began preaching the word.
2.3: There was a man who was paralyzed. Four men came there carrying him.
2.4: But because of the crowd, they were not able to get to Jesus. So they went up on the roof of the house where Jesus was. They dug a hole through the roof and lowered the paralyzed man through the hole, lying on his bed.
2.5: Jesus saw that these men had faith. He said to the paralyzed man, " My son, your sins are forgiven. "
2.6: Some of the teachers of the law were sitting there. In their hearts they were thinking,
2.7: " How can this man talk like this? He is saying an evil thing. Only God can forgive sin! "
2.8: Immediately Jesus knew in his spirit that they were thinking like this to themselves. Jesus said to them, " Why are you thinking these things in your heart?
2.9: Which is easier to say, 'Your sins are forgiven, ' or to say, 'Stand up, pick up your bed and walk? '
2.10: I will prove to you that I have the right to forgive sins on earth. " So Jesus said to the paralyzed man,
2.11: " I tell you, get up! Take your bed and go home! "
2.12: Immediately the man stood up, picked up his bed, and left in front of all of them. All the people were completely amazed. They began to praise God. They said, " We have never seen such things! "
2.13: Jesus went back again to Lake Galilee. All the people were coming to him and he was teaching them.
2.14: As Jesus was walking along, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office. Jesus said to him, " Follow me. " Then Levi got up and followed him.
2.15: While Jesus was having dinner at Levi's house, many tax collectors and sinful people joined Jesus and his students for dinner. Many of them were beginning to follow Jesus too.
2.16: Some of the Pharisees' teachers of the law saw that Jesus was eating with sinful people and tax collectors. These teachers continued to ask Jesus' students, " Why does Jesus eat with tax collectors and sinful people? "
2.17: When Jesus heard about this, he said to them, " Healthy people don't need the doctor, but sick people do. I didn't come to invite 'good' people — but sinners to change their hearts! "
2.18: The students of John and the Pharisees were fasting. Some people came and said to Jesus, " Why do John's students and the students of the Pharisees fast, but your students do not fast? "
2.19: Jesus said to them, " Would it be right for the friends of the groom to fast while the groom is still with them? As long as they have the groom with them, they cannot fast.
2.20: But the time will come when the groom will be taken away from them. Then his friends will fast.
2.21: " No one sews a piece of cloth, which has never been washed, onto an old robe. If he does, it will shrink and tear away from the robe. Then the hole will become worse.
2.22: No one puts new wine into old wine skins. If they do, the old wine skins will break open. The wine will spill out and the wine skins will be ruined. Instead, people put new wine into new wine skins. "
2.23: Once on a Sabbath day, Jesus was traveling through a field of grain. His students began picking some of the grain to eat.
2.24: The Pharisees said to Jesus, " Look! Why are they doing what is not right on the Sabbath? "
2.25: Jesus said to them, " Do you remember reading about what David did when he needed something? He and his men were hungry.
2.26: During the time when Abiathar was high priest, David went into the house of God. He took the holy loaves of bread and ate them. The law of Moses says only priests could eat them, but David gave some to his men. "
2.27: Jesus was saying this to the Pharisees, " The Sabbath was made for man. Man was not made for the Sabbath!
2.28: I am Lord even of the Sabbath day. "

3.1: Again Jesus went into the house of worship. A man with a crippled hand was there.
3.2: Some Jewish leaders were waiting to see if Jesus would heal the man on the Sabbath day. They wanted to see Jesus do something wrong so that they could accuse him.
3.3: Jesus said to the man with the crippled hand, " Stand in the middle. "
3.4: Then Jesus said to the Jewish leaders, " I ask you, which is right on the Sabbath day — to do good or to do evil? Is it right to save a life or to destroy one? " But they wouldn't answer.
3.5: Jesus looked around at all of them. He was angry, but he was sad too because their hearts were hard. He said to the man, " Stretch out your hand! " The man stretched it out. His hand was restored.
3.6: The Pharisees and the students of Herod Antipas left. They began to make a plot to kill Jesus.
3.7: Jesus and his students went down to Lake Galilee. A large group followed him from the Galilee and from the region of Judea,
3.8: from Jerusalem, from the land of Idumea, from the area across the Jordan River, and from the cities of Tyre and Sidon. They heard about the things Jesus was doing; so they came to him.
3.9: To keep the crowd from pushing up against Jesus, he told his students to get a boat ready for him.
3.10: The people were trying to get as close to Jesus as they could because he had healed many people. People with diseases wanted to touch him.
3.11: When people with evil spirits saw Jesus, they fell down in front of him and shouted, " You are the son of God! "
3.12: But Jesus warned them not to tell who he was.
3.13: Jesus went up on a hillside. He called for the ones he wanted. They came to him.
3.14: He appointed twelve and named them " delegates ". He wanted them to be with him and to send them out to preach.
3.15: They would have authority to throw out demons.
3.16: These are the twelve men whom Jesus chose: Simon ( Jesus called him Peter );
3.17: Jacob, the son of Zebedee; John, Jacob's brother ( Jesus gave them the name Boanerges — this means " sons of thunder " ),
3.18: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, Jacob ( the son of Alphaeus ), Thaddaeus, Simon the Revolutionary,
3.19: and Judas Iscariot ( the one who turned against Jesus ).
3.20: Jesus came to a house. Again, such a crowd came together that they didn't even have time to eat.
3.21: When Jesus' family heard this, they went out to get Jesus. They were saying, " He's crazy! "
3.22: The teachers of the law who came down from Jerusalem were saying, " Jesus has Beelzebub. Jesus uses the prince of demons to throw out demons! "
3.23: Jesus called them and began to speak to them with stories: " How could Satan throw out Satan?
3.24: If a kingdom is divided and fights against itself, that kingdom will not be able to stand.
3.25: If a family is divided and fights against itself, that family will not be able to stand.
3.26: And if Satan is fighting against himself then he is divided. How can he last? He has lost.
3.27: " No one can go into a strong man's house to rob him, unless he ties up the strong man first. Then he will rob his house.
3.28: " I am telling you the truth: every sin and terrible thing which people say may be forgiven.
3.29: But the person who says evil things against the Holy Spirit will never receive forgiveness — not ever. Instead, he is guilty of eternal sin! "
3.30: Jesus said this because they were saying, " Jesus has an evil spirit! "
3.31: Jesus' mother and his brothers came. They were standing outside. They sent someone inside to Jesus to call him.
3.32: A crowd was sitting around Jesus. They said to him, " Listen, your mother and your brothers are outside; they want to talk to you. "
3.33: Jesus answered them, " Who is my mother? Who are my brothers? "
3.34: Jesus looked around at the people who were surrounding him. He said, " Look, my mother and my brothers!
3.35: The person who does what God wants is my brother, my sister, and my mother. "

4.1: Again Jesus began to teach beside Lake Galilee. A very large crowd gathered around him. So Jesus got into a boat on the lake and sat down. The whole crowd was on the shore, at the edge of the lake.
4.2: Jesus was teaching them with many stories. While he was teaching, he said,
4.3: " Listen! A farmer went out to plant his seed.
4.4: While he was planting, some seeds fell along the road. The wild birds came and ate them up.
4.5: Some seeds fell on rocks where there was not much soil. The seeds grew up fast there because the ground was not deep.
4.6: But when the sun came up, the little plants were burned because their roots dried up.
4.7: Some more seeds fell among thorny weeds but the thorny weeds came up and killed them off later. They did not produce fruit.
4.8: And some seeds fell on good soil. They came up, grew, and produced a crop — some 30 times more, some 60 times more, and some 100 times more. "
4.9: Jesus said, " The person who has ears to hear with should use them! "
4.10: When Jesus was alone, the twelve delegates and some other people around Jesus asked him about the meaning of the stories.
4.11: Jesus said, " You have been chosen to learn the secrets of the kingdom of God. All these secrets are given to outsiders in stories
4.12: so that: 'They will certainly see, but they won't understand; and they will certainly hear, but they won't understand. Otherwise they might turn and be forgiven! ' "
4.13: Jesus said to them, " Since you don't understand this story, how can you understand any of the other stories?
4.14: The farmer was planting God's message.
4.15: The message was planted like seeds along the road. When those people hear it, Satan comes quickly and takes away the message which was planted in them.
4.16: Some people are like the seeds which were planted on rocks. When they hear the message, they accept it immediately with gladness.
4.17: However, they don't have deep roots in themselves; they don't last long. When trouble comes, or persecution comes because of the message, they soon get discouraged.
4.18: Those which were planted among the thorny weeds are the people who heard the message;
4.19: but the worries of this age, deceiving riches, and desires for other things come in and choke the message. It never produces fruit.
4.20: Those seeds which were planted on good soil are the ones who listen to the message and accept it. They produce fruit — some of it is 30 times more, some is 60 times more, and some 100 times more. "
4.21: Jesus said to them, " Do you bring a lamp, so that you can put it under a basket or under the bed? It is supposed to go on top of a table.
4.22: Everything that is hidden will become clear. Every secret thing will be made known.
4.23: If a person has ears to hear with, he should use them! "
4.24: Jesus said to them, " Think carefully about what you hear. The way you give is the way God will give to you. But God will give you more than you give!
4.25: Because the person who has something, he will get more. But this will happen to the person who has almost nothing: even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him. "
4.26: Jesus said, " The kingdom of God is like this: a man puts seed in the ground.
4.27: The seed comes up and grows while he sleeps at night and when he gets up every day. The man doesn't know how this happens.
4.28: The ground produces by itself. The grass comes first, then the head, then the ripe wheat in the head.
4.29: When the crop is ready, the man soon cuts it with a sickle; harvest time has come. "
4.30: Jesus said, " What is the kingdom of God like? What can I compare it with?
4.31: It is like the seed of the mustard plant which someone puts in the ground. It is one of the smallest seeds on earth.
4.32: But after it is planted and comes up, it is one of the largest garden plants. It produces great branches. Even wild birds build nests in it and are protected from the sun. "
4.33: With many stories like these, Jesus was telling them the message — but only as much as they were able to understand.
4.34: Jesus always spoke to them with a story. But when he was alone with his students, he would explain everything.
4.35: When it was evening of that same day, Jesus said to them, " Let us go across Lake Galilee. "
4.36: Jesus was in the boat. They took him and left the crowd. Other boats went with him.
4.37: Suddenly, there was a storm — a strong wind. The waves were getting into the boat; it was about to be filled with water.
4.38: But Jesus was in the back of the boat, asleep on a pillow. They woke him up, saying, " Teacher, we are going to die; don't you care? "
4.39: Jesus woke up and gave an order to the wind and the waves of the lake, " Be still! Stop! " The wind stopped blowing; it was very calm.
4.40: Jesus said to them, " Why were you so afraid? Do you not yet have faith? "
4.41: They were very frightened. They continued to say to one another, " What kind of a man is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him! "

5.1: Jesus and his students came to the other side of the lake, the land where the Gerasene people lived.
5.2: When Jesus was getting out of the boat, a man with an evil spirit met him. This man came from the tombs in the caves.
5.3: His home was among the tombs. No one was able to bind him with chains anymore.
5.4: His hands and feet had been bound many times, but he would always break the chains apart and smash the shackles. No one was strong enough to tame him.
5.5: Day and night he was always in the hills or among the tombs shouting and cutting himself with sharp stones.
5.6: When this man saw Jesus far away, he ran to Jesus and bowed down.
5.7: While Jesus was saying this to him, " Evil spirit, come out of this man! " the man shouted loudly, " What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? In the name of God, I beg you, don't punish me! "
5.9: Jesus asked him, " What is your name? " He said to Jesus, " My name is Legion, because we are many. "
5.10: The man started to beg Jesus many times. He wanted Jesus not to send them out of the area.
5.11: On that hill there was a large herd of pigs feeding.
5.12: They begged Jesus, " Send us into the pigs; we could go into them! "
5.13: Jesus allowed them. So the evil spirits came out of the man and went into the pigs. ( There were about 2, 000 pigs. ) The herd ran down the steep hill and into the lake. They drowned.
5.14: Some men had been taking care of the pigs. They ran away. They told the story in the fields and in the town. The people came to see what had happened.
5.15: They came to Jesus and saw the man sitting there. The man had clothes on and he was in his right mind. This man did not have a legion of evil spirits anymore. The people were afraid.
5.16: There were men who had seen what Jesus did to the man with demons. They told all about the pigs.
5.17: The people began to beg Jesus to leave their area.
5.18: As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who no longer had demons continued to beg Jesus; he wanted to stay with Jesus.
5.19: But Jesus would not allow him to do this. Instead, Jesus said to him, " Go home to your family. Tell them what the Lord has done for you. He has given you mercy. "
5.20: So the man went back and began to preach what Jesus had done for him in the area of Ten Towns. Everyone was amazed.
5.21: After Jesus went back across Lake Galilee in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered together near him. It was beside the lake.
5.22: A man named Jairus came too. He was one of the rulers of the house of worship. When Jairus saw Jesus, he fell down at Jesus' feet,
5.23: asking many times. He said, " My little girl is dying. Please come and put your hand on her so that she will be all right and live! "
5.24: Jesus left with Jairus. A large crowd was following Jesus. They were bumping up against him.
5.25: There was a woman who had a sore which had been bleeding for twelve years.
5.26: She had suffered much. Many doctors had tried to help her. She had spent all the money she had but she was not getting any better — only worse.
5.27: She had heard things about Jesus. So she went behind Jesus in the crowd and touched his robe.
5.28: She was thinking this: " If I can touch his clothes, I will be made well! "
5.29: Immediately the source of her bleeding was dried up. In her body she felt that she had been healed of the disease.
5.30: At once Jesus knew within himself that power had left him. He turned to the crowd and said, " Who touched my clothes? "
5.31: Jesus' students said to him, " You see the crowd. The people are pressing up against you. Yet you say, 'Who touched me? ' "
5.32: But Jesus continued to look around to see who had done this.
5.33: The woman was afraid; she was trembling. She knew what had happened to her. She came and bowed down to Jesus. Then she told him the whole truth.
5.34: Jesus said to her, " Dear woman, you are made well, because you believed. Go in peace. Be healed from your disease! "
