5.35: While Jesus was still speaking, some people came from the house of the worship ruler. They said, " Your daughter has died! Why bother the Teacher anymore? "
5.36: When Jesus heard this message, he said to the ruler of the house of worship, " Don't be afraid! Just believe! "
5.37: Jesus did not allow anyone to go with him — only Peter, Jacob, and John ( Jacob and John were brothers. )
5.38: They went into the ruler's house. Jesus saw that there was confusion. Many people were crying loudly and showing great sadness.
5.39: Jesus went and said to them, " Why are you making so much noise and crying? The child is not dead; she is only sleeping. "
5.40: They laughed at Jesus. After he made them all leave, Jesus took the child's father and mother along and those who were with Jesus. He went into the room where the child was.
5.41: Jesus held the child's hand and said to her, " Talitha, koum! " ( This means " My little lamb, I tell you, get up! " in Aramaic ).
5.42: Immediately the little girl stood up and began walking around. ( She was twelve years old. ) They were shocked.
5.43: Jesus gave them many strong warnings: " Don't make this known to anyone! " Then Jesus told them to give her something to eat.

6.1: Jesus left there and came to his own hometown. His students went along behind him.
6.2: When the Sabbath day came, Jesus began to teach in the house of worship. Many people were listening; they were amazed. They said, " Where did Jesus get all these things? Who gave him this wisdom? How do such miracles happen by his hands?
6.3: He is the one who works as a carpenter. He is the son of Mary. His brothers are: Jacob, Joseph, Judas, and Simon. His sisters are here with us too. " They were ashamed of Jesus.
6.4: Jesus said this to them: " A prophet is not accepted in his own hometown, or among his relatives, or in his own family. "
6.5: Jesus was not able to perform many miracle there. He only put his hands on a few sick people and made them well.
6.6: He was amazed that they did not believe. Jesus was going around all the villages, teaching people.
6.7: He called for his twelve delegates. He began to send them out in pairs, giving them authority over evil spirits.
6.8: Jesus ordered them: " When you travel, don't carry anything else along — no food, no bag, no money in your belt, and only one walking stick.
6.9: Wear a pair of shoes, but don't wear an extra shirt. "
6.10: Jesus continued to say to them, " When you go into a house, stay there until it is time to leave.
6.11: When people in one place don't welcome you, or they won't listen to you, leave there and shake off the dust from under your feet. This will be a warning to them. "
6.12: So Jesus' students went out. They preached that people must change their hearts.
6.13: They were rubbing olive oil on many sick people and healing them. They were throwing out many demons.
6.14: King Herod Antipas heard about Jesus. Jesus had become famous. People were saying, " John ( the one who immersed people ) has been raised from death! This is why miracles are working in him. "
6.15: Other people were saying, " He is Elijah! " Some other people were saying, " He is a prophet, like one of the prophets from long ago. "
6.16: When Herod heard this, he was thinking, " I cut off John's head; he must have been raised to life. "
6.17: Herod had arrested John, tied him up, and put him in jail. He did this because of Herodias. Herod had married her, even though she was the wife of Philip, Herod's brother.
6.18: John was always saying this to Herod: " It is not right for you to have your brother's wife! "
6.19: So Herodias held a grudge against John. She wanted to kill him, but she was not able to
6.20: because Herod was afraid of John. He knew that John was a good holy man; therefore he protected John. When Herod heard John preach, Herod was in doubt about many things, but Herod liked to listen to John.
6.21: One day Herodias' opportunity came. It was on Herod's birthday. He gave a dinner for his important government officials, army commanders, and leaders in the Galilee.
6.22: Herodias' daughter came in and danced. She pleased Herod and his guests. The king said to the girl, " Ask for whatever you want, and I will give it to you. "
6.23: He vowed to her, " I will give you whatever you ask for — even half of my kingdom! "
6.24: She left and asked her mother, " What should I ask for? " Herodias said, " The head of John! " ( The one who immersed people. )
6.25: At once the girl hurried back to the king. She demanded, " I want you to give me the head of John on a plate — now! "
6.26: The king was very sad but, because of the vow and the guests, Herod didn't want to refuse her.
6.27: Immediately the king sent a guard away with orders to bring John's head. He left. He cut off John's head in the prison.
6.28: He brought the head on a plate and gave it to the girl. The girl gave it to her mother.
6.29: When John's students heard about this, they came and carried away John's body. They put it in a tomb.
6.30: The delegates came together to Jesus. They told him everything they had done and taught.
6.31: There were so many people coming and going that they didn't even have a chance to eat. So Jesus said to them, " Let us go away to a quiet place to be alone. We can get some rest. "
6.32: So they left in a boat to be alone in a place where there were no people,
6.33: but many people saw them leaving and recognized them. From all the towns, together they ran ahead on land to where Jesus and his delegates were going.
6.34: When Jesus got out of the boat, he saw a large crowd; he felt sorry for them because they were like sheep that didn't have a shepherd. So he began to teach them many things.
6.35: Since it was already getting late, Jesus' students came to him and said, " This is a remote place and it is already very late.
6.36: Tell the people to go away. They need to buy something to eat for themselves in the fields and villages around here. "
6.37: Jesus answered them, " You give them something to eat! " They said to him, " Should we leave and buy 200 silver coins' worth of food and give them something to eat? "
6.38: Jesus said to them, " How much food do you have? Go see! " They found out that they had five loaves of bread and two fish.
6.39: Jesus ordered the people to sit down on the green grass in groups.
6.40: They sat down in groups of 50 or 100.
6.41: Jesus took the five loaves of bread and two fish. He looked up to heaven and thanked God for the food and divided the loaves of bread. Then he began giving them to his students so that they could distribute them to all the people. Jesus also divided the two fish for everyone.
6.43: They gathered up all the pieces of bread which were left over. They filled twelve large baskets with this bread and the fish.
6.44: ( There were 5, 000 men who were eating. )
6.45: Immediately Jesus asked his students to get into the boat and go on ahead to the other side of Lake Galilee to the town of Bethsaida. Jesus was sending the crowd away.
6.46: After Jesus sent the people away, he went to a mountain to pray.
6.47: That night the boat was in the middle of the lake. Jesus was alone on land.
6.48: He saw that his students were rowing hard because the wind was against them. It was about three o'clock in the morning. Jesus came to them; he was walking on the lake. He wanted to pass them by
6.49: but they saw him walking on the lake. They thought that Jesus was a ghost. They cried out;
6.50: they all saw him. They were afraid, but Jesus soon talked with them. He said, " Be strong! It is I. Don't be afraid. "
6.51: Jesus stepped into the boat with them. The wind stopped. They were completely astonished,
6.52: because they did not understand the miracle of the loaves of bread. Their heart was still hard.
6.53: After they crossed over, they came to the shore at Gennesaret. They tied up their boat.
6.54: After they left the boat, people recognized Jesus.
6.55: People began running all over that area. Wherever they heard that Jesus was, they brought sick people on small beds.
6.56: Jesus went into villages, towns, fields, and marketplaces — they placed the sick in the marketplaces. They were begging him to let them touch the tassel of his robe. The people who touched him were made well.

7.1: Some teachers of the law and some Pharisees came from Jerusalem to get together with Jesus.
7.2: They saw that some of Jesus' students were eating with unholy ( that is, unwashed ) hands.
7.3: ( The Pharisees and all the Jewish people won't eat unless they wash their hands with a ceremony. They carefully obey the tradition of the leaders.
7.4: They won't eat anything from the market place unless they wash it. They have received many other rules about washing cups, pots, and copper bowls which they must obey. )
7.5: The Pharisees and the teachers of the law asked Jesus, " Why are your students breaking the tradition of the elders? They are eating bread with unholy hands! "
7.6: Jesus said to them, " How right Isaiah was when he prophesied about you hypocrites. As it is written: 'These people honor Me with their lips, but their heart is far away from Me.
7.7: It does no good for them to worship Me. They teach commands made only by men, not God! '
7.8: You have forgotten about God's command and you are obeying the old commands of man. "
7.9: Jesus continued to speak to them, " You have a clever way of rejecting God's command so that you may keep your traditions.
7.10: Moses said, 'You must honor and obey your father and mother. ' and, 'The person who curses his father or mother must die. '
7.11: But you say that if anyone says to his father or mother, 'It is Corban' ( This means: 'Whatever you might have gotten from me is a gift to God. ' ),
7.12: then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother.
7.13: You are taking away the authority of God's teaching by using the traditions of men you have received. And you are doing many other things like this. "
7.14: Again, Jesus called for the crowd. He said to them, " Listen and understand!
7.15: What goes into the mouth from outside is not able to make a person unholy. No, the things which come out of the mouth make a person unholy.
7.16: If any person has ears to hear with, let him use them. "
7.17: Jesus went into a house away from the crowd. His students began asking him about the story.
7.18: Jesus said to them, " Do you still not understand? You know that everything which goes into a person from the outside is not able to make him unholy.
7.19: It does not go into his heart. No, it enters his stomach. Then it comes out as waste. ( Here Jesus was saying that all foods are clean. )
7.20: But what comes out of the mouth of a person makes him unholy.
7.21: These things come from the inside of man's heart: evil thoughts, sexual sin, stealing, murder,
7.22: unlawful sexual intercourse, greed, all kinds of evil things, treachery, sensuality, jealousy, slander, bragging, foolishness.
7.23: All these evil things come from the inside; they make a person unholy. "
7.24: Jesus got up from there and went up to the area near the city of Tyre. He went into a house. ( Jesus didn't want anyone to know where he was, but it was not possible for him to hide. )
7.25: Soon a woman heard about Jesus. Her daughter had an evil spirit. The woman came and bowed down at Jesus' feet.
7.26: She was not a Jew. She was born in the land of Phoenicia, an area of Syria. She kept begging Jesus to throw the demon out of her daughter.
7.27: Jesus said to her, " Let the children eat first. It is not good to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs. "
7.28: But the woman answered Jesus, " Yes, Lord, but even the dogs under the table eat the crumbs from the children! "
7.29: Jesus said to her, " Go! The demon has come out of your daughter — because of your answer! "
7.30: The woman went back home and found her child lying on a bed. And the demon was gone.
7.31: Jesus left the area near Tyre and went through the city of Sidon to Lake Galilee and the area of Ten Towns.
7.32: Some people brought a man to Jesus. They begged Jesus to put his hand on the man and heal him. The man was deaf. It was very hard for him to talk.
7.33: Jesus took the man along with him to be alone, away from the crowd. Then Jesus put his fingers into the man's ears, made some spit, and touched the man's tongue.
7.34: Looking up to heaven, Jesus sighed. He said to the man, " Ephphatha! " ( This means, " Be opened! " in Aramaic )
7.35: Then the man could hear clearly and the bond on his speech was released. He began to talk plainly.
7.36: Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about this. But the more he warned them, the more they proclaimed it!
7.37: The people were shocked. They said, " He has done everything well. He causes deaf people to hear and people who could not speak to speak! "

8.1: During that time there was another large crowd. They didn't have anything to eat. Jesus called his students and said to them,
8.2: " I feel sorry for the people. They have stayed with me for three days without eating anything.
8.3: I don't want to send them away hungry; they might faint on the road. Some of them have come from a long way off. "
8.4: Jesus' students asked him, " Where could we get enough to satisfy these people in this far away place? "
8.5: Jesus asked them, " How many loaves of bread do you have? " They answered, " Seven. "
8.6: Jesus ordered the crowd to sit down on the ground. He took the seven loaves of bread and thanked God. He divided it and began giving it to his students so that they could distribute it. The students did so.
8.7: They had a few fish too. Jesus blessed the fish and told the students to distribute them.
8.8: The people ate and were satisfied. They gathered up all the pieces of food which were left over. There were seven baskets full.
8.9: ( There were about 4, 000 men. ) Then Jesus sent them away.
8.10: Jesus got into a boat with his students. He went to the Dalmanutha area.
8.11: The Pharisees came out and began to argue with Jesus. They were trying to make Jesus prove that he came from God.
8.12: Jesus groaned in his spirit. He said, " Why do the people living today ask for a miracle? I am telling you the truth: no proof like that will be given to them! "
8.13: Then Jesus left them. He got into the boat and went across Lake Galilee.
8.14: Jesus' students forgot to bring along loaves of bread with them in the boat. They had only one loaf of bread.
8.15: Jesus warned them, " Be careful! Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of the students of Herod Antipas. "
8.16: They began talking to one another, saying, " Jesus said this because we don't have any loaves of bread. "
8.17: Jesus knew what was on their mind. He said, " Why are you talking about having no bread? Don't you know yet? Do you still not understand? Do you have hard hearts?
8.18: Do you have eyes, but don't see clearly? Do you have ears, but do not understand? Surely you remember
8.19: when I divided the five loaves of bread for the 5, 000 men. How many large baskets full of leftovers did you pick up? " Jesus' students answered, " Twelve. "
8.20: Jesus said, " When I divided the seven loaves of bread for the 4, 000 men, how many small baskets full of leftovers did you pick up? " They answered, " Seven. "
8.21: Jesus said to them, " Do you still not understand? "
8.22: Jesus and his students came into Bethsaida. The people were carrying a blind man to Jesus. They begged Jesus to touch him.
8.23: He held the blind man's hand and led him outside the village. After Jesus spit into the man's eyes, he put his hands on him. Jesus asked him, " Do you see anything? "
8.24: The man looked up and said, " I see people moving around; they look like trees to me! "
8.25: Jesus put his hands on the man's eyes again. Then the man could see; his sight came back. He could see everything clearly.
8.26: Jesus sent the man home with these words, " Don't go into the village! "
8.27: Then Jesus and his students went away to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. Along the road Jesus asked his students this question: " Who do people say I am? "
8.28: They answered, " Some people say John ( the one who immersed people ). Other people say you are Elijah, and others say you are one of the prophets. "
8.29: But Jesus continued to ask them, " But who do you say I am? " Peter answered Jesus, " You are the Messiah! "
8.30: Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about him.
8.31: Jesus began to teach them, " I must suffer many things. I will be rejected by the Jewish elders, the most important priests, and the teachers of the law. I will be killed, but after three days I will be raised from death. "
8.32: Jesus was speaking this message to them very plainly. Yet, Peter came to Jesus and tried to correct him.
8.33: Jesus turned around and looked at his students. He warned Peter, " Get behind me, Satan! You are not thinking the way God thinks, but the way man thinks. "
8.34: Jesus called the crowd together with his students. He said to them, " If anyone wants to follow me, he must carry his cross and follow me. He must say 'no' to himself.
8.35: The person who wants to save his life will lose it, but every person who gives his life to others for me and for the Good News will save it.
8.36: What good is it if a person gains the whole world, but loses his own soul?
8.37: What can a person use to trade for his soul?
8.38: If a person in this unfaithful, sinful generation is ashamed of me and my words, I will be ashamed of him when I come with holy angels in the glory of my Father. "

9.1: Jesus said to them, " I am telling you the truth: there are some people standing here who will not die until they have seen God's kingdom come with power. "
9.2: After six days, Jesus took Peter, Jacob, and John and took them up a tall mountain to be alone. Jesus' appearance began to change in front of them.
9.3: His clothes became shining white — as white as white could be. ( No one on earth could make them so white. )
9.4: Moses and Elijah appeared to them. These two men were talking to Jesus.
9.5: Peter said to Jesus, " Master, it is good that we are here. We will make three holy tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah. "
9.6: ( He didn't know what to say; they were afraid. )
9.7: A cloud came all around them and a Voice came from the cloud: " This is My Son, and I give Myself to him, for his good, expecting nothing in return. Listen to what he says! "
9.8: Suddenly they looked around. They no longer saw anyone except Jesus. He was the only one with them.
9.9: As they were going down the mountain, Jesus ordered them, " Don't tell anyone about what you saw until I rise from death. "
9.10: They obeyed and kept it to themselves. But they began to argue among themselves about what Jesus meant when he said, "... until I rise from death. "
9.11: They began to ask Jesus, " Why do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come before the Messiah does? "
9.12: Jesus answered, " Elijah does come first and he restores all things. Then why is it written that the Son of Man will suffer many things and be rejected?
9.13: No, I am telling you, Elijah did come first! They treated him the way they wanted to, as it was written about him. "
9.14: When they got back to the other students, they saw a large crowd around them. The teachers of the law were arguing with them.
9.15: As soon as the whole crowd saw Jesus, they were very surprised. They ran to him and greeted him.
9.16: Jesus asked them, " Why are you arguing with them? "
9.17: One man in the crowd answered Jesus, " Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a spirit that stops him from talking.
9.18: It attacks him and throws him down on the ground. He foams at the mouth and grinds his teeth. His body becomes stiff. I told your students so that they could throw out the spirit, but they were not strong enough. "
9.19: Jesus said to them, " You people are a generation with no faith! How long must I be with you and put up with you? Bring your son here! "
9.20: They brought the boy to Jesus. When the evil spirit saw Jesus, the boy lost control of himself. He fell down on the ground and began rolling around, foaming at the mouth.
9.21: Jesus asked the boy's father, " How long has he been like this? " The father said, " Since he was a child.
9.22: This spirit wants to kill him. It often throws him into fire or into water. Take pity on us! Help us, if you are able to! "
9.23: Jesus said to him, " 'If you are able'? All things are possible for the person who believes. "
9.24: Immediately the boy's father cried out, " I believe! Help me overcome my unbelief! "
9.25: When Jesus saw that a crowd was coming together, he gave an order to the evil spirit, " O spirit that keeps this boy from talking and hearing, I command you — come out of him! Never go into him again! "
9.26: The spirit screamed and again made the boy fall down and roll around on the ground. Then the spirit left. The boy looked as if he was dead. Many people said, " He's dead! "
9.27: But Jesus took hold of his hand and raised him up. The boy was on his feet.
9.28: After Jesus went into a house, his students began asking him questions when they were alone, " Why were we not able to throw out the spirit? "
9.29: Jesus answered them, " By fasting and prayer is the only way that you can throw this kind out. "
9.30: They left there and traveled through the Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were
9.31: because he was teaching his students. This is what he was telling them: " I am being turned over to some men. They will kill me but, three days after my death, I will rise to life. "
9.32: They did not understand the meaning of this but they were too afraid to ask him.
9.33: They came to the town of Capernaum. After they had gone into a house, Jesus began to ask them questions, " What were you arguing about along the road? "
9.34: They wouldn't answer him because on the road they were arguing with one another about who was the most important.
9.35: Jesus sat down and called for the twelve delegates. He said to them, " If one of you wants to be number one, he should be in last place. He should serve everyone. "
9.36: Jesus took a small child and stood him in the middle of them. He put his arms around the child and said to them,
9.37: " The person who welcomes one of the children like this one in my name welcomes me. And when a person welcomes me, that person welcomes the One who sent me. "
9.38: John said to Jesus, " Teacher, we saw someone throwing out demons by using your name. He was not following us! We kept telling him to stop because he was not following us. "
9.39: But Jesus said, " Don't stop him. There is no one who can perform a miracle in my name and then say something evil about me.
9.40: If someone is not against us, he is for us.
9.41: " If anyone gives you a cup of water in my name because you belong to the Messiah, I am telling you the truth, that person will not lose his reward.
9.42: " If someone causes one of these little ones to sin who believe in me, it would be better for him to have a large rock hanging around his neck and to be thrown into the sea.
9.43: " If your hand makes you sin, cut it off! It would be better for you to go into eternal life injured than to go away with two hands into hell, where the fire cannot be put out.
9.44: Where: 'Their worms never die, and the fire never goes out. '
9.45: " If your foot makes you sin, cut it off! It would be better for you to go into eternal life crippled than to be thrown into hell having two feet,
9.46: where: 'Their worms never die, and the fire never goes out. '
9.47: " If your eye makes you sin, throw it away! It would be better for you to go into the kingdom of God with only one eye than to be thrown into hell with two eyes.
9.48: Hell is where: 'Their worms never die, and the fire never goes out. '
9.49: " Every person will be salted with fire —
9.50: salt is a good thing but if the salt loses its salty taste, then it is no good. You cannot make it salty again. Have salt in yourselves; be at peace with one another. "

10.1: Jesus got up from there and went to the region of Judea which is on the other side of the Jordan River. Again, crowds traveled to him. Jesus was teaching them as he always did.
10.2: Some Pharisees came to Jesus. They were testing him with this question: " Is it all right for a man to divorce his wife? "
10.3: Jesus answered them, " What did Moses command you? "
10.4: They said, " Moses allowed a man who was divorcing his wife to give her divorce papers. "
10.5: Jesus said to them, " Moses wrote this command because your hearts were hard.
10.6: But in the beginning, when God created people, 'He made them male and female. '
10.7: and, 'This is why a man will leave his father and mother.
10.8: The husband and wife will become one flesh. ' — So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
10.9: Man must not separate what God has joined together. "
10.10: When they were in the house again, Jesus' students began to ask him about this.
10.11: Jesus said to them, " If a man divorces his wife and marries another woman, he is committing unlawful sexual intercourse against her.
10.12: If she divorces her husband and she marries another man, she is committing unlawful sexual intercourse. "
10.13: Then some people brought their small children to Jesus so that he could touch them, but his students told the people to stop doing that.
10.14: When Jesus saw this, it bothered him. He said to them, " Let the little children come to me. Don't stop them because the kingdom of God belongs to people who are like these little children.
10.15: I am telling you the truth: you must accept God's kingdom as a little child accepts things, or you will never enter it! "
10.16: Jesus put his arms around the children. He put his hands on them and blessed them.
10.17: As Jesus was leaving, a man ran up to him and kneeled down. He asked him, " Good Teacher, what must I do to get eternal life? "
10.18: Jesus said to him, " Why do you call me good? Only God is good.
10.19: But I will answer your question. You know the commands: 'You must not murder. '; 'You must not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. '; 'You must not steal. '; 'You must not lie. '; 'You must not cheat anyone. '; 'You must honor and obey your father and mother. ' "
10.20: The man said to Jesus, " Teacher, I have obeyed all these commands since I was a boy! "
10.21: Jesus was giving himself to the man, for his good, expecting nothing in return. He looked into his eyes and said to him, " But there is still one more thing you need to do: go, sell everything you have, and give it to the poor people. Then you will have a treasure in heaven. Then come, take up the cross, and follow me! "
10.22: But when Jesus said this, the man's face looked gloomy. He went away sad because he owned many things and wanted to keep them.
10.23: Then Jesus looked around and said to his students, " It will be hard for people who own many things to enter the kingdom of God. "
10.24: The students were amazed at Jesus' words. Again Jesus said to them, " My children, it is so hard for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God.
10.25: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God! "
10.26: Jesus' students were completely amazed. They said to one another, " Then who can be saved? "
10.27: Jesus looked into their eyes and said, " God can do things which do not seem possible to man. God can do anything! "
10.28: Then Peter began to say to Jesus, " Look, we have left everything and followed you! "
10.29: Jesus said, " I am telling you the truth: every person who has left his home, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children, or fields ( because of me and because of the Good News )
10.30: will surely be rewarded 100 times more now, in this time, with houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, fields — and with them, persecutions! However, he will get eternal life in the next age.
10.31: Many people who seem as though they are not important now will be important at that time. Those who seem important now will not be important then. "
10.32: They were on the road; Jesus was walking ahead of them, and going up to Jerusalem. This surprised them. Those who were following were afraid. Then Jesus took the twelve delegates aside. He began to tell them what was about to happen to him.
10.33: " Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem. The most important priests and the teachers of the law will turn against me. They will condemn me to death. Then they will give me to non - Jewish men.
10.34: Those people will laugh at me, spit on me, beat me with whips, and kill me, but I will rise from death on the third day. "
10.35: Jacob and John, the two sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus. They said to him, " Teacher, we want you to do us a favor. "
10.36: Jesus said to them, " What do you want me to do for you? "
10.37: They said to him, " Allow us to sit on thrones in your glory, one at your right side and one at your left side. "
10.38: Jesus said to them, " You don't know what you're asking. Can you drink the cup of suffering which I am drinking? Can you be immersed in the trouble in which I am being immersed? "
10.39: They said to Jesus, " We are able! " Jesus said to them, " Yes, you will drink from the cup of suffering which I am drinking, and you will be immersed in the trouble in which I am immersed,
10.40: but the privilege of sitting at my right side or my left side is not mine to give. No, that belongs to the people for whom it has been prepared. "
10.41: When the ten delegates heard about this, they began to be angry with Jacob and John.
10.42: Jesus called for them and said, " You know there are rulers of the world who seem to rule over their people. Important men use their authority over them.
10.43: You must not think that way. Instead, if one of you wants to be great, he should be your servant.
10.44: If one of you wants to be important, he should be the slave of everyone
10.45: because I did not come to be served. Instead, I came to serve and give my life to pay for many people's sins. "
10.46: They went into Jericho. Jesus, his students, and a large crowd left Jericho later. There was a blind man named Bartimaeus ( the son of Timaeus ). He was sitting beside the road. He was a beggar.
10.47: When he heard: " It is Jesus from Nazareth! " he began to shout, " Jesus! Son of David! Please help me! "
10.48: Some of the people told him to be quiet but he began shouting even louder, " Son of David! Please help me! "
10.49: Jesus stopped there and said, " Call him. " So they called for the blind man. They said to him, " Cheer up! Get up, Jesus is calling for you! "
10.50: The blind man threw his robe aside and jumped to his feet. He went toward Jesus.
10.51: Jesus asked him, " What do you want me to do for you? " The blind man said to Jesus, " Master, I want to see again! "
10.52: Jesus said to him, " Go. You are made well because you believed. " Immediately the man was able to see again. He began to follow Jesus on the road.

11.1: When Jesus and his students were coming near to Jerusalem, close to the towns of Bethphage and Bethany on the Hill of Olives, Jesus sent two of his students on ahead.
11.2: He said to them, " Go into the village just ahead of you. As you are going in, you will soon find a young donkey tied up. No one has ridden it yet. Untie it and bring it to me.
11.3: And if anyone says anything to you about why you are doing this, say, 'The Lord, its owner, needs it. ' Then he will send it here immediately. "
11.4: They went away and found the young donkey out on the street tied at the door. As they were untying it,
11.5: some of the people standing there asked them, " What are you doing? Why are you untying this young donkey? "
11.6: They answered them exactly as Jesus had told them. So they let them go.
11.7: They brought the young donkey to Jesus and threw their clothes on top of it. Jesus sat on it.
11.8: Many people spread their clothes on the road. Other people cut down branches in the fields, and spread them on the road too.
11.9: The people in front and in back were shouting, " Hosanna! Give praise to this one who is coming by the authority of the Lord God.
11.10: Give praise to the future kingdom of our ancestor David. Hosanna to God! "
11.11: Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple courtyard. He looked around at everything there, but it was already late so he went away with the twelve delegates to Bethany.
11.12: The next day, as they were leaving the town of Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
11.13: Far away he saw a fig tree with lots of leaves. So he went to it to find something to eat. But when he came to it, he found nothing — just leaves. ( It was not the season for figs. )
11.14: Jesus spoke to the tree, " May no one ever eat fruit from you! " Jesus' students were listening.
11.15: They came into Jerusalem. Then Jesus went into the temple courtyard and he began driving out all the people who were buying and selling. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves.
11.16: Jesus was not allowing anyone to carry containers through the temple courtyard.
11.17: Jesus was teaching them, " It is written, 'My house will be called a place of prayer for all nations. ' — But you have changed it into a hiding place for thieves! "
11.18: When the most important priests and teachers of the law heard this, they continued trying to find a way to kill Jesus. They were afraid of Jesus because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.
11.19: When evening came, Jesus and his students left Jerusalem.
11.20: Early the next morning, while they were walking along, they saw the same fig tree. It was dried up at the roots.
11.21: Peter remembered what happened the day before. He said to Jesus, " Master, look at the fig tree which you spoke to! It has dried up! "
11.22: Jesus answered them, " Have faith in God.
11.23: I am telling you the truth: you could say to this mountain, 'Pick yourself up and throw yourself into the sea! ' and it would happen for you. You must not doubt in your heart. Instead, believe that what you are saying will happen.
11.24: " This is why I am telling you: when you are praying and asking God for something, believe that you have received it, and it will happen for you.
11.25: And when you stand praying, if you have something against someone, forgive him. Then your heavenly Father will forgive you of the things you have done wrong.
11.26: But if you do not forgive others, your Father, who is in heaven, will not forgive your sins, either. "
11.27: They came into Jerusalem. While Jesus was walking around in the temple courtyard, the most important priests, the teachers of the law, and some Jewish leaders came to him.
11.28: They were asking him, " What sort of authority do you have to do these things? Who gave you this authority? "
11.29: Jesus answered them, " I will also ask you a question. Answer me and I will tell you what sort of authority I have to do these things.
11.30: Was John's immersion from God or from man? Answer me! "
11.31: They began thinking this among themselves: " If we say 'from God', then he will say this to us: 'Why didn't you believe John? '
11.32: But if we say 'from man', we are afraid of the people. All of them truly believe that John was a prophet. "
11.33: So they answered Jesus, " We don't know! " Jesus said to them, " Then I am not telling you what sort of authority I have to do these things either. "

12.1: Then Jesus began to use examples to talk to the people — " A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a hole for the wine press, and built a lookout tower. Then he rented the land to some farmers and went away on a trip.
12.2: At harvest time, he sent a slave to the farmers. He wanted to receive his share of the grapes in the field from the farmers.
12.3: But the farmers grabbed the slave and beat him up. They sent him away with nothing.
12.4: Again, the owner sent another slave to them. They wounded this slave in the head and made fun of him.
12.5: The owner sent another slave. The farmers killed him. They beat up and killed many slaves.
12.6: But the owner still had one man — his son, to whom he gives himself, for his good, expecting nothing in return. So he sent him to them last of all, thinking, 'The farmers will show respect for my son. '
12.7: But those farmers said to one another, 'When the owner dies, his son will get the vineyard. Come, let us kill him and we will have his field! '
12.8: So they took the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
12.9: What will the owner of the vineyard do to those farmers? He will come and kill them. After that he will give the field to some other farmers.
12.10: " You have read this Scripture: 'The stone that the builders did not want will become the cornerstone. '
12.11: The Lord God causes this to happen; it is a wonderful thing for us to see. "
12.12: They wanted to arrest Jesus but they were afraid of the people. They knew Jesus had told this story against them. They left him and went away.
12.13: They sent some of the Pharisees and students of Herod Antipas to Jesus. They wanted to trap him with a question.
12.14: They came to him and said, " Teacher, we know you are true. It doesn't matter to you what people think. You don't pay attention to how important someone is. Instead, you teach God's true way. Is it right that we should pay taxes to Caesar? Yes or no? Should we pay? Or should we not pay? "
12.15: But Jesus knew what they were actually trying to do. He asked, " Why are you trying to trap me? Bring me a coin so I can see it. "
12.16: They brought it. Then Jesus asked them, " Whose name and picture is on it? " They said to him, " Caesar's. "
12.17: Jesus said to them, " Give to Caesar the things which are Caesar's. Give to God the things which belong to God. " And they were amazed at Jesus.
12.18: Some Sadducees came to Jesus. ( Sadducees believe that no one will rise from death. ) They were asking Jesus,
12.19: " Teacher, Moses wrote this to us: 'If a brother dies and he leaves a wife behind, but no children, his brother must marry the widow. Then they will have children for the dead brother. '
12.20: There were seven brothers. The first one got married, but he died, leaving no children.
12.21: The second brother married the widow. He died too, leaving no children. The same thing happened to the third brother.
12.22: All seven men married her. None of the seven brothers had any children. The woman was the last of all to die. Therefore, when this woman rises from death, whose wife will she be? "
12.24: Jesus answered them, " You are wrong! You don't know either the Scriptures or God's power.
12.25: When people rise from death, they don't marry each other. Instead, they are like angels in heaven.
12.26: Do people rise from death? I know you have read what it says in the book of Moses at the place about the burning bush, how God said to him, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. '
12.27: God is not a God of dead people; He is the God of people who are alive! You are so wrong! "
12.28: One of the teachers of the law came to Jesus. This man had heard them arguing with Jesus. He knew that Jesus had answered them well. So he asked Jesus, " What is the most important command? "
12.29: Jesus answered, " This is the most important one: 'Listen, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord.
12.30: You must give yourself to the Lord your God, for His good, expecting nothing in return, with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength. '
12.31: The second most important command is this: 'You must give yourself to other people, for their good, expecting nothing in return, the same way you give to yourself. '. There are no commands more important than these two. "
12.32: The teacher of the law said to Jesus, " Fine, Teacher, you spoke the truth. There is only one God; besides Him, there are no other gods.
12.33: Giving yourself to God, for His good, expecting nothing in return, with all your heart, with all your understanding, and with all your strength, and giving yourself to other people the same way you give to yourself — these are more important than all sacrifices and offerings of animals. "
12.34: When Jesus saw that the man's answer was very wise, he said to him, " You are not far from God's kingdom. " No one dared to ask Jesus another trick question.
12.35: While Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courtyard, he asked, " How can the teachers of the law claim that the Messiah is the son of David?
12.36: By the power of the Holy Spirit, David himself said: 'The Lord God said to my Lord, " Sit at My right side until I put your enemies under your feet. ' "
12.37: David himself calls the Messiah 'Lord'! So how can the Messiah be the son of David? " A large crowd was gladly listening to Jesus.
12.38: As he was teaching, he said, " Watch out for the teachers of the law! They like to walk around wearing clothes which make them look important. They like the greetings of respect which people give them in the marketplaces.
12.39: They always want the most important seats in the houses of worship and the best seats at the dinners.
12.40: But they are unfair to widows: they steal their homes. Then they make themselves look good by saying long prayers. Because of all this, God will punish these men so much more. "
12.41: Jesus sat next to the temple treasury. He was watching the way the people were putting money in the box. Many people were rich; they put in a lot of money.
12.42: A poor widow came. She put two small coins ( worth less than a penny ) in the box.
12.43: Jesus called his students and said to them, " I am telling you the truth: this poor widow has put more in the box than all those rich people put there.
12.44: The rich have plenty; they only gave what they didn't need, but this woman gave everything she had. She needed that money to live on. "

13.1: As Jesus was leaving the temple courtyard, one of his students said to him, " Teacher, look at the great stones! Look at the great buildings! "
13.2: Jesus said to him, " Do you see all these great buildings? Everything you see here will be destroyed. No stone will stay on top of another. It will be completely destroyed! "
13.3: When Jesus was sitting on the Hillside of Olives across from the temple, Peter, Jacob, John, and Andrew asked him these private questions:
13.4: " Tell us, when will these things happen? How will we know when it is the time for these things to happen? "
13.5: Jesus began to answer them, " Be careful. Don't let anyone fool you.
13.6: Many people will come to you using my name. They will say, 'I am the one! ' And they will fool many people.
13.7: You will hear about wars, and wars which are about to happen. Don't become upset. These things must happen but the end will come later.
13.8: One country will fight against another country. Kings will fight against other kings. There won't be enough food to eat. Everywhere there will be earthquakes. These things are only the beginning of the pain.
13.9: " Watch out for yourselves! They will hand you over to the local courts. They will beat you in their houses of worship. Men will take you to be judged before governors and kings because you are associated with me. You will tell them the truth.
13.10: The Good News must first be preached to all the people in the world.
13.11: When they turn against you and arrest you, don't worry about what you will say. Say whatever is given to you at that time. You are not doing the talking; it is the Holy Spirit.
13.12: " A brother will betray his own brother, putting him to death. A father will do the same thing to his child. Children will rebel against their parents; they will put them to death.
13.13: All men will hate you because of my name. But the person who endures until the end will be saved.
13.14: " When you see 'The Abomination of Desolation' standing where it must not be ( let the reader note the meaning ), then those people who are in the region of Judea must run away to the mountains.
13.15: The person who is on top of his house must not come down and go inside the house to carry things out with him.
13.16: The person who is in the field must not turn back to get his robe.
13.17: At that time, it will be horrible for pregnant women and nursing mothers.
13.18: Pray that the time when you run away will not be during winter.
13.19: " During those days there will be great suffering. Never has there been such suffering since the beginning of the world when God created it until the present time. And there will never be such suffering in the future.
13.20: If that period of time lasted any longer, no one would be left alive. But those times will be cut short because of the elect people God has chosen.
13.21: At that time if someone says to you, 'Look, here is the Messiah! ' or 'There he is! ', don't believe him.
13.22: False messiahs and false prophets will appear. They will perform proofs and miracles to fool people — even God's chosen people, if that were possible.
13.23: Be careful! I am telling you everything ahead of time.
13.24: " After the trouble of those times, 'The sun will become dark. The light of the moon will not be seen.
13.25: The stars will fall from the sky. The powers in the universe will be moved. '
13.26: Then they will see me coming in the clouds with much power and glory.
13.27: Then I will send my angels out. They will gather together my chosen people from every place and time.
13.28: " Learn from the story about the fig tree: when its branches start becoming soft and green, you know that summer is near.
13.29: In the same way, when you see all of these things happening, you will know that the time is very, very near.
13.30: I am telling you the truth: all of these things will happen in this generation!
13.31: " The world will be destroyed but my words will never be destroyed!
13.32: No one knows when that exact time will be. The angels in heaven don't know it. I don't know it. Only the heavenly Father knows.
13.33: Be careful! Watch and pray, because you don't know when the right time will be.
13.34: It will be like a man who left his house for a trip. He gave his slaves authority. Each one of them had a job. He ordered the doorkeeper to watch closely.
13.35: " So watch! You don't know when I am coming. It might be in the evening, at midnight, before dawn, or at sunrise.
13.36: If I come suddenly, you must not let me find you sleeping.
13.37: I am telling you and everyone else — watch! "

14.1: It was two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The most important priests and the teachers of the law were trying to find a way to kill Jesus. They planned to use a trick to arrest him.
14.2: They were saying this: " Let us not begin during the Passover Festival so that there will be no trouble among the people. "
14.3: Jesus was in the town of Bethany in Simon's house. ( Simon had been a leper. ) While Jesus was sitting at the table, a woman opened an alabaster jar of some very expensive perfume. ( It was made of pure nard. ) Then she poured it on his head.
14.4: Some of Jesus' students were there. They were very angry, saying to one another, " Why waste this perfume? "
14.5: This could have been sold for more than 300 silver coins and given to poor people. They yelled angry words at her.
14.6: But Jesus said, " Leave her alone! Why are you bothering her? She has done a good thing to me.
14.7: You will always have poor people with you. When you want to, you can give yourselves to them, but you won't always have me!
14.8: She did what she could. She put perfume on my body ahead of time to prepare it for when I am buried.
14.9: I am telling you the truth: the Good News will be preached in the whole world. Wherever it is told, what she did will be mentioned to remember her. "
14.10: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve delegates, went away to talk to the most important priests; he wanted to give Jesus to them.
14.11: When they heard this, they were pleased. They promised to give Judas some money. Judas was waiting for the best way to give Jesus to them.
14.12: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, they were sacrificing the Passover lambs. Jesus' students said to him, " Where do you want us to go and prepare the Passover meal for you? "
14.13: Jesus sent two of his students, saying to them, " Go into the city. And you will see a man carrying a jar of water. Follow him.
14.14: Enter the house he enters and say this to the owner: 'The Teacher asks that you please show us the room where the Teacher and his students may eat the Passover Feast. '
14.15: He will show you a large room upstairs. This room is ready. Prepare the Passover meal there. "
14.16: So the students left and went into the city. Everything happened just as Jesus told them. Then they prepared the Passover meal.
14.17: When evening came, Jesus sat down at the table with his twelve students.
14.18: While they were sitting down and eating, Jesus said, " I am telling you the truth: one of you will turn against me. He is eating with me! "
14.19: They began to be sad. Each one of them asked Jesus, " I am not the one, am I? "
14.20: Jesus answered, " It is one of the twelve men who dipped his hand in the same dinner bowl with me.
14.21: I will die, just as it is written about me. However, how horrible it will be for that man who turned against me. It would be better if that man had never been born! "
14.22: While they were eating, Jesus took bread and gave thanks. He broke off some of it and gave it to them. He said, " Take it. This bread is my body. "
14.23: Then he took a cup. He gave thanks to God for it and gave it to them. He said, " All of you, drink from it.
14.24: This is my blood for the new covenant. It is being poured out for many people.
14.25: I am telling you the truth: I will never drink the fruit of the vine again until the day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God. "
14.26: Then they sang a song of praise and went out to the Hillside of Olives.
14.27: Then Jesus said to them, " All of you will be ashamed of me. This is written: 'I will strike the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered. '
14.28: But after I rise from death, I will go ahead of you to the Galilee. "
14.29: Peter said to Jesus, " Everyone else may be ashamed of you, but not I! "
14.30: Jesus said to him, " I am telling you the truth: tonight — this very night — you will say you don't even know me. You will do this three different times before the rooster crows a second time! "
14.31: But Peter insisted, " Even if I must die with you, I will always be loyal to you. " All of them were saying the same thing.
14.32: Then they went to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to his students, " Sit here while I go pray. "
14.33: He took Peter, Jacob, and John along with him. He began to feel very sad and depressed.
14.34: Then he said to them, " My soul is full of sorrow; I am going to die. Stay here and be watchful. "
14.35: Then Jesus went ahead a short distance and fell down on the ground. He was praying that, if possible, this time might pass away from him.
14.36: He continued to pray, " Daddy, dear Father, all things are possible for You. Take this cup of suffering away from me, but what You want is more important than what I want. "
14.37: Then Jesus came and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, " Are you asleep, Simon? Were you not strong enough to watch one hour?
14.38: Watch and pray for strength against temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak. "
14.39: Again Jesus went away. He prayed the same prayer.
14.40: Once more, Jesus came and found them sleeping. Their eyes were very tired. They didn't know what to say to him.
14.41: Jesus came back the third time and said to them, " Are you still sleeping and resting? That's enough! The time has come. Listen! I am being handed over to sinful men.
14.42: Get up, we must go. Look! The one who turned against me is near! "
14.43: And immediately, while Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve delegates, came. There was a crowd with him. They had come from the most important priests, the teachers of the law, and the Jewish elders. They had sticks and swords.
14.44: Judas had given them a signal: " Arrest the man to whom I give the kiss of friendship; lead him away carefully. "
14.45: Judas went at once to Jesus and said to him, " Master! " Then Judas kissed him.
14.46: Then they reached out and grabbed Jesus.
14.47: One of the men standing nearby pulled out his sword. He struck the high priest's slave, cutting off his ear.
14.48: Jesus asked them, " Why did you come out here with swords and sticks? Do you think I am a criminal?
14.49: I was teaching in the temple courtyard every day. You did not arrest me there. No, this occurred to make the Scriptures come true. "
14.50: Then all of Jesus' students left him; they ran away.
14.51: There was a young man who was following Jesus. He was wearing only a linen cloth. Some men grabbed him too.
14.52: He left the linen cloth behind and ran away naked.
14.53: They brought Jesus to the high priest. All of the important priests, the teachers of the law, and the Jewish elders came together.
14.54: Peter followed Jesus from a distance. He came as far as the high priest's courtyard. He was sitting with the servants, warming himself by the fire.
14.55: The most important priests in the whole Jewish Council wanted to find some men who would give evidence against Jesus so that they could kill him. But they did not find any real proof.
14.56: Many people were telling lies against Jesus, but their testimony did not match.
14.57: Some men stood up and told lies against Jesus,
14.58: " We heard this man say, 'I will destroy this temple sanctuary built by men and build another one in three days — without human hands! ' "
14.59: Their testimony still did not agree.
14.60: The high priest stood up in the center and asked Jesus, " Aren't you going to answer? What they are saying against you — is it true? "
14.61: Jesus continued to be silent; he gave no answers. Again the high priest asked Jesus, " Are you the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One? "
14.62: Jesus said, " I am! 'You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of God. ' 'He will be coming with the clouds of the sky! ' "
14.63: Then the high priest ripped his own clothes. He said, " Why do we need any more witnesses?
14.64: You heard the evil thing that Jesus just said. How does it look to you? " They all condemned him, saying, " He is guilty! He should be killed! "
14.65: Some of them began to spit on Jesus. They covered his face and hit him with their fists. They said to him, " Prophesy! " And when the guards took charge of him, they started beating him.
14.66: While Peter was down below in the courtyard, one of the high priest's servant girls came to him.
14.67: She saw Peter warming himself. She looked closely at him and said, " You were with Jesus from Nazareth too! "
14.68: But Peter said this was not true, " I don't know what you're talking about. I don't understand! " Later, Peter went out to the front part of the courtyard. The rooster crowed.
14.69: When the servant girl saw him again, she began to say to the men who were standing there, " This man is one of them! "
14.70: Again Peter denied it. After a little while, the men who were standing there began to talk to Peter again, " Surely you are one of Jesus' community. You are from the Galilee! "
14.71: Then Peter began to curse and to swear. He said, " I don't know this man. I don't know what you're talking about! "
14.72: Immediately the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: " Before the rooster crows twice, you will say that you don't even know me — three different times. " Then Peter broke down and began to cry.

15.1: It was early in the morning. The most important priests, the teachers of the law, and the Jewish elders — the whole council — were soon ready. They tied up Jesus, took him, and gave him to Pilate.
15.2: Pilate asked Jesus, " Are you the king of the Jews? " Jesus answered, " Yes. "
15.3: There were many important priests there accusing Jesus.
15.4: Again, Pilate asked him, " Won't you say something? Look at how many charges they are bringing against you! "
15.5: But Jesus gave no answers. Pilate was surprised.
15.6: At each Passover Feast, Pilate always set one prisoner free, the one whom the people wanted.
15.7: A man named Barabbas was arrested with some rebels. They had committed murder during a riot.
15.8: The crowd came up and began to ask Pilate to do the same as he always did for them.
15.9: Pilate answered them, " Do you want me to release the King of the Jews for you? "
15.10: ( Pilate knew they had turned Jesus over to him because they were jealous of Jesus. )
15.11: The most important priests made the people excited. They wanted Pilate to set Barabbas free for them instead of Jesus.
15.12: Again Pilate asked them, " What should I do with Jesus, the one you call 'King of the Jews'? "
15.13: They yelled again, " Nail him to a cross! "
15.14: Pilate said to them, " Why? What crime has Jesus done? " But they continued to yell even more, " Nail him to a cross! "
15.15: Pilate wanted to please the people. So he set Barabbas free for them. After beating Jesus with whips, Pilate handed him over to be nailed to the cross.
15.16: The soldiers took Jesus inside the courtyard of the Roman fortress. The whole group gathered around Jesus.
15.17: They dressed him with a purple robe. They used thorny branches to make a crown.
15.18: Then they began to salute Jesus, saying, " Hail, King of the Jews! "
15.19: They hit Jesus many times on the head with a stick and they were spitting on him. They kneeled down and acted as though they were worshipping him.
15.20: When they finished making fun of him, they took off the purple robe and dressed him with his own clothes. Then they led him away to nail him to the cross.
15.21: There was a man coming into the city from the fields. He was Simon, from the city of Cyrene. ( He was the father of Alexander and Rufus. ) They forced him to carry Jesus' cross.
15.22: They brought Jesus to the place of Golgotha. ( This means 'The Place of the Skull'. )
15.23: They gave him some wine mixed with myrrh, but Jesus didn't drink it.
15.24: Then they nailed him to the cross. The soldiers gambled to see who would get Jesus' clothes.
15.25: It was about nine o'clock in the morning when they nailed Jesus to the cross.
15.26: At the top of the cross, they nailed up his crime with these words: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
15.27: Along with Jesus, two criminals were nailed to crosses. One was at his right side. The other was on his left.
15.28: And the Scripture came true which says, " He was counted with sinners. "
15.29: The people who were passing by shook their heads and said terrible things to Jesus. They said, " You were the one who was going to destroy the temple sanctuary and build it again in three days!
15.30: Save yourself! Come on down from the cross! "
15.31: The most important priests, together with the teachers of the law, made fun of Jesus in the same way. They continued to say, " He saved other people, but he cannot save himself!
15.32: He is the King of Israel, the Messiah; let him come down from the cross now so that we can see and believe. " Even the men who were nailed to the other crosses were insulting Jesus.
15.33: From noon until three o'clock in the afternoon, there was darkness over the whole land.
15.34: About three o'clock, Jesus cried out loudly, " Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? " ( This means: " My God, my God, why did You abandon me? " in Aramaic. )
15.35: Some of the men standing there heard this. They said, " Look! He is calling Elijah. "
15.36: Someone ran and soaked a sponge in some sour wine. Then he put it on the end of a long stick and gave Jesus a drink. Someone said, " Leave him alone! Let us see if Elijah will come down for him! "
15.37: Jesus gave out a loud cry and died.
15.38: The curtain in the temple sanctuary was split from the top to the bottom into two parts.
15.39: There was a Roman army officer standing there in front of Jesus. When he saw the way Jesus died, he said, " This man really was God's Son! "
15.40: Some women were there too. They were far away, watching. Some of them were: Mary ( from the town of Magdal ), Mary ( the mother of the younger Jacob and Joses ), and Salome.
15.41: These women always followed Jesus and helped him while he was in the Galilee. Many women had come up to Jerusalem with Jesus.
15.42: It was already getting late. It was Preparation Day, the day before the Sabbath.
15.43: Joseph came. He was from the town of Arimathea. He was a very important member of the Jewish Council. He was expecting the kingdom of God too. He dared to go to Pilate and ask for the body of Jesus.
15.44: Pilate was surprised that Jesus had already died. He called for the army officer to ask him whether Jesus had been dead for a long time.
15.45: When Pilate found out from the officer that Jesus was dead, he gave the body to Joseph.
15.46: Joseph bought a sheet. He took the body down from the cross and wrapped it in the sheet. Then he put Jesus' body into a tomb which he had cut out of solid rock. He rolled a stone in front of the doorway of the tomb.
15.47: Mary ( the one from the town of Magdal ) and Mary ( the mother of Joses ) were watching where the body was placed.

16.1: When the Sabbath day had passed, Mary ( the one from Magdal ), Mary ( the mother of Jacob ), and Salome bought some sweet - smelling spices. They wanted to rub this on Jesus' body.
16.2: It was now very early on the first day of the week. As the sun was coming up, they were going to the tomb,
16.3: saying to one another, " Who will roll away the stone for us at the doorway of the tomb? "
16.4: ( The stone was very large. ) But they looked up and saw that the stone was already rolled away!
16.5: They walked into the tomb. They saw an angel sitting on the right side. He was wearing a long, white robe. They were stunned.
16.6: But the angel said to them, " Don't be alarmed! You are looking for Jesus from Nazareth, who was nailed to the cross. He is not here. He has risen from death! Look at the place where they put him!
16.7: Now go tell his students that he will go ahead of you to the Galilee. You will see him there, just as he told you. Tell Peter too. "
16.8: The women left the tomb. They ran away. They were trembling. They were shocked. They didn't say anything to anyone because they were afraid.
16.9: When Jesus came from the grave early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary ( the one from Magdal; Jesus had forced seven demons to leave her. ).
16.10: Jesus' students were crying; they were so sad. She went and told them.
16.11: When they heard that Jesus was alive and that he had been seen by Mary, they didn't believe it.
16.12: After this, while two more of them were walking to a field, Jesus used a different form to appear to them.
16.13: They went back and told this to the other students, but the students didn't believe them either.
16.14: Finally, Jesus appeared to the eleven delegates when they were sitting at the table. He rebuked them because their hearts were hard and they did not have faith. They did not believe those who had seen him after he came back from the grave.
16.15: Jesus said to them, " When you have gone into the whole world, preach the Good News to all mankind.
16.16: The person who believes the Good News and is immersed will be saved, but the person who doesn't believe it will be condemned.
16.17: These miracles will go with the ones believing: they will use my name to throw out demons. They will speak languages which are new to them.
16.18: They could hold snakes. If they drink poison, it won't hurt them. They will put their hands on sick people and the sick people will become well. "
16.19: After the Lord Jesus talked with them, he was lifted up into the sky. He sat down at God's right side.
16.20: They left and preached everywhere. And miracles went with them. The Lord used these miracles to prove that the message was true. He was working with them. Amen.

1.1: Dear Theophilus, since many people have tried to give an account of the things which have happened among us,
1.2: they have written the same things that we learned from others that saw those things from the beginning and preached the word.
1.3: I too thought, after I studied everything carefully from the beginning, your Excellency, that I should write it down for you. Therefore, I put it in order in a book
1.4: so you may be sure that the words you have been taught are true.
1.5: During the time when Herod the Great ruled Judea, there was a Jewish priest named Zechariah. He belonged to Abijah's section. His wife came from the family of Aaron. Her name was Elizabeth.
1.6: They were truly being made right before God, doing everything which was right and everything the Lord God commanded. They were spiritually spotless,
1.7: but they had no children; Elizabeth could not have a baby. Both of them were very old, too.
1.8: Zechariah was serving as a priest before God for his priestly division of Abijah.
1.9: The other priests chose him to offer the incense; so he went into the holy place of the temple sanctuary of the Lord God.
1.10: There was a large group of people outside. They were praying at the time the incense was being offered.
1.11: Then, standing on the right side of the incense table, an angel of the Lord God appeared to him.
1.12: When Zechariah saw the angel, he was disturbed and overcome with fear.
1.13: But the angel said to him, " Zechariah, don't be afraid. Your prayer has been heard. Your wife, Elizabeth, will give birth to a son. You will name him John.
1.14: You will be very, very happy. Many people will rejoice because of his birth.
1.15: John will be a great man in the presence of the Lord God. He will never drink wine or liquor. Even at the time when he is being born, he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.
1.16: He will help many Jewish people turn back to the Lord their God.
1.17: John himself will go ahead of the Lord in a powerful way, like Elijah. He will have the same forceful spirit that Elijah had. He will make peace between fathers and their children. He will bring those people who are not obeying God back to the right way that people should think. He will make ready a people for the coming of the Lord. "
1.18: Zechariah said to the angel, " How can I be sure of this? I am an old man, and my wife is old too. "
1.19: The angel answered him, " I am Gabriel. I stand before God. God sent me to talk to you and to tell you this good news.
1.20: Now listen! You won't be able to talk until the day when these things occur. You will lose your speech because you didn't believe what I told you. Nevertheless, these things will come true in their proper time. "
1.21: Outside, the people were still waiting for Zechariah. They were surprised that he was staying so long inside the temple sanctuary.
1.22: Then he came outside, but he could not speak to them. Then the people realized that he had seen a vision inside the holy place. Zechariah couldn't speak; he could only make signs to the people.
1.23: When his time of service was over, he went home.
1.24: Later, Elizabeth, Zechariah's wife, became pregnant. So she didn't go out of her house for five months. She said,
1.25: " Look what the Lord God has done for me! My people were ashamed of me, but now the Lord God has taken that shame away. "
1.26: During Elizabeth's sixth month of pregnancy, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a virgin who lived in Nazareth, a town in the Galilee. The virgin girl was engaged to marry a man named Joseph from the family of David. Her name was Mary.
1.28: The angel came to her and said, " Greetings! The Lord God is with you. He has blessed you. "
1.29: But Mary was very disturbed about what the angel said. She wondered, " What does this mean? "
1.30: The angel said to her, " Don't be afraid, Mary, because God has blessed you.
1.31: Listen! You will become pregnant and give birth to a son. And you will name him Jesus.
1.32: He will be great. People will call him the Son of the Highest One. The Lord God will give him the authority of King David, his ancestor.
1.33: Jesus will rule over the people of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end. "
1.34: Mary said to the angel, " How will this happen? I have had no sexual relations with any man. "
1.35: The angel said to Mary, " The Holy Spirit will come upon you and the power of the Highest One will cover you. The holy baby will be called God's Son.
1.36: Now listen to this: you know that Elizabeth, your relative, is very old but she is already pregnant with a son. The woman who could not have a baby has been pregnant for six months!
1.38: Mary said, " I am the slave girl of the Lord God. Let what you said happen to me! " Then the angel went away.
1.39: Mary got up and went quickly to a town in the hill country of Judea.
1.40: She went into Zechariah's house and greeted Elizabeth.
1.41: When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the unborn baby kicked inside Elizabeth's body and she was filled with the Holy Spirit.
1.42: Then Elizabeth said with a loud voice, " Mary, you have been blessed more than any other woman. The baby to which you will give birth has also been blessed.
1.43: You are the mother of my Lord, and you have come to me! How could something this good happen to me?
1.44: When I heard your voice, the baby inside me jumped for joy.
1.45: You are blessed, because you believed that what the Lord God said to you would actually take place. "
1.46: Then Mary said, " My life praises the Lord God;
1.47: my heart is happy because God is my Savior.
1.48: Though I am not important, God has looked upon me, His slave girl. Listen! From now on, all generations will be happy for me
1.49: because the Powerful One has done great things for me! His name is holy.
1.50: God will always give His mercy to those who worship Him.
1.51: His arm is strong. He scatters those who are proud and boastful.
1.52: He pulls men down from their thrones and He raises up the humble.
1.53: He fills hungry people with good things, but He sends rich, selfish people away with nothing.
1.54: He has always helped His people who served Him. He always gave them His mercy.
1.55: It was just as God said to our ancestors, to Abraham and to his children forever. "
1.56: Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months; then Mary returned home.
1.57: When it was time for Elizabeth to give birth, she had a son.
1.58: Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord God had been very good to her. They rejoiced with her.
1.59: Eight days later they came to circumcise the child. They wanted to name him Zechariah because this was his father's name.
1.60: But his mother said, " No! He will be called John instead. "
1.61: The people said to Elizabeth, " But no one in your family is named John! "
1.62: Then they began to make signs to his father, asking, " What would you like to name him? "
1.63: Zechariah asked for something to write on. Then he wrote, " His name is John. " All of the people were surprised.
1.64: Then Zechariah could talk again. He began to praise God.
1.65: All of their neighbors became afraid. Throughout the hill country of Judea, people continued to talk about all these events.
1.66: All of the people who heard about these things wondered about them. They thought, " What will this little child become when he grows up? " The people could see that the Lord God's hand was with this child.
1.67: Then Zechariah, John's father, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He told them what was going to take place:
1.68: " Praise the Lord God of Israel. He watches over His people and He has given them freedom.
1.69: He has given us a powerful Savior from the family of David, His special Servant.
1.70: God's holy prophets who lived long ago said that He would do this.
1.71: He will save us from our enemies and from the power of all those who hate us.
1.72: God said that He would give mercy to our fathers and remember His holy promise.
1.73: God vowed to Abraham, our ancestor,
1.74: that He would rescue us from the control of our enemies so that we could serve Him without being afraid.
1.75: We will be holy and being made right before God as long as we live.
1.76: " Now you, little boy, will be called a prophet of the Highest One. You will go ahead of the Lord to make His ways ready.
1.77: You will make His people know that they can be saved, through the forgiveness of their sins.
1.78: With the loving mercy of our God, a new day from heaven will shine upon us.
1.79: God will help those people who don't understand, people who dread death. He will lead us in the way which goes toward peace. "
1.80: And so the little boy was growing up and becoming stronger in spirit. John lived in the desert, away from other people, until the time when he came out to preach to Israel.

2.1: About that time, Augustus Caesar sent out an order to everyone in the empire that everyone must register.
2.2: This was the first registration. It occurred while Quirinius was governor of Syria.
2.3: Each person traveled to be registered in the town where he was born.
2.4: So Joseph left Nazareth, a town in the Galilee. He went to the town of Bethlehem in Judea. This was known as David's town. Joseph went there because he was from the family of David — a direct descendant.
2.5: Joseph registered with Mary because she was engaged to marry him. ( Mary was expecting a child. )
2.6: While they were in Bethlehem, the time came for Mary to have the baby.
2.7: She gave birth to her first son and wrapped him with cloths. There were no rooms left in the inn. So she laid the baby in a box where cattle are fed.
2.8: Some shepherds were in the fields there, watching their flock of sheep that night.
2.9: An angel of the Lord God stood in front of the shepherds. The glory of the Lord shined around them. They were very frightened.
2.10: The angel said to them, " Don't be afraid, because I am telling you good news. It will make all the people very happy.
2.11: Today your Savior was born in David's hometown. He is Messiah, the Lord.
2.12: This is how you will know him: you will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a box where cattle are fed. "
2.13: Suddenly a very large group of angels from heaven joined the first angel. They were all praising God:
2.14: " Give glory to God in heaven, and on earth, let there be peace among those who please God. "
2.15: The angels left the shepherds and went back to heaven. The shepherds kept saying to each other, " Let us go to Bethlehem and see this event which has occurred which the Lord God has revealed to us. "
2.16: So the shepherds went quickly and found Mary and Joseph. The baby was lying in the feeding box.
2.17: The shepherds saw the baby. Then they revealed what the angels had said about this child.
2.18: Everyone was amazed when they heard what the shepherds told them.
2.19: Mary was keeping all these things in her heart; she continued to think about them.
2.20: The shepherds went back, singing to God and praising Him for everything they had seen and heard. It was just as the angel had told them.
2.21: When the baby was eight days old, he was circumcised. Then he was named Jesus. ( This name was given by the angel before the baby began to grow inside Mary's womb. )
2.22: The time came for Mary and the baby to be made pure, according to the law of Moses. Joseph and Mary brought Jesus to Jerusalem so that they could present him to the Lord God.
2.23: It is written in the law of the Lord: " When the first male in every family is born, he will be called 'holy for the Lord God. ' "
2.24: The law of the Lord also says that the people must give a sacrifice: " You must sacrifice two young doves or two young pigeons. "
2.25: A man named Simeon lived in Jerusalem. He was a good man and very devout. Simeon was waiting for the time when God would comfort Israel. The Holy Spirit was upon him.
2.26: The Holy Spirit had revealed to Simeon that Simeon would not die before he saw the Lord's Messiah.
2.27: The Spirit led Simeon to the temple. The parents of the child went to the temple to do what the Jewish law said that they must do about the child.
2.28: Simeon held the baby in his arms and thanked God:
2.29: " Now, Master, You can let me, Your slave, die in peace, just as You said.
2.30: I have seen Your Safety from danger with my own eyes.
2.31: You prepared him before all people everywhere.
2.32: He is light for all the people of the world to see and honor for Your people, Israel. "
2.33: Jesus' mother and Joseph were surprised at what Simeon said about him.
2.34: Then Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, the baby's mother, " Many Jewish people will fall and many will rise because of this boy. He will be a proof from God which some people will not accept.
2.35: The things which people think in secret will be revealed. The things which will happen will slice through your heart. "
2.36: Anna, a prophetess, was there at the temple. She was from the family of Phanuel in the Asher tribe. Anna was very old. She had lived with her husband for seven years after her marriage.
2.37: She was a widow and was 84 years old at that time. Anna was always at the temple; she never left. She worshipped God day and night by fasting and praying.
2.38: Anna came up to them at that same moment, thanking God. She began to talk about Jesus to everyone who was waiting for God to bring safety from danger to Jerusalem.
2.39: Joseph and Mary finished doing everything which the law of the Lord commanded. Then they returned home to Nazareth, their own town in the Galilee.
2.40: The little boy began to grow up. He became stronger and wiser. God's help in time of need was upon him.
2.41: Every year Jesus' parents traveled to Jerusalem for the Passover Festival.
2.42: When Jesus was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem to the feast as they always did.
2.43: When the feast days were over, they were returning home but the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. His parents didn't know about it.
2.44: Joseph and Mary traveled for a whole day. They thought that Jesus was with them in the caravan. They began to look for him among their relatives and close friends,
2.45: but Joseph and Mary didn't find Jesus. So they went back to Jerusalem to look for him there.
2.46: After three days, they found him. Jesus was sitting in the temple courtyard among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
2.47: Everyone heard him. They were amazed at his understanding and wise answers.
2.48: When Jesus' parents saw him, they were very surprised. His mother said to him, " Son, why did you treat us like this? Your father and I were very worried about you. We were looking everywhere for you. "
2.49: Jesus asked them, " Why did you have to look for me? You should have known that I must be where my Father's work is! "
2.50: But they did not understand the meaning of what he said to them.
2.51: Jesus went down with them and came to Nazareth. He always obeyed them. His mother was still thinking about all of these things.
2.52: Jesus grew taller and continued to learn more and more. People liked him, and he pleased God.

3.1: While John, Zechariah's son, was in the desert, the message of God came to him. This occurred during the 15th year of the rule of Tiberius Caesar. These men were ruling for Caesar: Pontius Pilate ruled Judea; Herod Antipas ruled the Galilee; Philip, Herod's brother, ruled Iturea and Trachonities; Lysanias ruled Abilene.
