Annas and Caiaphas were high priests at that time.
3.2: [ no verse]
3.3: John went through the whole area around the Jordan River. He was preaching to the people: " Change your hearts and be immersed for the forgiveness of sins. "
3.4: As the words in the book of Isaiah the prophet are written: " There is a voice shouting in the desert: 'Prepare the Lord's way. Make His paths straight.
3.5: Every valley will be filled and every mountain and hill will be flattened. Crooked roads will become straight and rough roads will become smooth.
3.6: Everyone will see the safety from danger of God! ' "
3.7: People were coming to be immersed by John. John said to them, " You are like poisonous snakes! Who told you to run away from God's punishment which is coming?
3.8: You must do the things which will show that you have really changed your hearts. Don't start thinking this to yourselves: 'Abraham is our father. ' I tell you, God could make children for Abraham from these rocks here.
3.9: The ax is now ready to cut down the trees. Every tree which does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire. "
3.10: The people asked John, " What should we do? "
3.11: John answered, " If you have two shirts, share with the person who doesn't have one. If you have food, share that too. "
3.12: Even the tax collectors came to John. They wanted to be immersed. They asked John, " Teacher, what should we do? "
3.13: John answered them, " Don't take more taxes from anyone than you have been ordered to take. "
3.14: The soldiers asked John, " What about us? What should we do? " John said to them, " Don't do violence to anyone; don't accuse falsely. Be happy with the pay you receive. "
3.15: All of the people were hoping for the Messiah to come, and they were wondering about John. They thought, " Perhaps he is the Messiah? "
3.16: John answered everyone, " I immerse you in water but there is one coming who is more important than I am. I am not worthy to untie his shoe. He will immerse you in the Holy Spirit and in fire.
3.17: He will come ready to clean the grain, separating the good grain from the straw. He will put the good part into his barn. Then he will burn the part which is not good. He will burn it with a fire which cannot be put out! "
3.18: John continued to preach the Good News, saying many different things to encourage the people.
3.19: ( Later John denounced Herod Antipas, the ruler, by saying, " You were wrong to marry Herodias. Herodias is your brother's wife! " John also rebuked Herod for the many other evil things which Herod had done.
3.20: Then Herod did another evil thing ( it was the worst thing of all ) — he put John in prison.
3.21: Before John was put in prison, many of the people were immersed by him. Then Jesus came and was immersed too. While Jesus was praying, the sky opened up.
3.22: The Holy Spirit came down upon him in a physical form, as a dove. Then a Voice came from heaven and said, " You are My Son, and I give Myself to you, for your good, expecting nothing in return. I am very pleased with you! "
3.23: Jesus was about 30 years old when he began to teach. People thought that Jesus was Joseph's son. Joseph was Eli's son;
3.24: Eli was Matthat's son; Matthat was Levi's son; Levi was Melchi's son; Melchi was Jannai's son; Jannai was Joseph's son;
3.25: Joseph was Mattathias' son; Mattathias was Amos' son; Amos was Nahum's son; Nahum was Esli's son; Esli was Naggai's son;
3.26: Naggai was Maath's son; Maath was Mattathias' son; Mattathias was Semein's son; Semein was Josech's son; Josech was Joda's son;
3.27: Joda was Joanan's son; Joanan was Rhesa's son; Rhesa was Zerubbabel's son; Zerubbabel was Shealtiel's son; Shealtiel was Neri's son;
3.28: Neri was Melchi's son; Melchi was Addi's son; Addi was Cosam's son; Cosam was Elmadam's son; Elmadam was Er's son;
3.29: Er was Joshua's son; Joshua was Eliezer's son; Eliezer was Jorim's son; Jorim was Matthat's son; Matthat was Levi's son;
3.30: Levi was Simeon's son; Simeon was Judah's son; Judah was Joseph's son; Joseph was Jonam's son; Jonam was Eliakim's son;
3.31: Eliakim was Melea's son; Melea was Menna's son; Menna was Mattatha's son; Mattatha was Nathan's son; Nathan was David's son;
3.32: David was Jesse's son; Jesse was Obed's son; Obed was Boaz' son; Boaz was Salmon's son; Salmon was Nahshon's son;
3.33: Nahshon was Amminadab's son; Amminadab was Admin's son; Admin was Arni's son; Arni was Hezron's son; Hezron was Perez' son; Perez was Judah's son;
3.34: Judah was Jacob's son; Jacob was Isaac's son; Isaac was Abraham's son; Abraham was Terah's son; Terah was Nahor's son;
3.35: Nahor was Serug's son; Serug was Reu's son; Reu was Peleg's son; Peleg was Eber's son; Eber was Shelah's son;
3.36: Shelah was Cainan's son; Cainan was Arphaxad's son; Arphaxad was Shem's son; Shem was Noah's son; Noah was Lamech's son;
3.37: Lamech was Methuselah's son; Methuselah was Enoch's son; Enoch was Jared's son; Jared was Mahalaleel's son; Mahalaleel was Cainan's son;
3.38: Cainan was Enos' son; Enos was Seth's son; Seth was Adam's son; Adam was God's son.

4.1: Jesus returned from the Jordan River. He was full of the Holy Spirit. The Spirit was leading Jesus into the wilderness.
4.2: The devil tempted Jesus for 40 days. Jesus didn't eat anything during that time. When those days were over, Jesus was very hungry.
4.3: The devil said to him, " Since you are the Son of God, command this rock to become food. "
4.4: Jesus answered him, " It is written: 'A person does not live on bread alone, but by every word of God. ' "
4.5: The devil took Jesus and showed him in a moment of time all of the kingdoms of the world.
4.6: The devil said to him, " I will give you all of these kingdoms and all the power and glory which is in them. It has all been given to me. I may give it to anyone I want.
4.7: It will all belong to you, if you will only bow down in front of me. "
4.8: Jesus answered him, " Get behind me, Satan! It is written: 'You must worship the Lord God. Serve only Him! ' "
4.9: The devil led Jesus to Jerusalem and stood him on a very high place of the temple. He said to Jesus, " Since you are the Son of God, jump off,
4.10: because it is written: 'God will command His angels to take care of you. '
4.11: It is also written: 'Their hands will catch you so that you won't hit your foot on a rock. ' "
4.12: Jesus answered him, " But it also says: 'You must not test the Lord your God. ' "
4.13: The devil finished tempting Jesus and went away from him to wait until a better time.
4.14: Jesus went back to the Galilee with the power of the Holy Spirit. Stories about Jesus went all over the area around the Galilee.
4.15: He began to teach in their houses of worship. All of the people were praising him.
4.16: Jesus came to Nazareth, the town where he grew up. On the Sabbath day he went into the house of worship; that is what Jesus always did. He stood up to read.
4.17: The book of Isaiah the prophet was given to him. Jesus opened the scroll and found the place where this was written:
4.18: " The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me. He chose me to tell the Good News to poor people. He sent me to preach freedom to captives and to help blind people see again. He sent me to lift up broken - hearted people
4.19: and to announce the welcome year of the Lord God. "
4.20: Jesus rolled up the scroll and gave it back to the keeper. Then Jesus sat down. Every person in the house of worship was watching Jesus very closely.
4.21: Jesus began to speak to them. He said, " While you heard me reading these words just now, the words were coming true! "
4.22: All of the people were saying good things about Jesus. They continued to be amazed at the beautiful words which were coming from his mouth. The people asked, " Isn't this Jesus, the son of Joseph? "
4.23: Jesus said to them, " Surely you will tell me this old saying: 'Doctor, heal yourself. ' You would like to say, 'We have heard about some of the things you did in Capernaum. Do those things here in your own hometown too! ' "
4.24: Then Jesus said, " I am telling you the truth: a prophet is not accepted in his own hometown.
4.25: " I am telling you the truth: during Elijah's time it did not rain in Israel for three and one half years. There was very little food anywhere in the whole country. There were many widows in Israel during that time
4.26: but Elijah was sent to none of those widows. He was sent only to a widow in Zarephath, a town in the land of Sidon.
4.27: " And there were many people with leprosy living in Israel during the time of the prophet Elisha. However, not one of those people was healed; the only one was Naaman. And Naaman was from the country of Syria, not from Israel. "
4.28: All the people in the house of worship heard these things. The people became very, very angry.
4.29: Their town was built on a hill. They got up and forced Jesus out of town, bringing Jesus to the edge of a cliff. They wanted to throw him over,
4.30: but Jesus walked through the middle of them and went away.
4.31: On the Sabbath day Jesus went down to Capernaum, a town in the Galilee. Jesus was teaching the people.
4.32: They were amazed at what he taught; this message had authority.
4.33: In the house of worship there was a man who had an evil spirit inside him. The man shouted with a loud voice,
4.34: " Bah! Jesus of Nazareth! What do you want with us? Did you come here to destroy us? I know who you are — God's Holy One! "
4.35: But Jesus stopped the evil spirit. Jesus said, " Stop talking and come out of the man! " The demon threw the man down on the ground in front of all the people. Then the evil spirit left the man without hurting him.
4.36: The people were shocked. They continued to ask each other, " What does this mean? With such authority and power Jesus commands evil spirits and they come out! "
4.37: And so the news about Jesus was spreading to every place in the whole area.
4.38: Jesus left the house of worship. He went into Simon's house. Simon's mother - in - law was very sick; she had a high fever. They asked Jesus to do something to help her.
4.39: Jesus stood very close to her and commanded the fever to leave her. It left her immediately and she got up and began to serve them.
4.40: When the sun went down, the people brought their sick friends to Jesus. They had many different kinds of sicknesses. He put his hands on every one of them and healed them.
4.41: Demons were coming out of many people, shouting, " You are the Son of God! " But Jesus wouldn't let the demons say anything more; the demons knew that Jesus was the Messiah.
4.42: The next day Jesus traveled to a place to be alone. The people were looking for Jesus. When they found him, they wouldn't let him leave.
4.43: But Jesus said to them, " I must tell the Good News about God's kingdom to other towns too. This is why I was sent. "
4.44: Then Jesus began to preach in the houses of worship of Judea.

5.1: Jesus stood beside Lake Gennesaret. Many people pushed to get all around him. They wanted to hear the message of God.
5.2: Jesus saw two boats at the shore of the lake. The fishermen were washing their nets.
5.3: Jesus climbed into the boat which belonged to Simon. He asked Simon to push away from the shore a little. Then Jesus sat down and, from the boat, continued to teach the people on the shore.
5.4: Jesus finished speaking. He said to Simon, " Take the boat into the deep water. If all of you will drop your nets into the water, you will catch some fish. "
5.5: Simon answered, " Teacher, we worked hard all night long trying to catch fish, but we caught nothing. But you say I should lower the nets into the water so I will do it. "
5.6: The fishermen dropped their nets into the water. They caught so many fish that their nets were beginning to rip.
5.7: They called to some friends in another boat to come and help them. The friends came and both boats were filled so full of fish that they were almost sinking.
5.8: The fishermen were shocked because of the large number of fish that they caught. When Simon Peter saw this, he fell down in front of Jesus and said, " Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man! "
5.10: Jacob and John, the sons of Zebedee, were amazed too. ( Jacob and John were partners with Simon. ) Jesus said to Simon, " Don't be afraid. From now on, you will catch people instead of fish! "
5.11: The men brought their boats to the shore. They left everything and followed Jesus.
5.12: Once, Jesus was in a town; there was a man who was covered with leprosy. When the man saw Jesus, he bowed down in front of Jesus and begged him, saying, " Lord, you can heal me if you want to. "
5.13: Jesus said, " I do want to heal you — be healed! " Then Jesus stretched out his hand and touched the man. The leprosy disappeared immediately.
5.14: Then Jesus said, " Don't tell anyone about what happened. Instead, go show yourself to the priest. Then offer a gift to God because you have been healed. This is what the law of Moses commands. This will prove to the priests that you are healed. "
5.15: But the news about Jesus was spreading more and more. Many people were coming to listen to him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
5.16: Often Jesus went away to other places to be alone so that he could pray.
5.17: One day Jesus was teaching the people. The Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there too. They had come from every village in the Galilee and from Judea and Jerusalem. The Lord God was giving Jesus the power to heal people.
5.18: There was a man who was paralyzed. Some men carried him on a small bed. The men were trying to bring him and put him down in front of Jesus
5.19: but there were so many people that the men couldn't find a way to get to Jesus. So the men went up on top of the roof. They lowered the crippled man on his small bed down through a hole in the roof into the room in front of Jesus.
5.20: Jesus saw that these men believed. He said to the sick man, " My son, your sins are forgiven! "
5.21: The teachers of the law and the Pharisees began to think to themselves, " Who is this man? He speaks such an evil thing! Only God can forgive sins! "
5.22: But Jesus knew what they were thinking. He answered them, " Why are you reasoning in your hearts?
5.23: Which is easier to say: 'Your sins are forgiven', or to say, 'Stand up and walk'?
5.24: I will prove to you that I have the authority to forgive sins on earth. " So Jesus said to the paralyzed man, " I tell you, stand up! Pick up your bed and go home! "
5.25: Immediately the man got up in front of all of them. He took his bed and went home, praising God.
5.26: All of the people were completely amazed. They began to praise God. They were filled with awe. They said, " Today we have seen amazing things! "
5.27: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector sitting at the tax office. His name was Levi. Jesus said to him, " Follow me! "
5.28: Levi got up, left everything, and started to follow Jesus.
5.29: Then Levi, in his own home, gave a big feast in honor of Jesus. At the table there were many tax collectors and some other people.
5.30: The Pharisees and those men who taught the law for the Pharisees began to complain to the students of Jesus, saying, " Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners? "
5.31: Jesus answered them, " Healthy people do not need a doctor but sick people do.
5.32: I have not come to ask people being made right to change their hearts; I have come to call sinners. "
5.33: They said to Jesus, " John's students often fast and pray, the same as the Pharisees, but your students are always eating and drinking! "
5.34: Jesus said to them, " Can the friends of a groom be sad while he is still with them?
5.35: However, the time will come when the groom will be taken away from them. Then his friends will fast during that time. "
5.36: Jesus told this example: " No one takes cloth off a new robe to cover a hole in an old robe. If he does, the new piece of cloth will shrink and tear and not match the old cloth.
5.37: No one puts new wine into old wine bags. If he does, the old wine bags will break open. The wine will spill out and the wine bags will be ruined.
5.38: Instead, new wine should be put inside new wine bags.
5.39: No one who drinks old wine wants new wine because he says, 'The old is better. ' "

6.1: Once on a Sabbath day, Jesus was passing through a field of grain. His students were picking some of the grain, rubbing it in their hands, and eating it.
6.2: Some of the Pharisees asked, " Why are you doing this? You are doing what is not right to do on the Sabbath day. "
6.3: Jesus answered them, " Do you remember reading about what David did when he and his men were hungry?
6.4: David went into the house of God. He took the holy loaves of bread and ate them. The law says that only the priests can eat them but David gave some to his men. "
6.5: Then Jesus said to the Pharisees, " I am Lord over the Sabbath day. "
6.6: On another Sabbath day, Jesus went into the house of worship to teach the people. A man with a crippled right hand was there.
6.7: The teachers of the law and the Pharisees were waiting to see whether Jesus would heal on the Sabbath day. They wanted to see Jesus do something wrong so that they could accuse him.
6.8: But Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said to the man with the crippled hand, " Arise and stand in the middle. " The man got up and stood there.
6.9: Then Jesus said to them, " I ask you, which is right on the Sabbath day — to do good or to do evil? Is it right to save a life or to destroy one? "
6.10: Jesus looked around at all of them and said to the man, " Stretch out your hand! " The man did this; his hand was restored.
6.11: The Pharisees and the teachers of the law became very, very angry. They started saying to each other, " What can we do to Jesus? "
6.12: At that time Jesus went out to a hillside to pray. He stayed there all night long praying to God.
6.13: When morning came, Jesus called his students and chose twelve of them and named them " delegates ". They were:
6.14: Simon ( Jesus named him Peter. ), Andrew ( Peter's brother ), Jacob, John, Philip, Bartholomew,
6.15: Matthew, Thomas, Jacob ( the son of Alphaeus ), Simon ( He was named The Revolutionary. )
6.16: Judas ( the son of Jacob ), Judas Iscariot ( the one who turned against Jesus ).
6.17: Jesus and the delegates came down from the hillside. Jesus stood on a level place. A large group of his students were there. Also there were many, many people from all around Judea, Jerusalem, and the seacoast cities of Tyre and Sidon.
6.18: They all came to listen to Jesus and to be healed of their diseases. Jesus healed those people who were troubled by evil spirits.
6.19: All of the people were trying to touch Jesus because power was coming out of him. Jesus healed them all!
6.20: Jesus looked up at his students and began to speak: " Poor people, be happy, because God's kingdom belongs to you!
6.21: You who are hungry now, be happy, because you will be satisfied. You who are crying now, be happy, because you will laugh.
6.22: Be happy when people hate you and are cruel to you. Be happy even when they pull away from you as being evil and throw you out because you are my friend.
6.23: At that time you should jump for joy, because you will have a great reward in heaven. Their ancestors treated the prophets the same way that these people treat you.
6.24: " Nevertheless it will be horrible for you, you rich and selfish people, because you've had your comfort.
6.25: It will be horrible for you, you people who are full now, because you will be hungry. It will be horrible for you people who are laughing now, because you will mourn and cry aloud.
6.26: How horrible it is when everyone says good things about you; their ancestors always did that to the false prophets!
6.27: " However, I say to you people who are listening to me, give yourselves to your enemies, for their good, expecting nothing in return. Do good to those who hate you.
6.28: Bless those people who curse you. Pray for those people who are cruel to you.
6.29: If a person hits you on one side of your face, offer the other side too. If someone takes away your robe, let him have your shirt too.
6.30: Give to every person who asks you. When a person takes something that belongs to you, don't ask for it back.
6.31: " Treat other people the way you want them to treat you.
6.32: If you give yourself, expecting something in return, to those who give themselves to you for their good, expecting something in return — then you are not any better than anyone else. Even tax collectors do the same thing!
6.33: If you do good only to those who do good to you, you are no better than anyone else. Even 'sinners' do that!
6.34: If you lend something to someone, always hoping to get something back, what good have you done? Even 'sinners' lend to other 'sinners' so that they may get the same amount back!
6.35: " So give yourself to your enemies, for their good, expecting nothing in return, do good to them, and lend to them without expecting anything in return. God is good, even to the people who are full of sin and who are not thankful. If you do these things, you will have a great reward. You will be sons of the Highest One.
6.36: " Give mercy as your heavenly Father gives mercy.
6.37: Don't pass judgment on other people, and you won't be judged. Do not condemn other people, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
6.38: Give to others, and it will be given to you. You will be given much. It will be poured into your hands, shaken, and pressed down — more than you can hold. It will be so much that it will spill over into your lap. The measure you use to measure will be used to measure back to you. "
6.39: Jesus gave them this example: " Can a blind man guide a blind man? Both of them will fall into a pit.
6.40: A student is not higher than his teacher. However, when the student has learned, he will be like his teacher.
6.41: " Why do you see the speck of dust which is in your brother's eye but do not notice the wooden pole which is in your own eye?
6.42: How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me take hat speck out of your eye, ' while you still have that pole in your own eye? Can't you see it? You hypocrite! First take the pole out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
6.43: " A good tree does not produce rotten fruit; neither does a rotten tree produce good fruit.
6.44: Each tree can be known by its fruit. Do people gather figs from thorny weeds? Do people get grapes from bushes?
6.45: A good man brings good out of the good treasure of his heart, but an evil man brings out evil from an evil treasure. A person speaks what flows out of his heart.
6.46: " Why do you call me, 'Lord! Lord! ' yet you do not obey what I say!
6.47: Everyone who comes to me and listens to my words and obeys them
6.48: is like a man building a house. He digs down deep and builds his house on strong rock. Then the floods come, and the water tries to wash the house away, but the flood cannot move the house because it was built well.
6.49: However, the person who hears my words and does not obey them is like a man who does not build his house on rock. There is no solid foundation. When the floods come, the house quickly falls down, and that house is completely destroyed. "

7.1: Jesus finished saying all these things to the people. Then he went into Capernaum.
7.2: The slave of a Roman army officer was very sick — near death. The officer honored him very much.
7.3: When the officer heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to him to ask Jesus to come and save the life of his slave.
7.4: When the men came to Jesus, they begged him earnestly, " This officer deserves to have your help.
7.5: He built the house of worship for us; he gives himself to our people, for their good, expecting nothing in return. "
7.6: So Jesus went with the men. He was coming near to the officer's house when the officer sent friends to say, " Lord, don't bother to come into my house. I am not worthy to be with you.
7.7: That is why I did not come to you myself. Just give the order and my slave will be healed.
7.8: I am a person under authority too, and I have soldiers below me whom I command. I can say to one, 'Go! ' and he goes. I can say to another, 'Come! ' and he comes. Or, if I say to my slave, 'Do this! ' he does it.
7.9: When Jesus heard this, he was surprised. Jesus turned to the crowd that was following him. He said, " I tell you, I have not found this much faith anywhere — not even in Israel! "
7.10: The group that was sent to Jesus went back to the house. They found that the slave was made well.
7.11: The next day Jesus went to a town called Nain. His students and a large group of people were traveling with him.
7.12: When Jesus came near the town gate, he saw a funeral procession. A mother had lost her only son. She was also a widow. A large crowd from the town was there with the mother while the dead son was being carried out.
7.13: When the Lord Jesus saw her, he felt very sorry for her. He said to her, " Don't cry. "
7.14: Jesus came near the coffin and touched it. The men who were carrying it stopped. Jesus said, " Young man, I tell you, get up! "
7.15: Then the dead son sat up and began to talk. Jesus gave him to his mother.
7.16: All of the people felt much respect. They were praising God. They said, " A great prophet has come to us! " and, " God is taking care of His people. "
7.17: This news about Jesus spread into all Judea and throughout all the places around there.
7.18: John's students told John about all of these things. He called for two of his students.
7.19: John sent them to the Lord Jesus to ask, " Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for someone else? "
7.20: So the men came to Jesus. They said, " John ( the one who immerses people ) sent us to you with this question: 'Are you the one who is coming, or should we wait for another person? ' "
7.21: At that time Jesus healed many people of their sicknesses, diseases, and evil spirits. He gave sight to many blind people.
7.22: Then Jesus said to John's students, " Go tell John the things you have seen and heard. Blind people can see again. Crippled people can walk. Those with leprosy are made well. The deaf can hear; dead people are given life; and the Good News is given to the poor people.
7.23: The person who is not ashamed of me is truly happy! "
7.24: After John's messengers left, Jesus began to tell the crowds about John: " What did you people go out into the wilderness to see? A stalk of grass being blown by the wind?
7.25: Why did you go out there? Did you go to see a man dressed in fine clothes? The people who have fine, nice clothes live in palaces.
7.26: Really, what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you — John is even more than a prophet.
7.27: This was written about John: 'Listen! I am sending my messenger to go ahead of you. He will prepare the way for you. '
7.28: " I tell you, John is greater than any man ever born. However, the person who is the least important in God's kingdom is greater than John! "
7.29: ( All of the people and the tax collectors who heard this agreed that God's command was good; they had allowed themselves to be immersed by John.
7.30: But the Pharisees and teachers of the law refused to obey God's plan; they did not allow themselves to be immersed by John. )
7.31: Then Jesus said, " Now I will compare the people of this time to something. What are they like?
7.32: The people of this time are like little children sitting in the marketplace, calling to each other, 'We played a happy song, but you wouldn't dance. We played a sad song, but you wouldn't cry. '
7.33: John ( the one who immersed people ) came, not eating normal food or drinking wine, and you say, 'He has a demon! '
7.34: I came eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look, he eats too much, and he drinks too much wine! He is the friend of tax collectors and other sinners! '
7.35: True wisdom is shown to be right by all the things it does. "
7.36: One of the Pharisees asked Jesus to eat with him. Jesus went into the Pharisee's house and sat down at the table.
7.37: At that time there was a sinful woman in town. She knew that Jesus was having dinner at the Pharisee's house; so the woman brought some expensive perfume.
7.38: She stood crying at Jesus' feet. Then she began to wash his feet with her tears and to dry them with her hair. She kissed his feet again and again and rubbed them with perfume.
7.39: The Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this. He thought to himself, " If Jesus really were a prophet, he would know that the woman who is touching him is a sinner! "
7.40: Then Jesus said to the Pharisee, " Simon, I have something to say to you. " Simon said, " Say it, teacher. "
7.41: Jesus said, " There were two men. Both men owed money to the same moneylender. One man owed him 500 silver coins. The other man owed him 50 silver coins.
7.42: The men didn't have any money to pay back the moneylender. So the moneylender told the men that they didn't have to pay him. Which one of them will want to give himself to the moneylender, for his good, expecting nothing more from him? "
7.43: Simon answered, " I think it would be the one who owed him the most money. " Jesus said to him, " You are correct. "
7.44: Then Jesus turned to the woman and said to Simon, " Do you see this woman? When I came into your house, you provided me with no water for my feet, but she washed my feet with her tears and dried them with her hair.
7.45: You didn't give me the kiss of friendship, but she has not stopped kissing my feet since I came in!
7.46: You did not rub my head with oil, but she rubbed my feet with perfume.
7.47: Because of her great giving to me, for my good, expecting nothing in return — I tell you, her many sins are forgiven. The person who has only a little need to be forgiven will only give himself a little to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, when he is forgiven. "
7.48: Then Jesus said to her, " Your sins are forgiven. "
7.49: The guests at the table began to think to themselves, " Who does Jesus think he is? How can he forgive sins? "
7.50: Jesus said to the woman, " Because you believed, you are forgiven. Go in peace. "

8.1: Later, Jesus was traveling through each town and village. He was preaching and telling the Good News about God's kingdom. The twelve delegates were with him.
8.2: There were also some women with him. Jesus had healed these women of evil spirits and sicknesses. One of the women was Mary from a town called Magdala. Seven demons had come out of her.
8.3: Also, there were: Joanna, the wife of Chuza ( Herod Antipas' business manager ), Suzanna, and other women. These women used their own money to help Jesus and his delegates.
8.4: Many people came together. People came to Jesus from every town. He gave the people this example:
8.5: " A farmer went out to plant his seed. While he was planting, some seeds fell along the road. People walked on the seeds, and the wild birds ate them up.
8.6: Some seeds fell on rocky soil. They began to grow, but they died because they did not have any water.
8.7: Some other seeds fell among thorny weeds. They grew, but the weeds choked them off later.
8.8: And some seeds fell on good soil. They grew and produced fruit a hundred times more. " After saying these things, Jesus called out, " The person who has an ear to hear with should use it. "
8.9: Jesus' students asked him, " What does this story mean? "
8.10: And Jesus said, " You have been chosen to know the secrets of the kingdom of God. However, these secrets are given to other people in stories so that 'They will see, but they won't understand! They will hear, but they won't understand! '
8.11: " This is what the story means — 'The seed is God's message.
8.12: Those along the road are the people who hear, but then the devil comes and takes away the message from their hearts so that those people cannot believe it and be saved.
8.13: The seeds which fell on rocky soil are like the people who hear the message and accept it gladly, but they do not have deep roots. They believe for a while but, in time, temptation comes and they turn away from God.
8.14: The seeds which fell among the thorny weeds are like the people who heard God's message, but they are gradually choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of life. They never produce fruit.
8.15: But the seeds which fell on good soil are like the people who, when they listen to the message with a good, honest heart, obey it and patiently produce fruit. '
8.16: " No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a basket or hides it underneath a bed. Instead, he puts the lamp on a table so that the people who come in will have enough light to see by.
8.17: Everything which is hidden will become clear. Every secret thing will be made known.
8.18: So be careful how you listen, because the person who has something will get more. But this will happen to the person who has almost nothing: even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him! "
8.19: Jesus' mother and brothers came to visit him. They could not get to him because there were so many people.
8.20: Someone told Jesus, " Your mother and your brothers are standing outside. They want to see you. "
8.21: Jesus answered them, " My mother and my brothers are those people who listen to God's message and obey it! "
8.22: One day Jesus and his students climbed into a boat. He said to them, " Let us go across the lake. " And so they sailed.
8.23: While they were sailing, Jesus was asleep. Then a big storm blew down on the lake. The boat began to fill with water. They were in danger.
8.24: The students went to Jesus and woke him. They said, " Master! Master! We are going to drown! " Jesus woke up and gave an order to the wind and the waves. Everything stopped; the lake became calm.
8.25: He asked his students, " Where is your faith? " The students were afraid and amazed. They asked each other, " What kind of man is this? Even wind and water obey him! "
8.26: Jesus and his students sailed across the lake from the Galilee. They reached the land where the Gerasene people lived.
8.27: When Jesus went ashore, a man from the town met him. This man was full of demons. For a long time he had worn no clothes. He was living in the tombs, not in a house.
8.28: He had often been taken, put in jail, and tied with chains and shackles, but the man would always break the bonds and the demon inside him would force him to go out to the desert places. Then Jesus commanded the evil spirit to come out of this man. The man fell before Jesus and shouted, " What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Please, don't punish me! "
8.30: Jesus asked him, " What is your name? " He said, " Legion " ( because many demons had gone into him ).
8.31: The demons begged Jesus not to order them into the bottomless pit.
8.32: On that hill there was a large herd of pigs feeding. The demons begged Jesus to allow them to go into the pigs; so Jesus let them.
8.33: Then the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. The herd ran down the steep hill into the lake and drowned.
8.34: Some men had been taking care of the pigs. When they saw what happened, they ran away. They told the story in the fields and in the town.
8.35: People went out to see what had occurred. They came to Jesus and found the man sitting there at Jesus' feet. The man had clothes on and he was in his right mind — the demons were gone. The people became afraid.
8.36: The men who saw these things happen told the other people all about how Jesus had healed the man with demons.
8.37: All the people of the surrounding Gerasene area asked Jesus to go away from them. They were all very frightened. So he climbed into a boat and went back to the Galilee.
8.38: The demon - free man begged to stay with Jesus. But Jesus sent the man away, saying,
8.39: " Go back home and tell what God did for you. " So the man went all over town telling what Jesus had done for him.
8.40: When Jesus returned to the Galilee, a crowd of people welcomed him. Everyone was waiting for him.
8.41: A man named Jairus came too. He was a ruler of the house of worship. He bowed down at Jesus' feet and kept begging him to come to his house.
8.42: Jairus had only one daughter. She was twelve years old, and she was dying. While Jesus was going to Jairus' house, the crowds were pressing in upon him.
8.43: There was a woman who had a sore which had been bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all of her money on doctors but no one was able to heal her.
8.44: She went behind Jesus and touched the tassel of his robe. At that moment her bleeding stopped.
8.45: Then Jesus asked, " Who touched me? " Everyone denied touching Jesus. Peter said, " Teacher, the people are all around you and they are pressing against you. "
8.46: But Jesus said, " Someone did touch me! I felt it when power left me. "
8.47: When the woman saw that she could not hide, she came forward trembling. She bowed down before Jesus. While all the people listened, she told why she touched Jesus and how she was healed immediately.
8.48: Jesus said to her, " Dear woman, you are made well because you believed. Go in peace. "
8.49: While Jesus was still speaking, someone came from the house of the worship ruler and said, " Your daughter has just died! Don't bother the Teacher anymore. "
8.50: When Jesus heard this, he said to Jairus, " Don't be afraid! Just believe and your daughter will be well again. "
8.51: Jesus came to the house. He allowed only Peter, John, Jacob, and the girl's father and mother to go with him. He did not allow anyone else inside.
8.52: Everyone was crying and showing great sadness because of the girl. But Jesus said, " Stop crying, because she is not dead; she is only sleeping! "
8.53: They laughed at Jesus because they knew that the girl was dead.
8.54: But Jesus took hold of her hand and called to her, " Little girl, get up! "
8.55: Her spirit came back into her and she stood up immediately. Jesus said, " Give her something to eat. "
8.56: The girl's parents were amazed. Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about what had occurred.

9.1: Jesus called the twelve delegates together. He gave them authority over all demons and power to heal sicknesses.
9.2: Jesus sent them to preach about God's kingdom and to heal sick people.
9.3: He said to them, " When you travel, don't carry a walking staff. Also, don't carry a bag, food, or money. Don't even bring an extra set of clothes.
9.4: When you go into a house, stay there until it is time to leave that town.
9.5: If the people there won't welcome you, go outside the town and shake off the dust from your feet. This will be a warning to them. "
9.6: So the delegates went out, traveling through each village. They told the Good News and healed people everywhere.
9.7: Herod Antipas, the ruler, heard about all these things which were happening. He was confused, because some people said, " John has come back to life! "
9.8: Others said, " Elijah has appeared! " And some others said, " One of the prophets from long ago has risen from death. "
9.9: Herod said, " I cut off John's head. So who is this man I hear such things about? " Herod kept trying to see Jesus.
9.10: The delegates came back. They told Jesus what they had done on their trip. Then Jesus took them away to a town called Bethsaida where they could be all alone.
9.11: But the crowds found out where Jesus had gone and they followed him. Jesus welcomed them and began to talk with them about God's kingdom. He healed the people who were sick.
9.12: Late in the afternoon the twelve delegates came to Jesus and said, " No one lives here. Send the people away. They need to find food and places to sleep in the farms and small towns around here. "
9.13: But Jesus said to them, " You give them something to eat. " They said, " We have only five loaves of bread and two fish. Do you want us to go buy some food for all these people? "
9.14: ( There were about 5, 000 men there. ) Jesus said to his students, " Have them sit down in groups of about 50. "
9.15: So the students did this and all the people sat down.
9.16: Then Jesus took the five loaves of bread and two fish. He looked up to heaven. Jesus thanked God for the food and divided it. Then he began giving the food to the students. The students gave it to the crowd.
9.17: Everyone ate and was satisfied. They gathered up all the pieces of food which were left over. They filled twelve large baskets with them.
9.18: One time when Jesus was all alone praying, his students came together. Jesus asked them, " Who do the crowds say that I am? "
9.19: The students answered, " Some people say you are John ( the one who immersed people ). Others say you are Elijah. And some people say you are one of the prophets from long ago who has come back to life. "
9.20: Then Jesus said to his students, " But who do you say I am? " Peter answered, " You are God's Messiah. "
9.21: Jesus warned them not to tell this to anyone. Then Jesus said,
9.22: " I must suffer many things. I will be rejected by the Jewish elders, the most important priests, and the teachers of the law. I will be killed. However, after three days I will be raised from death. "
9.23: Jesus kept saying to all of them, " If anyone wants to follow me, he must carry his cross every day. He must say no to himself, and follow me.
9.24: The person who wants to save his life will lose it, but every person who gives his life to others for me will save it.
9.25: What good is it if a person gets the whole world but loses or wrecks his own life?
9.26: If a person is ashamed of me or my words, then I will be ashamed of him when I come with my glory and the glory of my Father and the holy angels.
9.27: I am telling you the truth: there are some people standing here who will see the kingdom of God before they die! "
9.28: After saying these things, about eight days later, Jesus took Peter, Jacob, and John and went up on top of a mountain to pray.
9.29: While Jesus was praying, his appearance began to change. His clothes became as bright as a flash of lightning.
9.30: Suddenly, two men were talking with Jesus. They were Moses and Elijah.
9.31: Moses and Elijah were shining brightly too. They were talking with Jesus about his death which was about to be fulfilled in Jerusalem.
9.32: Peter and the others were deep in sleep but they woke up and saw the glory of Jesus. They also saw the two men who were standing with Jesus.
9.33: As Moses and Elijah were about to leave, Peter said, " Teacher, it is good that we are here. We will set up three holy tents — one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah. " ( Peter didn't know what he was saying. )
9.34: While Peter was saying these things, a cloud came all around them. Peter, Jacob, and John became afraid when the cloud covered them.
9.35: A Voice came from the cloud, saying, " This is My Son; he is My chosen one. Listen to what he says! "
9.36: When the Voice finished, only Jesus was there. Peter, Jacob, and John said nothing. At that time they told no one about what they had seen.
9.37: The next day they came down from the mountain. A large group of people met Jesus.
9.38: A man from the crowd cried out to Jesus, " Teacher, please come and look at my son. He is the only child I have.
9.39: An evil spirit gets hold of my son and suddenly he shouts. He loses control of himself and he foams at the mouth. It hurts him and it will almost never leave him.
9.40: I begged your students to make it leave him, but they were not able to do this. "
9.41: Jesus answered, " You people are a generation with no faith. You are disobedient. How long must I be with you and put up with you? " Then Jesus said to the man, " Bring your son here. "
9.42: While the boy was coming, the demon threw him on the ground. The boy lost control of himself. Jesus gave a command to the evil spirit and healed the boy. Then Jesus gave him back to his father.
9.43: All of the people were shocked at the great power of God. The people were still amazed about all of the things which Jesus was doing. Jesus said to his students,
9.44: " Remember these words: I am about to be handed over to some men. "
9.45: But the students did not know what Jesus meant. The meaning was hidden from them so that they couldn't understand it, but they were afraid to ask Jesus about what he had said.
9.46: The delegates began to have an argument about which one of them was the most important.
9.47: Jesus understood what the argument was about. He knew what was in their hearts. So he took a little child and stood the child beside him.
9.48: Then Jesus said to them, " The person who welcomes this little child in my name welcomes me. And when a person welcomes me, this person welcomes the One who sent me. The one who is the most humble among you is the most important person. "
9.49: John answered, " Teacher, we saw someone who was casting demons out by using your name. We kept telling him to stop because he is not one of your students as we are. "
9.50: Jesus said to him, " Don't stop him, because if someone is not against you — he is for you. "
9.51: The time was coming near when Jesus would leave and go back up to heaven. He traveled toward Jerusalem.
9.52: Jesus sent some men ahead of him. The men went into a village in Samaria to make everything ready for Jesus.
9.53: But the people there would not welcome him because he was heading toward Jerusalem.
9.54: Jacob and John, the students of Jesus, saw this. They asked, " Lord, do you want us to call fire down from heaven and burn up these people as Elijah did? "
9.55: But Jesus turned and reprimanded them. Jesus answered, " You don't know what kind of spirit that you have. The Son of Man did not come to destroy the souls of men, but to save them. "
9.56: They all went to another village.
9.57: As they were all traveling along the road, someone said to Jesus, " I will follow you wherever you go! "
9.58: Jesus said to him, " The foxes have holes to live in. The wild birds have nests. I have no place where I may rest my head. "
9.59: Jesus said to another man, " Follow me! " But the man answered, " Lord, let me first go and bury my father. "
9.60: But Jesus said to him, " Let the 'dead' bury their own dead! You must go and tell about the kingdom of God. "
9.61: Another man said, " I will follow you, Lord, but first let me go and say goodbye to my family. "
9.62: Jesus said, " If anyone begins to plow a field but then looks back, he is not qualified for the kingdom of God. "

10.1: After this, the Lord Jesus chose 72 more men. He sent the men out in pairs ahead of him into every town and place where he was planning to go.
10.2: Jesus said to them, " The harvest is great but there are not many workers. Pray that the Owner of the harvest will send more workers out into the harvest field.
10.3: So you may go now. But listen, I am sending you like lambs into a pack of wolves.
10.4: Don't carry a pack, a bag, or extra shoes. Don't stop to talk with people along the road.
10.5: Before you go into a house, say, 'Peace be to this home. '
10.6: If a peaceful man lives there, your blessing of peace will stay upon him. However, if he is not peaceful, then your blessing of peace will come back upon you.
10.7: Stay in the peaceful house. Eat and drink what the people there give you. A worker should be given his pay. Don't move from that house to stay in another house.
10.8: If you go into a town and the people welcome you, eat what they give you.
10.9: " Heal the sick people who live there. Then tell them: 'The kingdom of God is very near to you! '
10.10: But if you go into a town and the people don't welcome you, then go out into the streets of that town and say:
10.11: 'Even the dust from your town which sticks to our feet we wipe off against you. But know this: the kingdom of God is very near! '
10.12: I tell you, on the Judgment Day, God will punish the people of that town more than He will punish the people of Sodom!
10.13: " How horrible it will be for you, O town of Chorazin! How horrible it will be for you, Bethsaida! Many miracles have occurred in you. If these same miracles had occurred in Tyre and Sidon, then those people in Tyre and Sidon would have changed their hearts and actions long ago.
10.14: But on the Judgment Day, God will punish you more than the people of Tyre and Sidon.
10.15: And you, Capernaum, do you think you will be lifted up to heaven? You will be thrown down to Hades!
10.16: When a person listens to what you say, he is really listening to me. When a person rejects you, I am the one he is rejecting. When a person rejects me, he is actually rejecting the One who sent me. "
10.17: When the 72 men returned, they were very happy. They said, " Lord, when we used your name, even the demons obeyed us! "
10.18: Jesus said to them, " I was watching Satan fall, as lightning falls from the sky.
10.19: Listen! I have given you the authority to walk on dangerous snakes and scorpions — even more power than the enemy has. Nothing will ever hurt you!
10.20: The evil spirits obey you. This is true, but don't be happy for that reason. Instead, be happy because your names are written in heaven. "
10.21: In that hour the Holy Spirit made Jesus rejoice. Jesus said, " Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I praise You because You have hidden these teachings from the 'wise' and 'intelligent' people, yet You reveal Your teachings to little children. Yes, Father, I praise You because this is what You really wanted to do.
10.22: " My Father has given me all things. Only the Father knows who the Son is. And only the Son knows who the Father is. The only people who will know about the Father are those whom the Son chooses to tell. "
10.23: Then Jesus turned to his students who were there alone with him. Jesus said, " You are very blessed to see what you now see!
10.24: I tell you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you now see. And many prophets and kings wanted to hear what you now hear but they didn't. "
10.25: Then a teacher of the law stood up. ( He was trying to test Jesus. ) He asked Jesus, " Teacher, what must I do to get eternal life? "
10.26: Jesus said to him, " What is written in the law? What do you read there? "
10.27: The man answered, " 'You must give yourself to the Lord your God, for His good, expecting nothing in return, with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind. ' Also, 'You must give yourself to your neighbor, for his good, expecting nothing in return, the same way you do to yourself. ' "
10.28: Jesus said to him, " You have answered correctly. Do this and you will have life forever. "
10.29: But the man wanted to make himself look good. So he said to Jesus, " But... who is my neighbor? "
10.30: Jesus understood what the man meant. So Jesus said, " A man was going down the road from Jerusalem to Jericho. Some bandits surrounded him. They tore off his clothes and beat him up. Then they left him lying there on the ground. He was almost dead.
10.31: By chance, a Jewish priest was going down that same road. When the priest saw the man, he just walked away.
10.32: Next, a Levite came to the spot too. The Levite saw him but he went around him; he also walked away.
10.33: A Samaritan man was traveling down the road. He came to the place where the man was lying. When he saw the man, he felt sorry for him.
10.34: The Samaritan went to him and poured olive oil and wine on his wounds. Then he bandaged the man's wounds. " The Samaritan had a donkey. He put the man on his donkey and took him to an inn where he took care of him.
10.35: The next day the Samaritan brought out two silver coins and gave them to the person who worked at the inn. The Samaritan said, 'Take care of this man. If you spend any more money on him than this, I'll pay you back when I return. ' "
10.36: Then Jesus said, " Which one of these three men do you think was a real neighbor to the one who was hurt by the thieves? "
10.37: The teacher of the law answered, " The one who showed mercy to him. " Jesus said to him, " Then you go and do the same thing! "
10.38: While Jesus and his students were traveling, Jesus went into a village. A woman named Martha welcomed him.
10.39: Martha had a sister named Mary. Mary was sitting at Jesus' feet and listening to his message but her sister Martha was doing the housework.
10.40: Martha became angry because she had so much work to do. She went in and said, " Lord, don't you care that my sister has left me alone to do all the housework? Tell her to help me! "
10.41: But the Lord answered her, " Martha, Martha, you are getting worried and upset about too many things.
10.42: Only one thing is important. Mary has made the right choice; and this will never be taken away from her. "

11.1: One time Jesus was somewhere praying. When he stopped, one of his students said to him, " John taught his students how to pray. Lord, please teach us how to pray too. "
11.2: Jesus said to them, " When you pray, pray like this: 'Our Father who is in heaven, may Your name always be kept holy. May Your kingdom come. May Your will be done in earth as in heaven.
11.3: Give us the food we need each day.
11.4: Forgive us of the sins we have committed because we, too, forgive everyone who has done wrong to us. And don't lead us into temptation, but rescue us from evil. ' "
11.5: Then Jesus said to them, " Suppose one of you went to your friend's house in the middle of the night and said to him, 'A friend of mine has come into town to visit me but I have nothing for him to eat. Please give me three loaves of bread. '
11.7: Your friend inside the house answers, 'Go away! Don't bother me! The door is already locked. My children and I are in bed. I cannot get up and give it to you. '
11.8: I tell you, perhaps friendship is not enough to make him get up to give you the bread. However, he will surely get up to give you what you need because you are not ashamed to continue asking.
11.9: So I tell you, continue asking and it will be given to you. Keep searching and you will find. Knock and the door will open for you.
11.10: You will receive if you will always ask. You will find if you keep looking. And the door will open for you if you continue knocking.
11.11: " Do any of you have a son? What would you do if your son asked you for a fish? Would any father give his son a snake? No, you would give him a fish.
11.12: Or if your son asks for an egg, would you give him a scorpion?
11.13: You are evil men, yet you know how to give good gifts to your children. Surely your heavenly Father knows how to give the Holy Spirit to those people who ask Him. "
11.14: One time Jesus was casting a demon out of a man who couldn't talk. When the demon came out, the man was able to speak. The crowds were amazed.
11.15: But some of the people said, " Jesus throws demons out by using the power of Beelzebub, the ruler of demons. "
11.16: Other people were trying to make Jesus prove that he came from God.
11.17: But Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said to them, " Every kingdom which is divided against itself will be ruined. And a family that does not work together will break apart.
11.18: So if Satan is fighting against himself, then he is divided. How could his kingdom stay together? You claim that I throw out demons by using the power of Beelzebub;
11.19: but if I cast out demons by using the power of Beelzebub, than by whose power do your own sons cast them out? Because of this, your own people prove you are wrong.
11.20: However, if it is true that I use the finger of God to cast out demons, then God's kingdom has come upon you!
11.21: " When a strong man guards his own house with many weapons, his house is safe.
11.22: But suppose a stronger man comes and defeats him. The stronger man will take away the weapons in which the first man had trusted to keep his house safe. Then the stronger man will keep the things he wants.
11.23: If a person is not with me, he is against me. The person, who does not work with me, scatters.
11.24: " When an evil spirit comes out of a man, it goes through dry places looking for a place to rest. If the spirit does not find a place, it says, 'I will go back to the house from which I came. '
11.25: And so it goes and finds that house cleaned up and orderly.
11.26: Then the evil spirit goes and brings seven other spirits worse than itself. They go into that man and live there. And that man has even more trouble than he had before. "
11.27: When Jesus said these things, a woman from the crowd spoke up, " Your mother, who gave birth to you and nursed you, must be very happy! "
11.28: But Jesus said, " The people who hear the message of God and keep it are the ones who are truly happy! "
11.29: The group of people grew larger and larger. Jesus said, " The people living today are evil. They ask for proof from God but no proof will be given to them except the Jonah miracle.
11.30: Jonah's coming was a warning to those people who lived in the city of Nineveh. It is the same with me. I am the warning to the people of this time.
11.31: " The Queen of Sheba will rise up on the Judgment Day with the men of this time and she will condemn them. Why? Because she came a very long way to listen to the wisdom of Solomon, yet I am greater than Solomon!
11.32: On the Judgment Day the men from the city of Nineveh will condemn the people of this time because when Jonah preached to them, they changed their hearts. I am greater than Jonah!
11.33: " No one puts a light under a basket and hides it. Instead, a person puts the light on the table so that everyone who comes in may see.
11.34: Your eye is like a lamp for the body. When your eye sees clearly, the whole body is made bright. However, if your eye is dark with sin, then your whole body is dark.
11.35: So be careful! Don't let the light in you become dark.
11.36: If your whole body is bright, and none of it is dark, then you will shine brightly as lightning does. "
11.37: While Jesus spoke, a Pharisee asked Jesus to eat with him. So Jesus came and sat at the table.
11.38: But the Pharisee was surprised when he saw that Jesus didn't wash his hands before the meal.
11.39: The Lord Jesus said to him, " You Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are greedy and full of evil.
11.40: You are foolish! The same One who made the outside of you also made the inside.
11.41: The next time you give to the poor people, give yourself ( heart ) too. Then you will be completely clean.
11.42: " But it will be horrible for you, you Pharisees! It is true that you give God ten percent of everything you have. You even give Him ten percent of all the little plants in your gardens — mint, rue, or other seasoning herbs, but you forget to give to Him, for His good, expecting nothing in return, and you forget to be fair to other people. You should always tithe, but you must remember to do the more important things too.
11.43: " It will be horrible for you, you Pharisees, because you give yourselves to things, to have the most important seats in the houses of worship. You give yourselves to feelings, to have the respect that people give you in the marketplaces.
11.44: It will be horrible for you because you are like hidden graves. People walk on them without knowing it. "
11.45: One of the teachers of the law said to Jesus, " Teacher, when you say these things about the Pharisees, you are insulting our group too. "
11.46: Jesus answered, " It will be horrible for you too, you teachers of the law! You put heavy loads on people which are hard for them to carry, but you yourselves don't even begin to help people carry those loads.
11.47: It will be horrible for you because you build tombs for the prophets, but these are the same prophets whom your ancestors killed!
11.48: And now you show everyone that you agree with what your fathers did. They killed the prophets, and you build tombs for the prophets!
11.49: " This is why the wisdom of God said, 'I will send prophets and delegates to them. Some of my prophets and delegates will be killed by evil men. Others will be hunted down. '
11.50: But you people will have to answer for the deaths of all the prophets who were killed since the beginning of the world.
11.51: You will have to answer for everything from the murder of Abel to the murder of Zechariah. ( Zechariah was killed between the altar and the temple. )
11.52: It will be horrible for you, you teachers of the law! You have hidden the key to learning about God. You yourselves would not learn and you also stopped others from learning. "
11.53: As Jesus was leaving, the teachers of the law and the Pharisees began to give him a lot of trouble. They asked Jesus questions about many things.
11.54: They hoped that Jesus would say something wrong. They were trying to trap him with something that he might say.

12.1: Many thousands of people came together. There were so many people that they were stepping on each other. Before Jesus began to speak to the people, he said to his students, " Be careful of the yeast of the Pharisees — they act as if they are good men, but they are not.
12.2: Everything which is hidden will be found out, and everything that is secret will be made known.
12.3: The things you say in the dark will be heard in the light. The things you whisper in secret rooms will be proclaimed from the tops of houses. "
12.4: " I tell you, my children, don't be afraid of people. People can kill the body but, after that, they can do nothing more to hurt you.
12.5: I will show you the One for whom to have awesome respect. You should have awesome respect for God who has authority over you to throw you into hell after you die. Yes, I tell you, He is the One you should have awesome respect for.
12.6: Five sparrows are sold for only a few small coins, but God doesn't forget about any of them.
12.7: Yes, God even knows how many hairs you have on your head. Don't be afraid. You are worth much more than many sparrows.
12.8: " I tell you, if anyone says he believes in me in front of other people, then I will speak for him in front of the angels of God.
12.9: But if anyone denies me in front of people, then I will deny him in front of the angels of God.
12.10: If a person says something against me, he may be forgiven. However, a person who says evil things against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
12.11: " When people bring you into the houses of worship before the leaders and other men with authority, don't worry about how you will answer their questions. Don't worry about what you will say.
12.12: At that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you must say. "
12.13: One of the men in the crowd said to Jesus, " Teacher, tell my brother to share my father's money with me! "
12.14: But Jesus said to him, " Sir, no one chose me to be a judge between you two. "
12.15: Then Jesus said to them, " Be careful and guard against all kinds of greed. A person's life is not measured by the things he owns. "
12.16: Then Jesus used this example: " There was a rich man who had some land which grew a very good crop.
12.17: The rich man was thinking to himself, 'What will I do? I have no place in which to keep all my crops. '
12.18: Then the rich man said, 'I know what I will do. I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones! I will put together all of my wheat and good things in my new barns.
12.19: Then I can say to myself, " I have many good things stored. I have saved enough for many years. Relax, eat, drink, celebrate! ". '
12.20: But God said to that man, 'Foolish man! Tonight you will die. So what about the things you prepared? Who will own those things now? '
12.21: " This is how it will be for the one who saves things only for himself. To God he is not rich. "
12.22: Jesus said to his students, " I say this to you because you shouldn't worry about what you will eat to stay alive. You shouldn't worry about what clothes you will wear.
12.23: You shouldn't worry, because life is more important than food. The body is more important than clothes.
12.24: " Notice the birds: they don't plant seeds or harvest them. Birds do not store their food in barns, yet God takes care of them. And you are worth so much more than birds.
12.25: None of you can grow a half meter taller by worrying about it.
12.26: If you cannot do a little thing like that, then why worry about the big things?
12.27: Notice how the wild flowers grow. They don't work or make clothes for themselves. But I tell you, even Solomon, with all his beautiful clothes, was not dressed as well as one of these flowers.
12.28: Why do you have so little faith? Look at how well God clothes the grass in the fields, but the grass is here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow to be burned. Wouldn't God dress you so much better? You are much more important than the grass in the fields. Don't have so little faith!
12.29: " So don't be wondering or worrying about what you will eat or what you will drink.
12.30: People without God put all these things first but your heavenly Father knows you need these things.
12.31: So put His kingdom first and all of the things you need will be given to you.
12.32: " Don't be afraid, little flock, your heavenly Father wants to give you the kingdom.
12.33: Sell the things you have and give that money to people who need it. Money does not last so don't trust in it. Let your riches be the treasure which is in heaven where it will never be stolen or destroyed.
12.34: The place where your treasure is will also be the place where your heart is.
12.35: " Be ready; be completely dressed and have your lights on.
12.36: Be like men who are waiting for their master to come home from a wedding party. The master comes and knocks. The slaves open the door for the master.
12.37: Those slaves will be blessed when their master comes home because he sees that his slaves are ready for him. I am telling you the truth: the master will dress for work and tell the slaves to sit at the table. Then the master will come and serve them.
12.38: Those slaves might have to wait all night long for their master, but they will be happy when their master comes in and finds them still waiting.
12.39: " Pay attention to this: suppose a man has a house. If the man knew the exact time a thief would come to rob him, the man would not allow the thief to break into his house.
12.40: So be ready! I will come at a time when you don't expect me! "
12.41: Peter said, " Lord, did you give this example for us or for everyone? "
12.42: The Lord Jesus said, " Well, who is the wise and trusted servant? Who is the servant whom the master can choose to take care of the master's family and the other servants, to give out the proper amount of food at the right time?
12.43: When the master comes and finds him doing the work he gave him, that slave will be very happy.
12.44: I am telling the truth: the master will choose him to take care of everything the master owns.
12.45: " But if that slave thinks that his master will not come back soon, then he will begin to beat the other slaves, both men and women. He will also eat too much and get drunk.
12.46: Then the master of that slave will come when he is not ready, at a time when he is not expecting the master. Then the master will punish him and send him away. This is what the master does to all of the slaves he cannot trust.
12.47: That slave knew what his master wanted him to do but he didn't try to do it. So he will be punished with a hard whipping!
12.48: What about the slave who didn't know what his master wanted? Although the slave did things which deserve punishment, he will get less punishment. Any person who has been given much will be responsible for much. Much more will be expected from the person who has been given more.
12.49: " I came to set the world on fire; I wish it were already burning!
12.50: I must be immersed with one more immersion; how hard pressed I feel until it is finished!
12.51: Do you think I came to bring peace to the world? No! I came to divide the world!
12.52: From now on a family with five people will be divided, three against two, and two against three.
12.53: A father and son will be divided: the son will be against his father; the father will be against his son. A mother and her daughter will be divided: the daughter will be against her mother; the mother will be against her daughter. A mother - in - law and her daughter - in - law will be divided: the daughter - in - law will be against her mother - in - law; the mother - in - law will be against her daughter - in - law. "
12.54: Then Jesus said to the crowds, " When you see clouds in the west growing bigger, immediately you say, 'A rainstorm is coming. ' And soon it starts to rain.
12.55: When you feel the wind begin to blow from the south, you say, 'It will be a hot day. ' And it happens.
12.56: You hypocrites! You can understand the weather but you don't know the importance of what is happening now.
12.57: Can't you decide for yourselves what is right?
12.58: " When a person is suing you, and you are going with him to court, try hard to settle it on the way to court. If you don't, then he may take you to the judge, and the judge will throw you in jail.
12.59: And you will never get out of there until they have taken everything you have. "

13.1: At that time some people came to Jesus. They told Jesus about what had happened to some people from the Galilee: Pilate had killed those people while they were worshipping, mixing their own blood with the blood of the animals that they were sacrificing.
13.2: Jesus answered, " Do you think this happened to those Galileans because they were more sinful than all others from the Galilee?
13.3: No, they were not! However, I am telling you, if all of you don't change your hearts, then you will be destroyed as they were!
13.4: What about those 18 people who died when the tower of Siloam fell on them? Do you think those people were more sinful than all others who live in Jerusalem?
13.5: They were not! But I tell you, if all of you don't change your hearts, then you will be destroyed too! "
13.6: Jesus gave this example: " A man had a fig tree. He planted the tree in his field. The man came looking for some fruit on the tree but he found none.
13.7: So the man said to his servant who took care of the field, 'Listen, I have been looking for fruit on this fig tree for three years but I never find any. Chop it down! Why should it waste the ground? '
13.8: But the servant answered, 'Master, let the tree have one more year to produce fruit. Let me dig up the dirt around it and put on some fertilizer.
13.9: Perhaps the tree will yield fruit next year. If it still does not produce, then you can chop it down. ' "
13.10: Jesus was teaching in one of the houses of worship on the Sabbath day.
13.11: In that house of worship there was a woman who had a spirit that made her sick for 18 years. Her back was always bent; she couldn't stand up straight.
13.12: When Jesus saw her, he called to her, " Woman, your sickness has left you! "
13.13: Jesus put his hands on her. Immediately she was able to stand upright. She began to praise God.
13.14: The house of worship leader was angry because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath day. The leader began to say to the crowds, " There are six days for work, so come to be healed on one of those days. Do not come for healing on the Sabbath day! "
13.15: The Lord Jesus answered, " You hypocrites! All of you untie your ox or your donkey from the stall and lead them to drink water every day — even on the Sabbath day!
13.16: This woman whom I healed is our Jewish sister but Satan has held her for 18 years. Why can't she be untied from her sickness on the Sabbath day? "
13.17: When Jesus said this, all the people who were opposing him felt ashamed of themselves. The whole crowd was happy. They were thanking God for the wonderful things Jesus was doing.
13.18: Then Jesus said, " What is God's kingdom like? With what can I compare it?
13.19: God's kingdom is like the seed of the mustard plant. A person plants this seed in his garden. The seed grows and becomes a large tree. The wild birds build nests among its branches. "
13.20: Again Jesus said, " With what can I compare God's kingdom?
13.21: It is like yeast which a woman puts into a tub of flour to make the bread rise. "
13.22: Jesus was teaching in every town and village. He continued to travel toward Jerusalem.
13.23: Someone asked Jesus, " Lord, how many people will be saved? Only a few? " Jesus said,
13.24: " Try hard to get through the narrow door! I tell you, many people will try to get in, but most of them won't be strong enough to enter.
13.25: If a man locks the door of his house, then you can stand outside and knock on the door but he won't open it. You can say, 'Master! Open the door for us! ' But the man will answer, 'I don't know where you come from! '
13.26: Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank with you. You taught in the streets of our town. '
13.27: Then he will say to you, 'Where do you come from? I don't know you. Go away from me! All of you are troublemakers! '
13.28: You will see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all of the prophets in God's kingdom, but you won't be allowed to come in. Then you will scream and grind your teeth.
13.29: People will come from the east, west, north, and south. They will sit down at the table in the kingdom of God.
13.30: Those who seem as though they are not important now will be important at that time. Those who seem important now will not be important then. "
13.31: At that time some Pharisees came to Jesus and said, " Go away from here and hide! Herod Antipas wants to kill you! "
13.32: Jesus said to them, " Go tell that fox: 'Listen, today and tomorrow I am throwing out demons and finishing my work of healing. Then the next day the work will be finished.
13.33: I must keep going today, tomorrow, and the next day for all prophets should die in Jerusalem. '
13.34: " O Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You killed the prophets. God sent you His men but you stoned them to death. I have often wanted to gather up your people like a hen gathers her baby chicks under her wings, but you wouldn't let me.
13.35: Listen! Your house is completely empty. I tell you, you will never see me again until you say, 'Praise be to the one who is coming with the authority of the Lord God. ' "

14.1: During a Sabbath day Jesus went to the home of an important Pharisee to eat with him. The Pharisees were all watching Jesus very closely.
14.2: A man had a swelling disease. He was put before Jesus.
14.3: Jesus asked the Pharisees and the teachers of the law, " Is it right or wrong to heal on the Sabbath day? "
14.4: But they kept quiet. So Jesus took the man and healed him. Then he sent the man away.
14.5: Jesus said to them, " If your son or ox falls into a well on the Sabbath day, you know that you would quickly pull him out. "
14.6: The Pharisees and teachers of the law were not able to say anything against what Jesus said.
14.7: Then Jesus noticed that some of the guests were choosing the best places to sit. So Jesus gave this example:
14.8: " When a person invites you to a wedding, don't sit in the most important seat. He may have invited someone more important than you.
14.9: If you do sit in the most important seat, then the one who invited you may come to you and say, 'Give this man your seat! ' Then you will start to move down to the last place. And you will be very embarrassed.
14.10: Instead, when a person invites you, go sit in the seat which is least important. The one who invited you will come to you and say, 'Friend, move up here to a more important seat! ' Then all of the other guests will respect you.
14.11: Every person who acts as if he is important will be made ashamed, but every person who truly humbles himself will be made important. "
14.12: Then Jesus said to the Pharisee who had invited him, " When you give a luncheon or a dinner, don't invite only your friends, brothers, relatives, and rich neighbors. They will just invite you back to eat with them. Then you will have your reward.
14.13: Instead, when you give a party, invite the poor people, the crippled, the lame, and the blind.
14.14: Then you will be happy because these people cannot pay you back. They have nothing. However, you will be rewarded when those being made right rise from death. "
14.15: One of the men at the table with Jesus heard these things. The man said to Jesus, " A person who eats bread in God's kingdom will be very happy! "
14.16: Jesus said to him, " A man was giving a big dinner. He invited many people.
14.17: When it was time to eat, the man sent his slave to tell the guests, saying, 'Come! Dinner is ready! '
14.18: But all the guests said they couldn't come. Each man gave an excuse. The first man said to him, 'I have just bought a field; I must go out and see it. Please excuse me. '
14.19: Another man said, 'I have just bought five pair of oxen; I must go and try them out. Please excuse me. '
14.20: A third man said, 'I have just gotten married; I can't come. '
14.21: " So the slave returned. He told his master what had happened. Then the master became angry and said, 'Hurry! Go into the streets and alleys of the town. Bring me the poor people, the crippled, the blind, and the lame. '
14.22: Later, the slave said to him, 'Master, I did what you told me to do, but we still have room for more people! '
14.23: The master said to the slave, 'Go out to the highways and country roads. Make them come. I want my house to be full!
14.24: I tell you, none of those men I invited first will ever eat with me! ' "
14.25: Many people were traveling with Jesus. He turned around and said to them,
14.26: " If someone comes to me, yet that person prefers his father, mother, wife, children, brothers, or sisters more than he prefers me, he cannot be my student. A person must prefer me more than he prefers himself!
14.27: The person who does not carry his own cross cannot be my student.
14.28: " If you wanted to build a building, you would sit down first and add up how much it would cost to see if you had enough money to finish the job.
14.29: If you didn't do that, you might begin the work but you wouldn't be able to finish it. Then all of the people watching you would laugh at you.
14.30: They would say, 'This man began to build but he wasn't able to finish! '
14.31: " If a king is going to fight against another king, first he will sit down and plan. If the king has only 10, 000 men, he will see if he is able to defeat the other king who is opposing him with 20, 000 men.
14.32: If he cannot defeat the other king, then he will send a group of men to ask for terms of peace from the other king while he is far away.
14.33: In the same way all of you must first count the cost. You must give up everything you have for me. If you don't, you cannot be my student!
14.34: " Salt is a good thing but if the salt loses its salty taste, then it is no good. You cannot make it salty again.
14.35: You can't even use it for dirt or fertilizer. People just throw it away. The person who has ears to hear with should use them! "

15.1: Tax collectors and " sinners " all came near to listen to Jesus.
15.2: Then the Pharisees and the teachers of the law began to complain, " This man welcomes sinners! He even eats with them! "
15.3: Then Jesus gave them this example:
15.4: " Suppose a man has 100 sheep but he loses one of them. He will leave the other ## sheep in the open country, and go out and look for the lost one. The man will continue to search for the lost sheep until he finds it.
15.5: And when he finds the sheep, the man is very happy. The man carries it home on his shoulders.
