15.6: He goes to his friends and neighbors and says to them, 'Rejoice with me because I found my lost sheep! '
15.7: I tell you, there is much joy in heaven when one sinner changes his heart. There is more joy for that one sinner than there is for ## good people who don't need to change their hearts.
15.8: " Suppose a woman has ten silver coins but she loses one of them. The woman gets a light and sweeps the house. She will look carefully for the coin until she finds it.
15.9: And when she finds the lost coin, she will call her friends and neighbors and say to them, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found the coin which I lost! '
15.10: In the same way, I tell you, there will be joy before the angels of God when one sinner changes his heart. "
15.11: Then Jesus said, " A man had two sons.
15.12: The younger son said to his father, 'Father, give me my part of all our holdings! ' So the father divided the property with his two sons.
15.13: Not long afterward the younger son gathered up all that he had and left. He traveled far away to another country. There the son wasted his money like a fool;
15.14: he spent everything he had. Then the land became very dry and it did not rain. There was not enough food to eat anywhere in that country. He began to starve.
15.15: So he went and got a job with one of the important men of that country. The man sent him into the fields to feed pigs.
15.16: The boy was so hungry that he wanted to stuff himself with the food which the pigs were eating. No one was giving him anything.
15.17: " Finally, the boy realized that he had been very foolish. He thought, 'All of my father's hired servants have plenty of food; yet here I am about to die because I have nothing to eat.
15.18: I will get up and go to my father. I will say to him: " Father, I sinned against God and in front of you.
15.19: I'm not worthy to be called your son anymore. Treat me as one of your paid servants. " '
15.20: So the son got up and went to his father. " While the son was still a long way off, his father saw him coming. He felt sorry for his son. So the father ran to him. He hugged and kissed his son.
15.21: The son said, 'Father, I sinned against God and in front of you. I'm not worthy to be called your son anymore. '
15.22: But the father said to his slaves, 'Hurry! Bring the best robe and dress him. Put a ring on his finger and good shoes on his feet too.
15.23: Bring our fattened calf. We will kill it and have plenty to eat. Then we can have a party!
15.24: My son was dead, but now he is alive again. He was lost, but now he is found! ' So they began to celebrate.
15.25: " The older son was in the field. As he came closer to the house, he heard the sound of music and dancing.
15.26: So the older son called to one of the servant boys and asked, 'What does all this mean? '
15.27: The servant said, 'Your brother has come back. Your father killed the fattened calf for him to eat. Your father was happy because your brother came back home safely! '
15.28: The older son was angry and wouldn't go inside to join the party so his father went out to beg him to come in.
15.29: But the son said to his father, 'Look, I have served you like a slave for many years! I have obeyed every one of your commands but you never even killed a goat for me so that I could have a party with my friends.
15.30: But this other son of yours has wasted all of your money on whores. Then he comes home and you kill the fattened calf for him! '
15.31: " But the father said to him, 'Son, you are always with me. All that I have is yours.
15.32: We must be happy and celebrate, because your brother was dead but now he is alive. He was lost, but now he is found! ' "

16.1: Jesus said to his students, " Once there was a rich man who hired a manager to take care of his business. Later the rich man learned that his manager was cheating him.
16.2: So he called in the manager and said to him, 'I have heard some bad things about you. Give me a report of what you have done with my money. You're fired! '
16.3: Later, the manager thought to himself, 'What will I do? My master is taking my job away from me! I'm not strong enough to dig ditches, and I'm too proud to beg.
16.4: I know what I will do! I will do something so that, when I lose my job, other people will welcome me into their homes. ' " So the manager called in each person who owed the master some money. He said to the first one, 'How much do you owe my master? '
16.6: The man answered, 'I owe him 100 barrels of olive oil. ' The manager said to him, 'Here is your bill; hurry, sit down and change it to 50 barrels. '
16.7: Then the manager said to another man, 'How much do you owe my master? ' The man answered, 'I owe him 1, 000 bushels of wheat. ' Then the manager said to him, 'Here is your bill; change it to 800 bushels. '
16.8: The master learned about this later. The master thought the dishonest manager had done a shrewd thing. Worldly people use their knowledge about worldly things better than spiritual people do.
16.9: " I ask you, should you make friends for yourselves with dishonest money? When the money is all gone, can they welcome you into homes which last forever?
16.10: I tell you, if a person can be trusted with small things, he may also be trusted with big things. If a person is dishonest in little things, then he will be dishonest in big things too.
16.11: If you cannot be trusted with worldly money, no one will trust you with true wealth.
16.12: And if you cannot be trusted with the things which belong to someone else, then no one will give you things for yourself.
16.13: " No slave can serve two masters at the same time. The slave will give himself to one, for his good, expecting nothing in return, over the other. Or, he will be more loyal to one and look down on the other. You cannot be a slave for God and Money at the same time. "
16.14: The Pharisees were listening to all these things. They were criticizing Jesus, because they all loved money.
16.15: Jesus said to the Pharisees, " You make yourselves look good in front of people but God knows what is really in your hearts. The things which are very important to people are worthless to God.
16.16: " Until the time of John there was the law and the prophets. Since then, the Good News about the kingdom of God is being told. Everyone is trying hard to get into the kingdom of God.
16.17: Even the smallest part of the law cannot be changed. It would be easier for the world to pass away.
16.18: If a man divorces his wife and marries another woman, he is committing unlawful sexual intercourse. And the man who marries a divorced woman is also committing unlawful sexual intercourse. "
16.19: Jesus said, " There was a rich man who always dressed up in the finest clothes. He was so rich that he was able to feast and have a party every day.
16.20: There was also a beggar named Lazarus. His body was covered with sores. He was often put at the rich man's gate.
16.21: Lazarus only wanted to eat the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table. Instead, the dogs came and licked his sores!
16.22: " After a while, Lazarus died. The angels took Lazarus and placed him in the arms of Abraham. The rich man also died and was buried.
16.23: He was sent to Hades and was in much pain. The rich man saw Abraham far away with Lazarus in his arms.
16.24: He called out, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me! Send Lazarus to me so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. I am suffering in this fire! '
16.25: But Abraham said, 'My child, do you remember when you lived on earth? You had all the good things in life but all the bad things happened to Lazarus. Now he is comforted here and you are suffering.
16.26: Also there is a great canyon set up between you and us. No one can cross over to help you; and no one can come over here from there. '
16.27: " The rich man said, 'Then, father Abraham, please send Lazarus to my father's house on earth!
16.28: I have five brothers. Lazarus could warn my brothers so that they won't come to this place of pain. '
16.29: But Abraham said, 'They have Moses and the prophets to read; let them learn from that! '
16.30: But the rich man said, 'No, father Abraham! If only someone could come back to them from death, then they would change their hearts. '
16.31: But Abraham said to him, 'No! If your brothers won't listen to Moses and the prophets, then they wouldn't be persuaded by anyone who might come back from death! ' "

17.1: Jesus said to his students, " Things will surely occur which will cause people to sin, but it will be horrible for the person who causes this to happen.
17.2: If he causes one of these little ones to sin, it would be better for him to drown with a big rock tied to his neck.
17.3: " Be careful! If your brother sins, tell him he is wrong; but if he changes his heart, forgive him.
17.4: If your brother does something wrong to you seven times in one day, but each time he says that he is sorry, then you should forgive him. "
17.5: The delegates said to the Lord Jesus, " Give us more faith! "
17.6: The Lord said, " If your faith were the size of the seed of the mustard plant, then you would say to this mulberry tree, 'Dig yourself up and plant yourself in the sea! ' and the tree would obey you. "
17.7: " Suppose one of you has a slave who has been working in the field, plowing the ground or caring for the sheep. When the slave comes in, what would you say to him? Would you say, 'Hurry, come in! Sit down to eat! '?
17.8: No, you would say this to your slave: 'Prepare something for me to eat. Then get dressed up and serve me. When I finish eating and drinking, then you may eat. '
17.9: The slave does not get any special thanks for doing his job. He is only doing what his master told him to do.
17.10: It is the same with you too. When you do all of the things you are told to do, you should think: 'We are not good slaves; we have only done our duty and nothing more. ' "
17.11: Jesus was traveling to Jerusalem, going from the Galilee through Samaria.
17.12: He came into a village. Ten men met him there. These men did not come close to Jesus because they all had leprosy.
17.13: But the men shouted to Jesus, " Jesus! Teacher! Take pity on us! "
17.14: When Jesus saw the men, he said, " Go and show yourselves to the priests. " As the ten men were going to the priests, they were healed.
17.15: When one of the men saw that he had been healed, he went back to Jesus and praised God with a loud voice.
17.16: He bowed down at Jesus' feet and thanked Jesus. ( This man was a Samaritan. )
17.17: Jesus answered, " Ten men were healed; where are the other nine?
17.18: Is this Samaritan man the only one who came back to give glory to God? "
17.19: Then Jesus said to him, " Stand up! You may go. You were healed because you believed. "
17.20: Some of the Pharisees asked Jesus, " When will the kingdom of God come? " Jesus answered, " God's kingdom is not coming in such a way that you will be able to watch it.
17.21: People will not say, 'Look, God's kingdom is here! ' or, 'There it is! ' No, God's kingdom is inside of you. "
17.22: Then Jesus said to his students, " The time will come when you will want very much to re - live one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not be able to.
17.23: People will say to you, 'Look, there it is! ' or, 'Look, here it is! ' Stay where you are; don't go away and search. "
17.24: " I will come again. On the day when I come, I will shine as lightning flashes across the sky.
17.25: But first I must suffer many things and be rejected by the people of this time.
17.26: " When I come again, it will be the same as it was when Noah lived.
17.27: In the time of Noah, people were eating, drinking, getting married, and giving their daughters away in marriage — even on the day when Noah entered the ship. Then the flood came and killed everyone else.
17.28: " It will be just like it was in the time of Lot. Those people were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, and building houses.
17.29: The people were doing these things even on the day when Lot left Sodom. Then fire and sulfur rained down from the sky and killed them all.
17.30: " This is exactly how it will be when I come again.
17.31: On that day if a man is on his roof, he won't have time to go inside and get his things. If a man is in the field, he must not go back home.
17.33: The person who tries to save his life will lose it, but the person who gives his life to others will save it.
17.34: " I tell you, when I come again, there may be two men sleeping in one room: one man will be taken and the other man will be left.
17.35: There may be two women working together; one woman will be taken and the other will be left.
17.36: There will be two men in the field; the one will be taken and the other will be left. "
17.37: The students asked Jesus, " Where will this be, Lord? " Jesus answered, " People can always tell where a dead body is; they can see the vultures gathering. "

18.1: Then Jesus used this story to teach the students that they should always pray and never give up:
18.2: " Once there was a judge in a town. He didn't respect God. The judge didn't care what people thought about him, either.
18.3: In that same town there was a woman who was a widow. The woman was always coming to this judge and saying, 'There is a man who is trying to ruin me. Give me my rights! '
18.4: The judge didn't want to help the woman. However, after a long time the judge thought to himself, 'Even though I don't respect God, and I don't care what people think,
18.5: this woman is beginning to bother me. If I give her what she wants, then she will leave me alone. If I don't give her what she wants, she will keep coming back until I get sick! ' "
18.6: The Lord Jesus said, " Listen to what the bad judge said. "
18.7: " God's chosen people cry out to Him night and day. God will always give them what is right; He will not be slow to answer His people.
18.8: I am telling you, God will soon help His people! Nevertheless, when I come again, will I find people on earth who have faith in me?
18.9: There were some people who were sure that they were being made right on their own. They acted as if they were better than other people. " Jesus gave this example to teach:
18.10: " Once there was a Pharisee and a tax collector. They both went up into the temple courtyard one day to pray.
18.11: The Pharisee stood there alone. He was praying like this: 'O God, I thank you that I am not like other people. I am not like men who steal, cheat, commit unlawful sexual intercourse, or even like this tax collector.
18.12: I fast twice a week and I give ten percent of everything I make! '
18.13: The tax collector stood alone too. However, when he prayed, he wouldn't even look up to heaven. The tax collector felt very humble before God. He said, 'O God, have mercy on me. I am a sinner! '
18.14: I am telling you, when this man went back home, he had been made upright with God. The Pharisee was not right with God. Every person who acts as if he is important will be made ashamed, but every person who humbles himself will be made very important. "
18.15: Some people were bringing their small children to Jesus so that he could touch them. When his students saw this, they told the people not to do this.
18.16: But Jesus called the little children to him and said to his students, " Let the children come to me. Don't stop them because the kingdom of God belongs to people who are like these children.
18.17: I am telling you the truth: you must accept God's kingdom as a little child accepts things, or you will never enter it! "
18.18: A rich leader asked Jesus, " Good Teacher, what must I do to get eternal life? "
18.19: Jesus asked him, " Why did you call me 'good'? Only God is good!
18.20: But I will answer your question. You know the commands: 'You must not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. ', 'You must not commit murder. ', 'You must not steal. ', 'You must not lie. ', 'You must honor and obey your father and mother... ' "
18.21: But the leader said, " I have obeyed all these commands since I was a boy! "
18.22: When Jesus heard that, he said to the leader, " But there is still one more thing you need to do. Sell everything you have and distribute it to the poor people. Then you will have a treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me! "
18.23: But when the man heard this, he was very sad. ( The man was very rich and wanted to keep his money. )
18.24: When Jesus saw that the man was very sad, he said, " It will be so hard for people with a lot of money to enter the kingdom of God!
18.25: It would be easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God! "
18.26: When the people heard this, they asked, " Then who can be saved? "
18.27: Jesus answered, " God can do things which don't seem possible to men! "
18.28: Peter said, " Look, we have left everything we had and followed you! "
18.29: Jesus said, " I am telling you the truth: every person who has left his home, wife, brothers, parents, or children because of God's kingdom
18.30: will surely be rewarded many times in this time and, in the age to come, with eternal life. "
18.31: Then Jesus took the twelve delegates aside. He said to them, " Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem. Everything which God told the prophets to write about me will take place!
18.32: The Jewish people will turn against me and give me to the non - Jewish men. They will laugh at me and spit on me, and insult me.
18.33: They will beat me with whips and then kill me! But on the third day after my death, I will rise. "
18.34: The delegates tried to understand this but they could not; the meaning was hidden from them. They did not know what Jesus was talking about.
18.35: Jesus came near the city of Jericho. There was a blind man sitting beside the road. The man was begging people for money.
18.36: When this man heard the crowd coming down the road, he asked, " What's happening? "
18.37: The people told him, " Jesus, the one from Nazareth, is coming here. "
18.38: The blind man became excited and cried out, " Jesus! Son of David! Take pity on me! "
18.39: The people who were in front leading the group told the blind man to be quiet, but he shouted even louder, " Son of David! Take pity on me! "
18.40: Jesus stopped there and said, " Bring that man to me! " When the blind man came near, Jesus asked him,
18.41: " What do you want of me? " The blind man said, " Lord, heal me! Let me be able to see again. "
18.42: Jesus said to him, " See again! You are made well because you believed. "
18.43: Immediately the man was able to see again. He followed Jesus, giving glory to God. All of the people who saw this praised God for what had occurred.

19.1: Jesus was going through the city of Jericho.
19.2: In Jericho there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a very important, rich tax collector.
19.3: He wanted to see Jesus, but there were also many other people and Zacchaeus was too short to see over them.
19.4: So he ran ahead to a place where he knew Jesus would pass. Then he climbed a sycamore - fig tree so that he could see Jesus.
19.5: When Jesus came to that spot, he looked up. Jesus said to him, " Zacchaeus, hurry! Come down! I must stay at your house today! "
19.6: Then Zacchaeus came down quickly. He was so happy to have Jesus in his house.
19.7: All of the people saw this. They began to complain, saying, " Look at the type of person Jesus stays with. Zacchaeus is a sinner! "
19.8: Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord Jesus, " Lord, I am now giving half of my money to the poor. If I have cheated anyone, I am now paying him back four times more! "
19.9: Jesus said, " This man is a son of Abraham. Today, safety from danger has come to this house!
19.10: I came to find lost people and to save them. "
19.11: Jesus traveled closer to Jerusalem. Some of the people thought that God's kingdom would soon appear. Jesus knew that the people thought this so, while the people were listening to these things, he continued with a story:
19.12: " A very important man was preparing to go to a far away country to be made a king. After that the man planned to return home and rule.
19.13: So the man called ten of his slaves together. He gave a gold coin to each slave. The man said, 'Do business with this money until I come back. '
19.14: But the people in his kingdom hated the man, so the people sent a group of their own men to follow the man to the other country. There these men said, 'We don't want that man to rule over us! '
19.15: " However, he did become king. When he came home, he said, 'Call those slaves who have my money. I want to know how much more money they earned with it. '
19.16: The first slave came and said, 'Sir, I earned ten gold coins with the coin you gave me! '
19.17: The king said to the slave, 'Fine! You are a good slave. I see that I can trust you with small things. So now I will let you have authority over ten of my cities! '
19.18: The second slave said, 'Sir, with the one gold coin which belongs to you, I earned five coins! '
19.19: The king said to this slave, 'You may rule over five cities! '
19.20: Then the next slave came in. The slave said to the king, 'Sir, here is your gold coin. I hid it in a piece of cloth.
19.21: I was afraid of you; you are a hard man. You take money which you didn't earn and gather food you didn't even grow! '
19.22: Then the king said to the slave, 'You evil slave! I will use your own words to condemn you. You said that I am a hard man. You said I take money which I didn't earn and gather food I didn't even grow.
19.23: If this is true, then you should have put my money in the bank. Then after I came back, my money would have earned some interest. '
19.24: " The king said to the men who were watching, 'Take the gold coin away from this slave and give it to the slave who earned ten coins. '
19.25: The men said to the king, 'But, sir, that slave already has ten gold coins! '
19.26: The king said, 'The person who uses what he has will get more, but the person who doesn't use what he has will have everything taken away from him! '
19.27: " 'Now, where are my enemies? Where are the people who didn't want me to rule over them? Bring my enemies here and kill them. I will watch them die! ' "
19.28: After Jesus said these things, he continued traveling upward toward Jerusalem.
19.29: He came near to Bethphage and Bethany, villages close to the Hill of Olives. Jesus sent two of his students on ahead.
19.30: He said, " Go into that village over there. You will find a young donkey tied there that has not been ridden. Untie it and bring it to me here.
19.31: If someone asks you why you are taking the donkey, you will say, 'The Lord, its owner, needs it. ' "
19.32: The two students went into town. They found the donkey exactly as Jesus had told them.
19.33: The students untied the donkey, but its owners came out. They asked the students, " Why are you untying our donkey? "
19.34: Jesus' students answered, " The Lord, its owner, needs it. "
19.35: Then the students brought it to Jesus. They put some of their clothes on the donkey's back. Then they helped Jesus get on top of it.
19.36: While Jesus was riding along the road toward Jerusalem, the students were spreading their robes on the road in front of him.
19.37: Jesus was coming close to Jerusalem. He was already near the bottom of the Hill of Olives. The whole group of students were happy. They were very excited and they praised God for all the powerful things they had seen. They said,
19.38: " Give praise to this king who is coming with the authority of the Lord God! Let there be peace in heaven and glory to God! "
19.39: From the crowd some of the Pharisees said to Jesus, " Teacher, tell your students not to say such things! "
19.40: But Jesus answered, " I am telling you, these things must be said. If my students don't say them, then these very stones will shout! "
19.41: Jesus came near to Jerusalem and saw it. He began to cry over the city.
19.42: Jesus spoke to Jerusalem, " I wish you knew today what would bring you peace but it is hidden from your eyes!
19.43: A time is coming when your enemies will build a wall around you. Your enemies will hold you in on all sides.
19.44: They will completely destroy you and all of your children. Not one stone will remain on top of another. All this will happen because you didn't know the time when God came to save you. "
19.45: Jesus went into the temple courtyard. He began to throw out the people who were selling things there.
19.46: Jesus said, " It is written, 'My house will be a place for praying. ' But you have changed it into a hiding place for thieves! "
19.47: Every day, Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courtyard. The most important priests, the teachers of the law, and some of the leaders of the people were trying to kill Jesus,
19.48: but they didn't know how they could do it because all of the people were listening closely to Jesus. The people were very interested in what Jesus had to say.

20.1: One day Jesus was in the temple courtyard teaching the people. Jesus told them the Good News. The most important priests, teachers of the law, and Jewish elders came.
20.2: They said to Jesus, " Tell us! What sort of authority do you have to do these things? Who gave you this authority? "
20.3: Jesus answered, " I will also ask you a question. Tell me:
20.4: when John immersed people, did that authority come from God or from man? "
20.5: They all talked about this. They said to each other, " If we answer, 'From God', then Jesus will say, 'Then why didn't you believe John? '
20.6: But if we say, 'It was from man', then all of the people will stone us to death, because they believe John was a prophet. "
20.7: So they decided to give this answer: " We don't know where John's immersion came from. "
20.8: So Jesus said to them, " Then I won't tell you what sort of authority I have to do these things! "
20.9: Then Jesus began to give this example to the people: " A man planted a vineyard. He rented the land to some farmers. Then he went away on a trip for a long time.
20.10: At harvest time the man sent a slave to those farmers. They were supposed to give the owner of the land some of the grapes, but the farmers beat the slave and sent him away with nothing.
20.11: So the man sent a different slave. They also beat this slave. They showed no respect for him and sent the slave away with nothing.
20.12: The man sent a third slave to the farmers. The farmers wounded this slave and kicked him out.
20.13: The owner of the vineyard said, 'What will I do now? I will send my son, to whom I give myself. Perhaps the farmers will show respect for him! '
20.14: When the farmers saw the son, they began to think to themselves, 'This is the owner's son. If we kill him, then this field will be ours! '
20.15: So the farmers forced the son out of the field and killed him. " What do you think the owner of this field will do to those farmers?
20.16: He will come and destroy them! After that, he will give the field to some other farmers. " The people heard this story. They said, " No! May this never happen! "
20.17: But Jesus looked into their eyes and said, " Then what does this verse mean: 'The stone that the builders did not want became the cornerstone. '?
20.18: Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken. If that stone falls on you, it will crush you! "
20.19: The Jewish leaders heard this. They knew that this story was about them. They wanted to arrest Jesus right then but they were afraid of what the people would do to them if they did.
20.20: So the teachers and priests waited for the right time. They sent some men to Jesus and told them to act as if they were good men. They wanted to find something wrong with the words that Jesus said. ( If they found anything wrong, then they could hand Jesus over to the high priest and the governor to be punished. )
20.21: So the men asked Jesus, " Teacher, we know what you say and teach is right. You don't care how important or unimportant a person is. You always teach the truth about God's way.
20.22: Now tell us, is it right that we should pay taxes to Caesar or not? "
20.23: But Jesus knew that these men were trying to trick him. Jesus said to them,
20.24: " Show me a coin. Whose name and picture is on it? " They said, " Caesar's. "
20.25: Jesus said to them, " Then give to Caesar the things which are Caesar's. And give to God the things which belong to God. "
20.26: The men were amazed at his wise answer; they could say nothing. The men were not able to trick Jesus in front of the people.
20.27: Some Sadducees came to Jesus. ( Sadducees believe that no one will rise from death. ) They asked Jesus,
20.28: " Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if a married man dies and he did not have children, his brother must marry the widow. Then they will have children for the dead brother.
20.29: Now there were seven brothers. The first one got married, but died. He had no children.
20.30: Then the second brother also married her and he died. They also had no children. The same thing happened with all the other brothers.
20.32: The woman was the last to die.
20.33: All seven men had married her; so when this woman rises from death, whose wife will she be? "
20.34: Jesus answered the Sadducees, " During this age, people marry each other.
20.35: Some people will be declared worthy enough to be raised from death and live again after this life. However, in that life they will not marry or be given in marriage.
20.36: They cannot die anymore because they will be like angels. When they rise from death, they will be the children of God.
20.37: Moses clearly showed that people are raised from death. When Moses wrote about the burning bush, he said that the Lord is the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
20.38: This means that the Lord God is not a God of dead people; He is the God of people who are alive! To God, everyone is alive. "
20.39: Some of the teachers of the law said, " Teacher, your answer was very good. "
20.40: No one dared to ask him another question.
20.41: Then Jesus said to them, " How can they claim that the Messiah is the son of David?
20.42: In the book of Psalms, David himself says: 'The Lord God said to my Lord: " Sit at my right side
20.43: until I put your enemies under your feet. " '
20.44: Therefore, David is calling the Messiah 'Lord'. So how can the Messiah be the son of David? "
20.45: While all of the people were listening to Jesus, he said to his students,
20.46: " Watch out for the teachers of the law. They want to walk around wearing clothes which make them look important. They like the greetings of respect which people give them in the marketplaces. They always want the most important seats in the houses of worship and the best seats at the dinners,
20.47: but they cheat widows and steal their homes. Then they make themselves look good by saying long prayers. Because of all this, God will punish these men so much more. "

21.1: As Jesus looked up, he saw some rich people putting their gifts for God into the temple money box.
21.2: Then Jesus saw a widow who was very poor. She put two small coins into the box.
21.3: Jesus said, " I am telling you the truth: this poor widow has given more than all those rich people.
21.4: The rich people have plenty; they only gave what they didn't need, but this woman gave everything she had. She needed that money to live on. "
21.5: Some of the students were talking about the temple. They said, " This is a beautiful temple. It has the best stones. Look at the many good gifts which have been offered to God! " But Jesus said,
21.6: " The time will come when everything you see here will be destroyed. Not one stone will stay on top of another. This will be completely destroyed! "
21.7: Some students asked Jesus, " Teacher, when will these things occur? How will we know when it is the time for these things to happen? "
21.8: Jesus said, " Be careful! Don't be fooled. Many people will come to you using my name. They will say, 'I am the one! ' and, 'The right time has come near! ' But don't believe them.
21.9: When you hear about wars and riots, don't be afraid. These things must happen first. The end will come later. "
21.10: Then Jesus said to them, " One country will fight against another country. Kingdoms will fight against other kingdoms.
21.11: There will be great earthquakes, sicknesses, and other terrible things in many places. In some places there will be no food for the people. Great wonders and amazing proofs will come from heaven.
21.12: But before all of these things happen, men will arrest you and persecute you. They will hand you over to their house of worship courts and throw you in jail. Men will lead you to kings and governors because you are associated with my name.
21.13: " But this will give you an opportunity to tell about all of the things you have seen me do.
21.14: Don't worry about how you will answer them or what you will say.
21.15: I will give you the ability to speak well with much wisdom. None of your enemies will be able to show that you are wrong.
21.16: Even your parents, brothers, relatives, and friends will turn against you. They will have some of you put to death.
21.17: All people will hate you because of my name,
21.18: but not one hair on your head will be harmed.
21.19: By enduring all of these things, you will keep your souls.
21.20: " You will see armies all around Jerusalem. Then you will know that the time for the destruction of Jerusalem is very near.
21.21: At that time the ones in Judea should run away to the mountains. Those inside Jerusalem must leave quickly. If you are near the city, don't go in!
21.22: The prophets wrote many things about the time when God will punish His people. This is the time when all of these things must occur.
21.23: " At that time it will be horrible for pregnant women and nursing mothers because very hard times will come to this land. God will be angry with the Jewish people.
21.24: Some of the people will be killed by soldiers. Other people will be made prisoners and taken to every nation. The holy city of Jerusalem will be walked on by people of the world until their time is completed.
21.25: Amazing things will occur with the sun, moon, and stars. On earth, people without God will feel trapped. The oceans will be upset and the people will not know why.
21.26: Men will become so afraid that they will faint. They will be very worried about the things which will happen to the whole world. The powers in the universe will be moved.
21.27: Then people will see me coming on a cloud with power and great glory.
21.28: When these things begin to happen, don't be afraid. Stand straight and lift up your heads! The time is near when God will save you! "
21.29: Then Jesus gave them this story: " Look at all of the trees. The fig tree is a good example.
21.30: When you see it turning green, no one needs to tell you that summer is near.
21.31: In the same way you will see all of these amazing things occur. Then you will know that God's kingdom is coming very soon.
21.32: I am telling you the truth: all of these things will occur while the people of this time are still alive!
21.33: " The world will be destroyed, but my words will never be destroyed!
21.34: Be careful! Otherwise your hearts will become burdened with drinking, getting drunk, and the worries of this life. That day may come suddenly when you are not ready.
21.35: It will come as a surprise to all people who live on earth.
21.36: So be ready all the time. Pray that you will be strong enough to endure all of these things when they occur and to stand before me. "
21.37: During the day Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courtyard. At night he went out of the city and stayed all night on the Hill of Olives.
21.38: Every morning all of the people got up early to go listen to Jesus in the temple courtyard.

22.1: It was almost time for the Feast of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover Festival.
22.2: The most important priests and teachers of the law were trying to find a way to kill Jesus but they were afraid of the people.
22.3: One of Jesus' twelve delegates was named Judas Iscariot. Satan entered Judas.
22.4: He went off and talked with the most important priests and some of the soldiers who guarded the temple. Judas talked to them about a plan he had to hand Jesus over to them.
22.5: They were pleased. They agreed to give Judas some money.
22.6: Judas said, " Yes. " He waited for the best time to give Jesus to them — when there was no crowd around to see it.
22.7: The day came for the Passover Feast. This was the day when the priests sacrificed the Passover lambs.
22.8: Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, " Go and prepare the Passover meal for us to eat. "
22.9: Peter and John said to Jesus, " Where do you want us to prepare the meal? " Jesus said to them,
22.10: " Listen! After you go into Jerusalem, you will see a man carrying a jar of water. Follow him. He will go into a house. Go inside with him.
22.11: " Say this to the owner of that house: 'The Teacher asks that you please show us the room where the Teacher and his students may eat the Passover Feast. '
22.12: Then he will show you a large upstairs room. This room is ready. Prepare the Passover meal there. "
22.13: So Peter and John left. Everything happened just as Jesus had told them. Then they prepared the Passover meal.
22.14: The time came for them to eat the Passover meal. Jesus and the delegates were around the table.
22.15: Jesus said to them, " I wanted very much to eat this Passover meal with you before I die.
22.16: I tell you, I will never eat another Passover meal until it is given its true meaning in the kingdom of God. "
22.17: Then Jesus took a cup. He gave thanks to God for it. Then he said, " Take this cup and give it to everyone here.
22.18: I tell you, I will never drink from the fruit of the vine again until God's kingdom comes. "
22.19: Then Jesus took bread and gave thanks. He broke off some of the bread and gave it to them. Then he said, " This bread is my body which I am giving for you. Eat this to remember me. "
22.20: In the same way, after supper, Jesus took the cup and said, " This cup is God's new covenant in my blood which is being poured out for you. "
22.21: Jesus said, " Listen! One of you will turn against me. He is sitting with me at this table now!
22.22: I will do what God has planned, but how horrible it will be for the man who hands me over. "
22.23: Then the delegates began to ask each other, " Which one of us would do such a thing to Jesus? "
22.24: Later, the delegates began to argue about which one of them was the most important.
22.25: But Jesus said to them, " The kings of the nations rule over their people. Men who have authority over other people are called 'benefactors'.
22.26: But you must not think that way. The greatest person among you should be like the younger person. Leaders should be like servants.
22.27: Who is more important? A man who is sitting at the table or the one who is serving him? You may think it is the one sitting at the table but I am like a servant among you!
22.28: " You men have stayed with me through many struggles.
22.29: My Father has given me a kingdom. I also give you authority to rule with me.
22.30: In my kingdom you will eat and drink at my table. You will sit on thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel. "
22.31: " O Simon, Simon. Listen! Satan has asked to sift you like a farmer sifts his wheat.
22.32: I have prayed that you will not lose your faith! When you come back to me, help your brothers be stronger. "
22.33: But Peter said to Jesus, " Lord, I am ready to go to jail with you. I will even die with you! "
22.34: But Jesus said, " Peter, I tell you, before the rooster crows in the morning, you will say that you don't even know me three different times! "
22.35: Then Jesus said to the delegates, " I sent you to preach to the people without a bag, money, or extra shoes. Did you need anything? " The delegates said, " Nothing. "
22.36: Jesus said to them, " But now if you have a bag or money, carry that with you. If you don't have a sword, sell your robe and buy one.
22.37: The Scripture says: 'They classed him with the criminals. ' I tell you, this verse must come true; it was written about me, and it is being fulfilled now. "
22.38: They said, " Look, Lord, here are two swords! " He said to them, " That will be enough! "
22.39: Jesus went out of Jerusalem to the Hill of Olives. His students went with him. ( Jesus often went there. ) He said to his students, " Pray for strength against temptation. "
22.41: Then Jesus went about 45 meters away from them; He kneeled down and began to pray,
22.42: " Father, if it is in Your plan, then take this cup of suffering away from me. However, what You want is more important than what I want. "
22.43: Then an angel from heaven appeared. The angel was sent to help Jesus.
22.44: Jesus was full of deep concern; he struggled hard in prayer. Sweat dripped from his face to the ground as though he were bleeding.
22.45: When Jesus finished praying, he went to his students. They were asleep. ( Their sadness had made them very tired. )
22.46: He said to them, " Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray for strength against temptation. "
22.47: While Jesus was speaking, a crowd came. One of the twelve delegates was leading them. His name was Judas. He came near Jesus so that he could give him the kiss of friendship.
22.48: But Jesus said to him, " Judas, are you using the kiss of friendship to betray me? "
22.49: The delegates of Jesus were standing there too. They saw what was going to happen. They asked him, " Lord, shall we use our swords? "
22.50: And one of the students did use his sword. He cut off the right ear of the high priest's slave.
22.51: Jesus answered, " Stop! " Then Jesus touched the slave's ear and healed him.
22.52: A group came to arrest Jesus. They were the important Jewish priests, the Jewish elders, and the soldiers who guarded the temple. Jesus asked them, " Why did you come out here with swords and sticks? Do you think I am a criminal?
22.53: I was with you every day in the temple courtyard. Why didn't you try to arrest me there? But this is your time — the time when darkness rules. "
22.54: They arrested Jesus and took him away. They brought him into the high priest's house. Peter was following from a distance.
22.55: The soldiers started a fire in the middle of the yard and sat together. Peter sat with them.
22.56: Because of the light from the fire, a servant girl saw Peter sitting there. The girl looked closely at Peter's face. Then she said, " This man was also with Jesus! "
22.57: But Peter said that this was not true. He said, " Lady, I don't know him. "
22.58: After a little while, a different person saw Peter and said, " You are one of the men who follow Jesus too. " But Peter said, " Sir, I am not! "
22.59: About an hour later, another man kept insisting, " It is true! This man was with Jesus. He is from the Galilee! "
22.60: But Peter said, " Man, I don't know what you are talking about! " Immediately, while Peter was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
22.61: Then the Lord Jesus turned and looked into Peter's eyes. And Peter remembered what the Lord had said to him: " Before the rooster crows in the morning, you will say that you don't even know me three times. "
22.62: Then Peter went outside and cried bitterly.
22.63: Some men were guarding Jesus. This is the way they made fun of Jesus: they covered his eyes so that he couldn't see them. Then they hit him on the face and said, " Prophesy for us! Let God tell you which one of us hit you! "
22.65: The men were saying many terrible things to Jesus.
22.66: When morning came, the elders of the people, the most important priests, and the teachers of the law came together. They led Jesus away to the Jewish Council.
22.67: They said, " Since you are the Messiah, tell us that you are! " Jesus said to them, " If I were to tell you I am the Messiah, you would not believe me.
22.68: And if I ask you, you won't answer or let me go.
22.69: But I will sit at the right side of God's throne — from now on. "
22.70: They all asked, " Then you are the Son of God? " Jesus said to them, " Yes, I am. "
22.71: They said, " Why do we need witnesses now? We ourselves heard it from his own lips! "

23.1: Then the whole group stood up and led Jesus to Pilate.
23.2: They began to accuse Jesus. They said, " We caught this man telling things which were confusing our people. He says we should stop paying taxes to Caesar. He calls himself the Messiah, a king. "
23.3: Pilate asked Jesus, " Are you the King of the Jews? " Jesus answered, " Yes. "
23.4: Pilate said to the most important priests and to the crowds, " I find nothing wrong with this man. "
23.5: They said again and again, " But Jesus is making trouble with the people! He teaches all over Judea. He began in the Galilee and now he is here! "
23.6: Pilate heard this and asked if Jesus were from the Galilee.
23.7: Pilate learned that Jesus was under the authority of Herod Antipas. Herod was in Jerusalem at that time so Pilate sent Jesus to him.
23.8: When Herod saw Jesus, he was very glad. Herod had heard all about Jesus. For a long time, he had wanted to meet Jesus. Herod wanted to see a miracle. He was hoping that Jesus would work one.
23.9: Herod asked Jesus many questions but Jesus wouldn't answer him.
23.10: The important priests and teachers of the law stood there. They continued to accuse Jesus. They were very excited.
23.11: Then Herod and his soldiers laughed at Jesus. They made fun of him by dressing him in royal clothes. Then Herod sent Jesus back to Pilate.
23.12: In the past, Pilate and Herod had always been enemies, but on that day Herod and Pilate became friends.
23.13: Pilate called everyone together. He called the most important priests, the leaders, and the people.
23.14: He said to them, " You brought this man Jesus to me. You said he was making trouble among the people. But listen, I judged him before all of you. I found nothing wrong with him. Jesus is not guilty of the things you are saying against him.
23.15: Herod Antipas found nothing wrong with him either; he sent him back to us. Look, Jesus has done nothing wrong. He shouldn't be killed.
23.16: So after I give him some punishment, I will let him go free. "
23.17: Now he was required to release one to them at the feast.
23.18: But all of the people yelled, " Kill him! Set Barabbas free for us! "
23.19: ( Barabbas was a man who was thrown into prison because of a riot which took place in the city and for murder. )
23.20: Pilate really wanted to let Jesus go free; so Pilate appealed to them again.
23.21: But they yelled again, " Kill him! Nail him to a cross! "
23.22: A third time Pilate said to them, " Why? What crime has Jesus done? He is not guilty. I can find no reason to kill him. So I will set him free, after I give him a little punishment. "
23.23: But the people continued to yell. They demanded that Jesus be killed on a cross. Their yelling became so loud that
23.24: Pilate decided to give them what they wanted. The people wanted Barabbas to go free. ( Barabbas was the man who had been thrown into jail because of a riot. He was a murderer. ) Pilate let Barabbas go free, but Pilate gave them Jesus to be killed. This is what the people wanted.
23.26: The soldiers led Jesus away to be killed. At that same time there was a man coming into the city from the fields. His name was Simon. He was from the city of Cyrene. The soldiers forced him to carry Jesus' cross and to walk behind Jesus.
23.27: A very large crowd was following Jesus. Some of the women were crying and mourning for Jesus. They felt so sorry for him,
23.28: but Jesus turned and said to the women, " Women of Jerusalem, don't cry for me — cry for yourselves and also for your children!
23.29: Listen, the time is coming when people will say, 'Happy are the women who cannot have babies! Happy are the women who have never had children to care for. '
23.30: Then the people will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us! ' The people will say to the hills, 'Cover us! '
23.31: If people do things like this now when life is good, what will happen when bad times come? "
23.32: There were also two criminals led out with Jesus. Jesus and the two criminals were led to a place where they would be killed. The people called this place " The Skull ". There some men nailed Jesus to his cross. They also nailed the criminals to their crosses; Jesus' cross was between the crosses of the two criminals.
23.34: Jesus said, " Father, forgive these people. They don't know what they are doing. " The soldiers gambled to see who would get Jesus' clothes.
23.35: The people stood there watching. The Jewish leaders were laughing at Jesus. They said, " Since he is God's chosen one, the Messiah, let him save himself! He saved other people, didn't he? "
23.36: Even the soldiers made fun of him. They came to Jesus and offered him some sour wine.
23.37: The soldiers said, " If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself! "
23.38: At the top of the cross these words were written: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
23.39: One of the criminals who was hanging there began to say awful things to Jesus: " Aren't you the Messiah? Then save yourself! And save us too! "
23.40: But the other criminal stopped him. He said, " You should fear God! All of us are about to die!
23.41: You and I are guilty; we should be killed because we did wrong. But this man Jesus has done nothing wrong! "
23.42: Then he said to Jesus, " Jesus, Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom! "
23.43: Then Jesus said to him, " I am telling you the truth: today you will be with me in Paradise! "
23.44: It was about noon but the whole area became dark until three o'clock in the afternoon.
23.45: There was no sun! The curtain hanging between the holy place and the most holy place in the temple was torn down the middle.
23.46: Jesus shouted, " Father, I put my spirit into Your hands. " After Jesus said this, he died.
23.47: The Roman army officer saw what happened. He was giving glory to God, saying, " This man was truly made right! "
23.48: Many people had come out of the city to see this event. When the people saw it, they felt deep sorrow and left.
23.49: The people who were close friends of Jesus were there. There were some women who had followed Jesus from the Galilee also. They all stood far away from the cross to watch.
23.50: There was a man from Arimathea, a Judean town. His name was Joseph. He was a good, being made right man. He was looking for the kingdom of God. Joseph was a member of the Jewish Council but he did not vote when the priests decided to kill Jesus.
23.52: Joseph went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
23.53: So Joseph took the body down from the cross and wrapped it in a sheet. Then he put Jesus' body into a cave which was cut out of solid rock. This tomb had never been used before.
23.54: This was late on the Preparation day afternoon. The Passover was about to start.
23.55: The women who had come from the Galilee with Jesus followed Joseph. They saw the tomb. Inside they saw where the body of Jesus was placed.
23.56: Then the women left to prepare some sweet - smelling spices to put on Jesus' body. They rested on the Sabbath day, according to God's command.

24.1: Very early on the first day of the week, the women came to the tomb. They brought the sweet - smelling things they had prepared.
24.2: But the women found that the rock was rolled away from the tomb.
24.3: They went in but they didn't find the Lord Jesus' body.
24.4: While they were wondering about it, suddenly two angels stood beside them in shining clothes.
24.5: The women were frightened; they bowed their heads down to the ground. The two men said to the women, " Why are you looking here for a living person? This is a place for dead people!
24.6: Jesus is not here. He has risen from death! Do you remember what he said in the Galilee?
24.7: Jesus said that he must be handed over to evil men, be killed on a cross, and rise from death on the third day. "
24.8: Then the women remembered Jesus' words.
24.9: The women left the tomb and went to the eleven delegates and the other students. The women told them everything which had occurred at the tomb.
24.10: The women were: Mary of Magdala, Joanna, Mary, the mother of Jacob, and some other women. These women told the delegates everything that had happened
24.11: but the men didn't believe what the women said. It sounded crazy.
24.12: However, Peter got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down and looked in, but he only saw the grave clothes. Peter went off by himself, wondering what had taken place.
24.13: That same day, two of Jesus' students were going to a village named Emmaus. ( It was almost 11 kilometers from Jerusalem. )
24.14: They were talking about everything which had happened.
24.15: While they were discussing these things, Jesus himself came near and walked along with them.
24.16: ( But the two men were not allowed to recognize Jesus. )
24.17: Jesus walked with them for a while. Then he said, " What are these things you are talking about as you walk? " They stood still. Their faces looked very sad.
24.18: The one named Cleopas answered, " You must be the only man in Jerusalem who doesn't know what has just happened there! "
24.19: Jesus asked them, " What are you talking about? " The men said to him, " It is about Jesus, the one from Nazareth. He was a prophet from God to all the people. He said and did many powerful things.
24.20: Our leaders and important priests gave him away to be judged and killed. They nailed Jesus to a cross,
24.21: but we were hoping that Jesus was about to bring safety from danger to Israel. Besides all this, it has been three days since this happened.
24.22: And today some of our women told us some amazing things. Early this morning the women went to the tomb
24.23: but they didn't find Jesus' body there. They came and told us that, in a vision, they had seen two angels. The angels said that Jesus was alive!
24.24: Some of our group also went to the tomb. They found that it was just as the women had said, but none of us saw him. "
24.25: Then Jesus said to the two men, " You are foolish and slow to realize what is true. You should believe everything the prophets said:
24.26: the Messiah must suffer these things before he enters his glory. "
24.27: Then Jesus began to explain everything which had been written in the Scriptures about him. Jesus started with the books of Moses and then he talked about what the prophets had written about him.
24.28: They came near the village of Emmaus, their destination, and Jesus acted as though he didn't plan to stop there.
24.29: They begged him, " Stay with us. It is late; it is almost night. " So he went in to stay with them.
24.30: Jesus sat down with them and took some bread. He gave thanks for the food and broke off some of it. Then he gave it to them.
24.31: At that time the men were allowed to recognize Jesus. They saw who he really was, but he disappeared.
24.32: They said to each other, " While Jesus was talking to us on the road, it felt like a fire burning in us when he explained the true meaning of the Scriptures. "
24.33: During that same hour they got up and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the students of Jesus meeting together. The eleven delegates and those people who were with them said, " The Lord Jesus has actually come back to life! He appeared to Simon Peter. "
24.35: Then the two men gave a report about the things which had happened on the road. They talked about how they recognized Jesus when he broke off some of the bread.
24.36: While they were saying these things, Jesus himself stood among them. He said to them, " Peace to you. "
24.37: They began to be filled with fear. They were terrified. They thought they were seeing a ghost.
24.38: But Jesus asked, " Why are you disturbed? Why do you doubt what you see?
24.39: Look at my hands and my feet. It is really I! Touch me. You can see that I have a living body; a ghost doesn't have a body like this. "
24.40: After Jesus told them this, he showed them the holes in his hands and feet.
24.41: They were amazed and very, very happy to see that he was alive. They still couldn't believe it, so Jesus asked them, " Do you have any food here? "
24.42: They gave him a piece of cooked fish.
24.43: While they watched, Jesus took it and ate it.
24.44: Jesus said to them, " Do you remember when I was with you before? I said that everything written about me must come true — everything written in the law of Moses, the books of the prophets, and the Psalms. "
24.45: Then Jesus explained the Scriptures. He opened their minds so they could understand the things which had been written about him.
24.46: Then Jesus said to them, " It is written that the Messiah would be killed and come back to life on the third day.
24.47: You saw these things happen. You must go and tell all nations that their sins can be forgiven. Tell them that they must change their hearts. You must start from Jerusalem and preach these things with my authority.
24.49: Listen, I am sending my Father's promise upon you but you must stay in Jerusalem until you are clothed with that power from heaven. "
24.50: Jesus led them out of Jerusalem, almost to the town of Bethany. He raised his hands and blessed them.
24.51: While Jesus was blessing them, he was separated from them and carried up into heaven.
24.52: They worshipped him. Then they went back to Jerusalem. They were very happy.
24.53: They were always in the temple courtyard, praising God.

1.1: The Word was in the beginning, and the Word was with God, and the Word is the essence of God.
1.2: He was with God in the beginning.
1.3: Through him everything was made. Without him nothing which has happened would have happened.
1.4: He was the Source of life and that life was the light for people.
1.5: The same light shines in the darkness; the darkness never understood it!
1.6: There was a man sent from God. His name was John.
1.7: This man came to give proof about the light so that through him, everyone might believe.
1.8: John was not the light; he was sent to tell the truth about the light.
1.9: The true light was coming into the world to give light to every person.
1.10: He was in the world. The world was made through him, but the people of the world did not recognize him.
1.11: He came to what was his, but his own people would not accept him.
1.12: Yet he gave the right to become God's children to those who did accept him, to those who believe in his name.
1.13: They were born, not in a human way from the natural human desire of men, but born of God.
1.14: The Word became human and lived among us. We saw his glory, the glory of the Father's one and only son — who came from the Father, full of help in time of need and truth.
1.15: John was telling the truth about him. John cried out, " This is the man I talked about: 'The one, who is coming after me, has been ahead of me' — because he was alive before I was! "
1.16: We have all received one blessing after another from the fullness of his help in time of need.
1.17: Though the law was given through Moses, help in time of need and truth have come through Jesus Christ.
1.18: No human being has ever seen God. The divine son, who is in the arms of the Father, has made Him known.
1.19: This is the proof that John gave when the Jewish leaders from Jerusalem sent some priests and Levites to ask John this question: " Who are you? "
1.20: John did not refuse to answer; he spoke freely. He clearly said, " I am not the Messiah! "
1.21: They asked him, " Who are you? Are you Elijah? " John said, " No, I am not Elijah. " They asked, " Are you that Prophet? " John answered, " No. "
1.22: Then they asked him, " Who are you? We must give an answer to the men who sent us here. What do you say about yourself? "
1.23: John said, " I am 'a voice shouting in the desert: Prepare the Lord's highway', just as Isaiah the prophet said. "
1.24: ( They had been sent from the Pharisee group. )
1.25: They asked John, " If you are not the Messiah, Elijah, or that prophet, why are you immersing people? "
1.26: John answered them, " Yes, I immerse people in water, but there is another one who stands among you about whom you don't know.
1.27: He is the one who is preferred that comes after me. I am not worthy to untie his shoelace. "
1.28: This happened in the town of Bethany across the Jordan River where John was immersing people.
1.29: The next day, John saw Jesus coming toward him. He said, " Look, the Lamb of God who will take away the world's sin!
1.30: This is the one I was talking about: 'The man who is preferred that is coming after me has been ahead of me, because he was alive before I was. '
1.31: I didn't know him. Why did I come, immersing people in water? To show him to the people of Israel. "
1.32: This is the proof that John gave: " I saw the Spirit coming down like a dove from the sky, resting on him.
1.33: I didn't know him, but the One who sent me to immerse people in water said to me, 'When you see the Spirit coming down and staying upon someone, this is the one who immerses in the Holy Spirit. '
1.34: I have seen it! I am telling you the truth. He is the Son of God! "
1.35: Again on the next day, John stood there with two of his students.
1.36: He looked at Jesus walking by and said, " Look, the Lamb of God! "
1.37: When the two students heard John say this, they followed Jesus.
1.38: Jesus turned around and saw them following him. He said to them, " What do you want? " They asked him, " Where do you live, Rabbi? " ( This word means 'Teacher'. )
1.39: Jesus said to them, " Come and see. " So they went and saw where Jesus was staying. They spent the rest of the day with him. ( It was about 16: 00 hours. )
1.40: Andrew ( Simon Peter's brother ) was one of the two men who heard John and followed Jesus.
1.41: The first thing that Andrew did was to find his own brother, Simon. Andrew said to him, " We have found the Messiah! " ( This word means 'Christ'. )
1.42: Then Andrew led Peter to Jesus. When Jesus looked at Peter, he said, " You are Simon, John's son. You will be called Cephas. " ( Translated into Greek, this name means 'a stone'. )
1.43: The next day, Jesus decided to leave for the Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, " Follow me! "
1.44: Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town where Andrew and Peter came from.
1.45: Philip found Nathanael and told him, " We have found the one of whom Moses wrote in the law. The prophets wrote about him too! He is Jesus, the son of Joseph, from Nazareth. "
1.46: Nathanael said to him, " Is it possible for anything good to come from Nazareth? " Philip said to him, " Come and see for yourself! "
1.47: When Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, he said this about Nathanael: " Look, here is a real man of Israel! There is nothing false about him! "
1.48: Nathanael asked Jesus, " From where do you know me? " Jesus answered him, " Before Philip called you to come here, I saw you under that fig tree! "
1.49: And Nathanael answered Jesus, " Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the king of the people of Israel! "
1.50: Jesus said to him, " Do you believe because I told you that I saw you under a fig tree? You will see even greater things than this.
1.51: I am telling you the truth: you will all see heaven open and God's angels coming down and going up from me. "

2.1: On the third day in the town of Cana in the Galilee, there was a wedding. Jesus' mother was there.
2.2: Jesus and his students were invited to the wedding.
2.3: When the wine was gone, Jesus' mother said to him, " They have no more wine! "
2.4: Jesus asked her, " What do you want with me, woman? My time has not yet come. "
2.5: His mother said to the servants, " Do whatever he tells you. "
2.6: There were six stone water jars sitting there. ( Jewish people used them to make things ceremonially pure. ) Each water jar could hold about 75 to 115 liters.
2.7: Jesus said to them, " Fill the jars with water. " They filled the jars to the top.
2.8: Jesus said to the servants, " Now pour some of this and take it to the master of ceremonies. " They did it.
2.9: He didn't know from where it came, but the servants who had gotten the water knew. When the master of ceremonies tasted the water which had now been changed into wine, he called for the groom.
2.10: He said to the groom, " Everyone serves the good wine first and, when the people have had plenty to drink, he serves the cheaper wine. But you have reserved the good wine until now! "
2.11: This was the first miraculous sign which Jesus performed. It was in the town of Cana in the Galilee. Jesus revealed his glory and his students believed in him.
2.12: After this, Jesus, his mother, his brothers, and his students went down into the town of Capernaum. They stayed there for a few days.
2.13: The time for the Jewish Passover was near. Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
2.14: He found some men in the temple courtyard selling cattle, sheep, and pigeons. The money - exchangers were also sitting there.
2.15: Jesus made a whip from some ropes. He forced all of them to leave the courtyard — even the cattle and the sheep. He turned the money - exchangers' tables over and scattered their coins.
2.16: He said to the men who were selling pigeons, " Get those things out of here! Don't turn my Father's house into a place of business. "
2.17: His students remembered that this verse was in the Scriptures: " The fire which I feel for Your house burns within me! "
2.18: The Jewish leaders asked Jesus this question: " What proof do you give to show us that you have the authority to do these things? "
2.19: Jesus answered them, " Destroy this temple and I will raise it up in three days! "
2.20: Then the Jewish leaders said, " It took 46 years to build this temple — and you would build it again in three days? "
2.21: ( Jesus was talking about his own body.
2.22: After Jesus was raised from death, his students remembered that he used to say this. They then believed the Scriptures and what Jesus had said. )
2.23: While Jesus was in Jerusalem during the Passover Feast, many believed in his name because they saw the miraculous signs which he was doing.
2.24: Jesus was not committing himself to them. Jesus knew what people were like. He didn't need anyone to tell him about men; he always knew what was in man.

3.1: There was a man named Nicodemus. He was a Jewish leader, one of the Pharisees.
3.2: This man came to Jesus at night. Nicodemus said to him, " Rabbi, we know you are a teacher who has come from God. No one could do these miracles which you are performing if God were not with him. "
3.3: Jesus answered him, " I am telling you the truth: if a person is not born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God! "
3.4: Nicodemus asked him, " When a man is already old, how can he be reborn? It is not possible for him to go inside his mother's womb the second time and be born! "
3.5: Jesus answered, " I am telling you the truth: if a person is not born from water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God!
3.6: What has been born from men is human. And what has been born from the Spirit is spiritual.
3.7: " Don't be surprised because I said this to you: 'You must be born again. '
3.8: The wind blows wherever it wishes. You hear the sound of it, but you don't know where it comes from or where it is going. It is the same way with everyone who has been born of the Spirit. "
3.9: Nicodemus responded to Jesus, " How can these things happen? "
3.10: Jesus answered him, " Are you a teacher of the people of Israel, and you don't know these things?
3.11: I am telling you the truth: we are talking about what we know. We are telling the truth about what we have seen. But you are not accepting our truth.
3.12: " Since I am talking to you about things on earth and you are not believing them, if I were to tell you about heavenly things, how could you believe?
3.13: I am the only one who ever came down from heaven and ever went up to heaven.
3.14: Moses lifted up the brass snake in the desert. In the same way, I must be lifted up
3.15: so that everyone who commits himself to me will have eternal life. "
3.16: God gave Himself to the people of the world, for their good, expecting nothing in return, by giving up His one and only Son. Every person who commits himself to Jesus will not be destroyed. Instead, that person will have eternal life.
3.17: " God did not send His Son into the world to judge it. God sent Jesus so that the people of the world could be saved through him.
3.18: The person who commits himself to Jesus is not condemned, but the one who does not commit himself to Jesus has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God's one and only Son.
3.19: This is the verdict: light has come into the world, but people gave themselves to darkness instead of light because the things which they were doing were evil.
3.20: Everyone who does evil hates the light. He does not come toward the light. He doesn't want his evil deeds to be exposed.
3.21: But the person who is living by the truth comes into the light. He wants his actions to become clear because he did them through God. "
3.22: After this, Jesus and his students went to the land of Judea. He stayed there with them and he was immersing some people.
3.23: John was immersing people in the town of Aenon ( which is not far from the town of Salim ) because there was plenty of water there. People continued coming to be immersed.
3.24: ( John had not yet been thrown into prison. )
3.25: There was an argument between some of John's students and a Jewish man about making things pure.
3.26: They came to John and said to him, " Rabbi, the man you have endorsed, who was with you on the other side of the Jordan River, look, he is immersing people too. Everyone is coming to him! "
3.27: John answered, " No one can receive anything if heaven has not given it to him.
3.28: You yourselves know that I told the truth when I said, 'I am not the Messiah! ' I have been sent ahead of him.
3.29: The groom is the one who will get the bride. The best man is the one who stands by and listens. He is glad when he hears the groom's voice. This is my joy; it is now complete.
3.30: " Jesus must become more important; I will become less important.
3.31: The one who comes from above is greater than all things. The person who comes from the earth belongs to the earth and talks about the earth. The one who comes from heaven is the most important.
3.32: He tells the truth about what he has seen and heard, but no one accepts his proof.
3.33: The person who does accept his proof confirms that God is true.
3.34: " God sent Jesus. Jesus speaks the words of God because God gave him the Spirit without limit.
3.35: The Father has given Himself to the Son, for his good, expecting nothing in return, and has put everything in the Son's control.
3.36: The person who commits himself to the Son has eternal life, but the person who does not obey the Son will not see eternal life. Instead, God's punishment stays on that person. "

4.1: The Pharisees heard that Jesus was making more students and immersing more people than John.
4.2: ( Jesus was really not the one who performed the immersion; his students did it. )
4.3: When Jesus heard this, he left Judea and went back to the Galilee.
4.4: Jesus needed to go through the area of Samaria.
4.5: He came to a town in Samaria called Sychar. It was near the property which Jacob had given to Joseph, his son.
4.6: Jacob's well was there. Jesus was tired because of traveling so he sat down for a while at the well. It was about noon.
4.7: A Samaritan woman came to get some water. Jesus said to her, " Please, give me a drink of water. "
4.8: ( His students had gone into town to buy some food. )
4.9: The Samaritan woman said to Jesus, " You are a Jewish man and I am a Samaritan woman. Why are you asking me for a drink of water? " ( Jewish people didn't want to associate with Samaritans. )
4.10: Jesus answered her, " If you knew about God's gift and who I really am, you would ask me to give you a drink of living water! "
4.11: The woman said to Jesus, " Sir, you don't even have a bucket and the well is deep. Where are you going to get this living water?
4.12: You are not greater than Jacob, our ancestor, are you? Jacob's flocks and herds, his sons, and Jacob himself drank from this well. He gave it to us! "
4.13: Jesus answered her, " Any person who drinks this water will become thirsty again
4.14: but if anyone drinks the water which I will give him, he will never be thirsty again. The water which I give him will become a spring inside him, welling up to eternal life. "
4.15: The woman said to Jesus, " My Lord, give me some of this water so that I won't get thirsty and won't have to come back here again and again to get water. "
4.16: Jesus said to her, " Go, call your husband. Then come back here. "
4.17: The woman answered him, " I don't have a husband. " Jesus said to her, " So true!
4.18: You have had five husbands, and the man you have now is not your husband. You spoke the truth. "
4.19: The woman said to him, " My Lord, I now understand that you are a prophet.
4.20: Our ancestors worshipped on this mountain, but you Jews say that Jerusalem is the place where people must worship. "
4.21: Jesus said to her, " Believe me, woman, the time is coming when you won't worship the Father on this mountain or in Jerusalem.
4.22: You Samaritans are worshipping that which you don't understand, but we Jews are worshipping what we know. Deliverance from sin comes from the Jewish people.
4.23: But the time is coming and has now come when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth. The Father is searching for this kind of people to worship Him.
4.24: God is spirit — the people who worship God must worship Him in spirit and in truth. "
4.25: The woman said to Jesus, " I know that Messiah ( the one called Christ ) is coming. When he comes, he will tell us about everything. "
4.26: Jesus said to her, " I am the one! "
4.27: Just then, Jesus' students came. They were amazed that Jesus was talking with a woman. However, not one of them asked, " What do you want? " or " Why are you talking with her? "
4.28: Then the woman left her water bucket and went back into town. This is what she said to the people:
4.29: " Come, see a man who told me everything I've ever done. He must be the Messiah! "
4.30: So they left town and they were coming to him.
4.31: Meanwhile, Jesus' students were encouraging Jesus to eat something. They said, " Rabbi, eat! "
4.32: But Jesus said to them, " I have food to eat which you don't know about. "
4.33: The students said to one another, " No one brought Jesus anything to eat, did they? "
4.34: Jesus said to them, " I must obey what God wants; He sent me. I must finish His work. That is food for me!
4.35: You say, 'Four months more and then the time for harvest comes. ' But, listen, I am telling you to look up and see the fields. They are ready for harvest now.
4.36: The person who gathers the harvest receives his pay; he gathers the crops for eternal life. The person who plants and the person who gathers will be happy at the same time.
4.37: This saying is true: 'One person plants and another person gathers. '
4.38: I sent you to gather the harvest for which you have not worked. Other men worked hard; you are gaining from their work. "
4.39: Many Samaritan people in that city believed in Jesus because of the woman's word. She testified, " He told me everything I ever did! "
4.40: When the Samaritan men came to Jesus, they were begging him to stay with them. Jesus stayed there for two days.
4.41: Many more people believed because of Jesus' message.
4.42: They said to the woman, " We believe not only because of what you said, but also because we ourselves have heard Jesus. We know that he is truly the Savior of the world! "
4.43: After two days Jesus left there to go to the Galilee.
4.44: Jesus himself said that this was true: " A prophet is not accepted in his own hometown. "
4.45: When he came to the Galilee, the people of the Galilee welcomed him. They had seen all the things he did in Jerusalem at the Passover Festival. ( They also went to the feast. )
4.46: Again Jesus went to the town of Cana in the Galilee, where he had changed the water into wine. There was a government official there. He had a son who was sick in the town of Capernaum.
4.47: This man heard that Jesus had arrived in the Galilee from the land of Judea. The man came to Jesus and begged him to go to his home and heal his son. ( The son was about to die. )
4.48: Jesus said to the man, " You people must see proofs from God and miracles or you will never believe. "
4.49: The government official said to Jesus, " Lord, please go to my house before my little boy dies! "
4.50: Jesus answered him, " Go, your son lives. " The man believed. He took Jesus at his word and left.
4.51: While the man was going home, his slaves met him. They said, " Your child lives! "
4.52: Then the man began asking them questions about the exact time when the boy got better. They answered, " The fever left him yesterday at one o'clock in the afternoon. "
4.53: The father knew that this was the exact time when Jesus had said, " Your son lives! " The man and his whole family believed.
4.54: This was the second miracle that Jesus performed, after he came to the Galilee from the land of Judea.

5.1: Later there was another Jewish festival. Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
5.2: Near the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem there is a pool that is called Bethesda in Aramaic. It has five porches.
5.3: A crowd of people used to lie around among the porches. Some of them were sick, blind, lame, or crippled.
5.4: An angel went down at a certain time and stirs the water: whoever was the first to step into the water then was made well of whatever disease he had.
5.5: One man had been there as an invalid for 38 years.
5.6: When Jesus saw the man lying there, he knew that the man had been there a long time. Jesus asked him, " Do you want to be well? "
5.7: The sick man answered Jesus, " Sir, I don't have anyone to put me into the pool when the water stirs. While I am going, someone else goes ahead of me. "
5.8: Jesus said to him, " Get up! Pick up your small bed and walk! "
5.9: Immediately the man got well. He picked up his bed and began walking around. ( This happened on a Sabbath day. )
5.10: The Jewish leaders were saying to the man who had been healed, " It is the Sabbath day! It is not right for you to carry your bed. "
5.11: The man answered them, " The one who made me well told me to pick up my bed and walk. "
5.12: They asked him, " Who is the man who told you to pick up your bed and walk? "
5.13: The man who was healed didn't know who Jesus was because Jesus had slipped away in the crowd that was there.
5.14: Later, Jesus found the man in the temple courtyard. Jesus said to him, " Look, you have been made well. Stop sinning so that something worse won't happen to you. "
5.15: The man went and told the Jewish leaders that Jesus was the one who had made him well.
5.16: Because of this, the Jewish leaders were persecuting Jesus — he was doing these things on the Sabbath day.
5.17: Jesus answered them, " My Father always works and I must work too. "
5.18: Because of this, the Jewish leaders were trying even harder to kill Jesus. They thought that Jesus was not only breaking the rules about the Sabbath day but he was also claiming that God was his own Father, thus making himself equal with God.
