7.28: But if you do get married, you have not done wrong. And if a virgin girl gets married, she has not sinned. However, married people will have many troubles at this time and I would like to protect you.
7.29: Brothers, I am saying this because time is short. Soon men who have wives must act as though they are not married.
7.30: People who are crying must act as though they are not really crying. Those who are happy must act as though they are not happy. People who buy things must act as though they don't own what they have bought.
7.31: Those who do business with the world must act as though they don't care. Why? Because this world, as you see it, won't last long.
7.32: I want you to be free from worry. An unmarried believing man is concerned about the Lord's things and he is trying to please the Lord.
7.33: A married believing man is worried about worldly things: he is trying to please his wife.
7.34: He is torn between the two. An unmarried believing woman or virgin girl is concerned about the Lord's things: she wants to be holy in body and spirit. A married believing woman worries about worldly things: she is trying to please her husband.
7.35: I am saying this to help you. I'm not trying to add an extra burden to you. Do what seems right. Give yourselves completely to the Lord without distraction.
7.36: Someone may not think he is doing the right thing with his bride - to - be. She may not be getting any younger either. He may feel he should marry her. Let him do what he wants to; he is not sinning. Let them get married!
7.37: However, another man may have already firmly decided that he does not need to get married because he has complete control of his sexual will power. He has decided in his heart that he won't marry her. He'll be doing a fine thing too.
7.38: The man who marries his bride - to - be is doing a good thing, but the man who does not marry will be doing even better.
7.39: A believing woman is bound by her marriage promise as long as her husband lives, but if her husband dies, she becomes free from it. She may marry anyone — anyone in the Lord Jesus.
7.40: But I think she would be happier if she stayed a widow. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.

8.1: You wrote me about meat offered to false gods. We know that all of us have spiritual knowledge. Knowledge makes a person proud but giving yourself to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, builds up people.
8.2: Someone may seem to know a lot but he still doesn't know what he must know.
8.3: If someone gives himself to God, for His good, expecting nothing in return, God knows this person.
8.4: You wrote me about eating meat which has been offered to false gods. We know that they really don't exist. There is only one true God.
8.5: There are " gods " in heaven and on earth — many " gods " and many " lords " — but they are not real.
8.6: To us, there is only one God — the Father. He is the Source of everything. We live for Him. There is only one Lord — Jesus Christ. Everything was created through him. We live through him.
8.7: However, not everyone has this spiritual knowledge. Some people still have the habit of treating idols as though they were real when they eat such meat. Their conscience is weak; they feel that the food makes them unclean.
8.8: Food is not the thing that brings us closer to God. We are not losing anything if we don't eat some things. We are not any better off if we do eat.
8.9: But be careful — don't let your freedom cause a weak person to sin.
8.10: You have spiritual knowledge. Suppose you sit down to eat meat inside the temple of a false god and suppose a person with a weak conscience sees you. His conscience would become bold; he would go inside and eat meat offered to false gods too!
8.11: So your spiritual knowledge would destroy a person with a weak conscience. And Christ died for that brother!
8.12: In this way you would have sinned against the brothers. You would have hurt their weak consciences and you would have sinned against Christ!
8.13: Therefore if meat causes my brother to sin, I will never eat meat. I don't want to make my brother sin.

9.1: I am free, am I not? I'm a delegate, am I not? I have seen our Lord Jesus, haven't I? You are the result of my efforts for the Lord, aren't you?
9.2: Others may not think I truly am a delegate. At least to you I am a delegate because you are the proof of it in the Lord Jesus!
9.3: When people criticize me, this is my defense:
9.4: we have the right to receive food and drink for work.
9.5: Do not each of us have the right to travel with a believing wife? We have the same right as the other delegates, brothers of the Lord Jesus, and Peter.
9.6: Are we, Barnabas and myself, the only ones who have to work for a living?
9.7: Soldiers don't pay their own wages. A farmer who plants a vineyard is allowed to eat some of the grapes. A shepherd who takes care of the flock of sheep gets some of the milk from the flock.
9.8: I am not claiming these things from human examples. The law says the same things.
9.9: This is written in the law of Moses: " Don't cover the ox's mouth while it is walking around on the wheat straw. " Did God say this because He cares about oxen?
9.10: God said all this for us; it was written to teach us something. The person who is plowing should plow with hope. The man who separates the grain from the straw should hope to share part of the grain.
9.11: Since we planted spiritual things among you, it should be no big thing to harvest physical things from you.
9.12: Other people have the right for support from you. Shouldn't we have it too? Yes, but we have not used this right. We endure all of these things because we don't want to do anything to slow down the Good News of Christ.
9.13: Surely you realize that those priests who work in the temple area eat some of the food that is offered there. And those who work near the altar share in the food that is offered there.
9.14: In the same way, the Lord Jesus commanded that the men who are preaching the Good News should be able to make a living from preaching it.
9.15: I have not used any of these privileges. I am not writing these things so that I can get something from you — I would rather die first! No one will take away what I'm so proud of!
9.16: I am telling the Good News, but that is nothing I can brag about. I feel compelled to do it. How awful it would be for me if I were not telling the Good News!
9.17: If I do it because I really choose to do it, I could get a reward. But if I do it as a duty, I am only doing the job that God gave me.
9.18: What reward do I get? I tell the story of the Good News of Christ free of charge. So I don't use my privilege when I am telling the Good News.
9.19: I am my own man; no man owns me. I make myself a slave to everyone so that I may win many people for the Good News.
9.20: To Jews, I became more Jewish to win them. I obey the law for the good of those who think they are under its rule. ( I am not really under its authority ). I am only trying to win those who obey the law.
9.21: I obey no special rules for the good of non - Jewish people. This does not mean that I am free from God's law; I am within Christ's law! I am only trying to win non - Jewish people for the Good News.
9.22: To weak people, I became weak so that I could win weak people. I have become almost anything for the good of everyone so that I could save some of them in some way.
9.23: Everything I do, I do for the spreading of the Good News. I want to share in it.
9.24: Surely you realize that, of all those who are running a race in the stadium, only one of them can receive the prize. In the same way, run your race so that you may win the prize.
9.25: Every athlete who is in training must have complete control of his body. He trains to receive a prize — it will not last. But we do it to receive a prize which lasts forever.
9.26: So I am not just running in one spot. I'm not shadowboxing; I really punch!
9.27: I make my body tough, bringing it under complete control. Otherwise I might be disqualified after I have preached to others.

10.1: Brothers, I want you to realize that all of our ancestors were under the cloud and all of them passed through the Red Sea.
10.2: All of them were immersed into Moses' protection under the cloud and in the sea.
10.3: All of them ate the same spiritual food.
10.4: All of them drank the same spiritual drink. They were drinking from the spiritual rock which was following them. ( That rock was Christ. )
10.5: However, God was not pleased with most of them. Their dead bodies were scattered all over the desert.
10.6: But these things are examples for us. We must not want evil things as our ancestors did.
10.7: We must not worship false gods as some of them did. This is written: " The people sat down to eat and drink and then they got up to play around. "
10.8: We must not commit unlawful sexual intercourse as some of them did. In one day God destroyed 23, 000 people!
10.9: We must not test the Lord as some of them did. They were killed by snakes.
10.10: You must not complain as some of them did. An angel of death killed them.
10.11: But all of these things happened to them for examples. This was written to warn us — we who are confronted by the end of the ages.
10.12: The person who thinks he is safe should be careful — he might fall!
10.13: You have been tempted the same way all people have been tempted, but God is faithful. He will not allow Satan to tempt you with more than you can resist. No, when you are being tempted, God will also give you a way to escape so that you can endure it.
10.14: So, you — to whom I give myself — run away from false gods.
10.15: I am talking the way I would talk to wise men. Weigh what I am saying.
10.16: The cup of blessing for which we thank God is the sharing of Christ's blood, isn't it? When we all break off a piece of bread, it is the sharing of Christ's body, isn't it?
10.17: Though there are many of us, we are one body. There is one loaf but all of us share this one loaf.
10.18: Look at physical Israel: the people who eat what is offered to God share in the altar.
10.19: So what am I saying? Does something offered to a false god mean anything? Is an idol real?
10.20: No! The people of this world are offering things to demons, not to the true God. I don't want you to be partners with demons!
10.21: You must not drink from the cup of the Lord and from the cup of demons. You must not share at the Lord's table and at the table of demons.
10.22: Are we trying to make the Lord jealous? Are we stronger than He is?
10.23: " I am allowed to do anything ", but not everything is the best thing to do. Yes, " I am allowed to do anything ", but not everything builds up other people.
10.24: Look for things which are good for someone else, not only for yourself.
10.25: Eat anything that is sold in the meat market. Don't ask any questions because of conscience.
10.26: " The earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord. "
10.27: If an unbeliever invites you to his home and you want to go, eat whatever he puts in front of you. Don't ask any questions because of conscience.
10.28: But if anyone says this to you: " This was offered to an idol! " Don't eat it — because of the one who said this and because of conscience.
10.29: By " conscience " I mean not yours, but his! But why is my freedom being judged by the conscience of someone else?
10.30: If I am thankful for what I have, why can someone say evil things about something for which I am thankful to God?
10.31: If you are eating, drinking, or doing anything, do everything to give glory to God.
10.32: Don't cause anyone to sin — Jews, non - Jews, or anyone in the community of God.
10.33: I try to please everyone in every way. I'm not looking for what is best for me, but what is best for most people so that they will be saved.

11.1: Follow my example as I am following the example of Christ.
11.2: I praise you because you remember me in all things. You are loyal to the teaching that I passed on to you:
11.3: I want you to understand that God is over Christ. Christ is over every male. And males are over females.
11.4: Every male who is praying or prophesying with his head covered brings shame to his head.
11.5: Any female who is praying or prophesying with her head uncovered brings shame on her head. This means the same thing as shaving the head.
11.6: If a woman's head is not covered, she should cut off all her hair! Since it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or shaved, she should wear a covering.
11.7: A male ought not to cover his head. He is the image and glory of God; the female is the glory of the male.
11.8: The male did not come from the female; she came from him.
11.9: The male was not made for the female; she was made for him.
11.10: This is why a female ought to show some sign on her head that she is respecting authority. She should also do it because of the angels.
11.11: In the Lord Jesus, she is not independent. But the male is not independent of the female either.
11.12: The female came from the male, but males also come from females. Everything comes from God.
11.13: Decide for yourselves: does it seem right to you that a woman should pray to God without a covering?
11.14: Don't you just naturally conclude that it is shameful for a man to wear long hair?
11.15: A woman's glory is her long hair. It is given to her for a covering.
11.16: If someone wants to argue about it, we don't have a different custom, neither do the called out people who belong to God.
11.17: I am not praising you with the following instructions: your meetings are hurting you instead of helping you!
11.18: First, when you come together as a called out people, I hear that there are divisions among you. I believe part of this is true.
11.19: It is apparently necessary to have factions among you so that it will become plain which of you are " true " believers.
11.20: When you gather together, you are not eating the Lord's supper
11.21: because each person takes his own supper. He does not wait for others; he just goes ahead and eats. So one stays hungry and another gets drunk.
11.22: You have houses where you can eat and drink. Do you look down on God's called out people? Do you want to make poor people ashamed? What should I say to you? Should I praise you? I most certainly do not!
11.23: I received from the Lord what I passed on to you: during the night that the Lord Jesus was betrayed, he took bread.
11.24: Then he thanked God for it and broke off some of it. Jesus said, " This bread is my body which is broken for you. Eat this to remember me. "
11.25: After supper, Jesus took a cup in the same way. He said, " This cup is the new covenant with God in my blood. Drink this to remember me. Every time you drink this, you will be remembering me. "
11.26: Every time you eat this bread and drink from this cup, you are telling about the Lord Jesus' death until he returns.
11.27: So if anyone eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord with the wrong attitude, he will be guilty of sinning against the body and the blood of the Lord Jesus Christ!
11.28: Each person must look deeply into his own heart. Then he should eat the bread and drink from the cup in the right way.
11.29: If someone is eating and drinking without recognizing the meaning of the body of Christ, he is condemning himself by eating and drinking!
11.30: This is why many of you are weak and sick. A large number of you have died too.
11.31: If we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.
11.32: No, the Lord judges us. We are being corrected so that we will not be condemned with the people of the world.
11.33: So, my brothers, when you gather together to eat the supper of the Lord, wait for one another.
11.34: If someone comes only for the food, he should stay home and eat there! Meeting together should not bring condemnation on you. I will give more orders when I come.

12.1: Brothers, I want you to know the truth about spiritual gifts.
12.2: Do you remember when you were people of the world? You were controlled by false gods which couldn't talk; you followed them.
12.3: So I make this clear to you: no one who is speaking by God's Spirit can say, " Jesus, be cursed! "; and no one can say, " Jesus is Lord ", unless he says it by the Holy Spirit.
12.4: There are many different spiritual gifts, but it is the same Spirit who gives them.
12.5: There are many different ways of serving, but it is the same Lord Jesus who is being served.
12.6: There are many different abilities, but it is the same God who gives them. God gives all of these powers to all of the people who have them.
12.7: The showing of the Spirit is given to each one for the good of everyone:
12.8: the ability to speak wisely is given through the Spirit to one person. The ability to give knowledge is given by the same Spirit to another person.
12.9: A different person receives faith by the same Spirit. The ability to heal diseases is given to another by the one Spirit.
12.10: The ability to work miracles is given to someone else. The ability to prophesy is given to another person. The ability to see the difference between what spirits teach is given to another one. The ability to speak different languages is given to one. The ability to interpret different languages is given to someone else.
12.11: All of these powers are given by one and the same Spirit. He distributes them to each person as he chooses.
12.12: The body is a unit but it has many parts. All of the many parts of the body make up one body. Christ is the same way.
12.13: All of us were immersed into this one body of Christ by one Spirit — Jews / non - Jews, slaves / free men — we all drink from the same Spirit.
12.14: The body does not have only one part; it has many parts.
12.15: The foot might say, " Since I am not a hand, I don't belong with the body. " But it still belongs with the body!
12.16: The ear might say, " Since I'm not an eye, I don't belong with the body. " But it still does belong with the body!
12.17: If the whole body were an eye, how would the body hear? If the whole body were an ear, where would smelling come from?
12.18: God has now put each member in the body as He chose to do.
12.19: If everything were just one member, there would be no body!
12.20: But now though we are many members, we are one body.
12.21: The eye cannot say this to the hand: " I do not need you! " Again the head cannot say to the feet: " I do not need you! "
12.22: No, the members of the body which seem to be weaker than other parts are truly necessary.
12.23: There are parts of the body which we think are ugly. We give these parts special care. We treat an unmentionable part of the body with special attention.
12.24: The more beautiful parts of our body do not need this. But God has joined the parts of the body together. He gives more honor to the parts that need it.
12.25: God wants no division in the body. Instead, He wants the members to care about one another.
12.26: If one member is suffering, all of the members are suffering too. If another member receives an honor, then all the members are happy for him.
12.27: All of you are the body of Christ. Each one of you is part of Christ's body.
12.28: Among all those called out peoples, God put in: first, delegates; second, prophets; third, teachers; next, those who work miracles; then, people who heal diseases; people who help others; organizers; those who speak different languages.
12.29: All of them are not delegates, are they? Not all of them are prophets, are they? Are all of them teachers? All of them are not miracle workers, are they?
12.30: All of them do not have the gift of healing diseases, do they? Not all of them speak different languages, do they? All of them cannot interpret different languages, can they?
12.31: Eagerly desire the more important spiritual gifts. I will now show you the best way of all. —

13.1: Even if I speak with human languages or the language of angels, but do not give myself to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, I have only become like the noisy sound of a gong or the ringing sound from cymbals.
13.2: I may have the ability to prophesy, know all secrets, possess all knowledge, and have the kind of faith which can move mountains — but if I don't give myself to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, I am nothing.
13.3: I could give away everything I own and sacrifice my body so that I could brag about it, but if I did not give myself to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, I have gained nothing.
13.4: Giving yourself to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, is patient; is kind; is not jealous; is not boastful; is not proud;
13.5: is not rude; is not interested solely in himself; is even - tempered; does not hold grudges;
13.6: is not happy when someone else does wrong; is happy when truth wins;
13.7: it always protects; always trusts; always hopes for the best; always keeps on going.
13.8: Giving yourself to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, lasts forever. There are such things as prophecies, but they will disappear. There are languages, but they will stop. There is such a thing as knowledge from God, but it will disappear.
13.9: We only know portions of things from God. We prophesy in parts
13.10: but when that which is complete comes, the parts will disappear.
13.11: When I was a child, I used to talk about the things that a child would talk about. I thought and reasoned as a child does; but now that I have become an adult, I have put aside the ways of children.
13.12: At this time we see only a blurred image in the metal mirror. At that time we will see plainly — as one person looking at another's face. Now I know things only partially, but then I will know everything completely, just as God knows me.
13.13: And now these three remain: faith, hope and the giving of yourself to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return. But the greatest of these is giving yourself to others.

14.1: Follow the giving of yourself to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, and eagerly desire the spiritual gifts, especially prophesying.
14.2: Anyone who is speaking in a different language is not communicating to men, but to God. No one understands him. He is speaking the secrets of God by inspiration.
14.3: But everyone who prophesies to people is speaking to build them up, to encourage them, and to comfort them.
14.4: The one who is speaking a different language is only helping himself, but the one who is prophesying is helping the called out people.
14.5: I wish that all of you could speak in different languages but, even more, I wish you could prophesy. The one who is prophesying is more effective than the one who speaks in different languages — unless he can interpret it in such a way that the called out people will get some good from it.
14.6: Now, brothers, if I come speaking different languages to you, what good will you get out of it? I may speak to you by revelation, different knowledge, prophecy, or different teaching.
14.7: Lifeless instruments, such as a flute or a harp, produce a sound. This sound must be made clearly or no one can recognize the tune that is being played on the flute or the harp.
14.8: If the bugle makes a sound that is not clear, no one will prepare for battle.
14.9: In the same way, if you use a different language to give your fine message, how will anyone understand what is being said? You will seem to be like a person who talks to himself!
14.10: There are many different languages in the world. All of them have meaning.
14.11: If I don't understand the meaning of the language, I am a foreigner to the one who is speaking and he is a foreigner to me.
14.12: Since you are eager for spiritual gifts, eagerly desire those which will help the whole called out people the most.
14.13: So the one who is speaking in a different language must pray that he will be able to interpret what he said.
14.14: When I am using a different language in prayer, my spirit is praying but my understanding has no part in it.
14.15: So what should I do? I will pray with my spirit and pray with understanding too. I will sing to God with my spirit and sing with understanding also.
14.16: When you are praising God in a different language only with your spirit, how will the ordinary person know when to say, " Amen "? You are giving thanks to God but that man doesn't know what you are saying.
14.17: It is a fine thing that you are giving thanks to God but the other person is not getting any good out of it.
14.18: I thank God that I speak in different languages more than all of you.
14.19: However, in the meeting I would rather speak five words with understanding to teach other people than thousands of words in a different language!
14.20: Brothers, be as innocent as children about evil things, but don't be like children in how you think. Be mature!
14.21: This is written in the law: " I will speak to this nation with different languages and different dialects, but they will not obey me. " That is what the Lord God said.
14.22: Speaking different languages is a proof from God to unbelievers, not to the people who already believe. The ability to prophesy is proof to believers, not to unbelievers.
14.23: Suppose the whole called out people gathers together and everyone is speaking with different languages. Then an ordinary person or unbeliever comes into the room. Would he not say you are crazy?
14.24: But if everyone can prophesy, and an unbeliever or ordinary person comes into the room, he will feel convicted of sin by everything that is happening. He will feel judged by everyone.
14.25: The secret things of his heart will come out into the open. He will bow down his face and begin to worship God, confessing: " God is really among you! "
14.26: Brothers, what should be done? When you gather together, someone may have a song. Someone else may have a teaching to give, a special revelation, a different language, or an interpretation. Everything should be done for the good of the whole community.
14.27: If someone speaks with a different language, let him speak — but only two or three at the most. Let them speak by taking turns, and let only one person interpret.
14.28: If no interpreter is there, the person who speaks a different language must not speak among the called out people. However, he is allowed to think to himself and worship God silently.
14.29: Let two or three prophets talk while others evaluate carefully what they say.
14.30: If a revelation from God comes to another person who is sitting down, the first prophet must stop talking immediately.
14.31: All of you will have an opportunity to prophesy, but it must be by turn so that everyone will learn and be encouraged.
14.32: The people who have the gift of prophecy can control their own spirits.
14.33: God is a God of peace, not confusion. This is the way it should be in all of the called out people who are the saints!
14.34: The women must be quiet in the meetings. They are not allowed to speak. They must be under authority, as the law says.
14.35: If the women want to learn more about something, they should ask their husbands at home. It is shameful for a woman to speak in the meeting.
14.36: Did God's message come from you? Are you the only ones it came to?
14.37: Someone may think he is a prophet or an inspired person. However, that person must acknowledge that what I am writing to you is a command from the Lord!
14.38: If he doesn't want to listen, he won't be listened to.
14.39: So, my brothers, eagerly desire the ability to prophesy. And don't try to stop people from speaking in different languages.
14.40: Everything should be done properly and orderly.

15.1: Brothers, I am telling you the Good News which I've already told you. You accepted it and you are still staying with it.
15.2: If you hold onto the Good News which I told you, then through it you are being saved — unless you believed it for nothing!
15.3: First of all, I passed on to you the same thing which was passed on to me: Christ died for our sins. ( The Scriptures told about this before it happened. )
15.4: He was buried and he was raised from death on the third day. ( The Scriptures foretold this too. )
15.5: Then Jesus appeared to Peter, and later to all the delegates.
15.6: Then he appeared to more than 500 brothers at the same time. Most of these people are still alive today, but some of them have already died.
15.7: Christ appeared to Jacob, and then to all the delegates.
15.8: Last of all, he also appeared to me. I was like a baby born very late.
15.9: Of all the delegates, I am the least important. I don't even deserve to be called a delegate; I persecuted the called out people of God!
15.10: But I am what I am because of God's help in time of need which he pointed toward me. This paid off! I worked harder than all of the other delegates. But it was not really I that was working so hard — it was God's help in time of need which I have with me!
15.11: It doesn't matter whether the Good News came through me or through other delegates — we preached it and you believed it!
15.12: Since it is being preached that Christ has been raised from death, why do some of you claim that when people die, they do not live again!
15.13: If people don't rise from death, then Christ has not been raised from death.
15.14: And if Christ hasn't been raised from death, then what we are preaching is not true. You have believed in something which is false!
15.15: We are guilty of being liars about God. We told the truth from God — that God raised Christ from death. But if people don't rise from death, then God did not raise Christ from death!
15.16: If people don't rise from death, then Christ has not been raised from death either.
15.17: And if Christ hasn't been raised from death, your faith is worthless. You are still lost in your sins!
15.18: And all of those who died in Christ are gone.
15.19: If we have put our hope in Christ in this life and Christ did not rise from death, then, of all people, we should be pitied the most.
15.20: But now, Christ has been raised from death! He was the first one of those whom have already died.
15.21: Death came into the world through one man; rising from death has also come through one man.
15.22: Everyone dies because of what Adam did, and everyone will live because of what Christ did.
15.23: Each one will rise from death in his proper order. Christ was the first one. The people who belong to Christ will rise from death when Jesus comes from heaven.
15.24: Then the end will come. Christ will hand over the kingdom to God the Father. Christ will destroy every ruler, every authority and power.
15.25: Christ must be the king until God puts all Christ's enemies under Christ's feet.
15.26: Death is the last enemy to be destroyed.
15.27: " God will put everything under his feet. " ( When it says " everything ", it is clear that this does not include God, the One who puts everything under Christ's authority ).
15.28: After God does this, Christ will put himself under God's authority ( the One who put everything under Christ ). This is the way that God will be above all things in everything.
15.29: Some people are immersed on account of people who died. If people do not rise from death, then why do they do this?
15.30: Why are we always in danger?
15.31: I face death every day. ( Brothers, I am proud of you; that is the one thing I have in Christ Jesus our Lord. )
15.32: I fought against wild animals in the city of Ephesus. If people don't rise from death, what good did I get from it? If it were for only human reasons, then: " Let's eat and drink today, for we will die tomorrow! "
15.33: Don't be fooled, " Bad friends will spoil good habits. "
15.34: Be alert and do what is right. Some people don't have a true knowledge of God. ( I say this to make you feel ashamed. )
15.35: But someone will say, " How do people rise from death? What kind of body do they come back with? "
15.36: You are foolish! What you plant does not live unless it dies first.
15.37: When you plant something, you are not planting the full - grown plant! No, it is a bare seed, perhaps wheat or some other grain.
15.38: God gives it the shape He wants. Each kind of seed has its own shape.
15.39: All cell tissue is different. Human beings have their own kind of flesh. Animals have a different type, as do birds and fish.
15.40: There are bodies in the universe and bodies on earth, but the beauty of the universe is different from the beauty of anything on earth.
15.41: The sun has its own beauty; the moon has another kind of beauty. The stars have still another type of beauty. Even the stars are different from one another in their beauty.
15.42: So people do rise from death! A dead body is buried in decay, but it will be raised, never to die again.
15.43: A dead body will be buried with sadness, but it will be raised from death with splendor. A dead body is buried in weakness, but it will be raised with power.
15.44: A dead body is buried as a physical body, but it will be raised as a spiritual body. Since there is a physical body, there is also a spiritual body.
15.45: This has been written: " The first man, Adam, became a living soul. " But the last Adam became a life - giving spirit.
15.46: The physical body came first, not the spiritual body.
15.47: The first man came from the dust of the earth. The second man came from heaven.
15.48: Earthly people are like the one who came from dust. The ones who go to heaven will be like the one who came from heaven.
15.49: Now we look like the one who came from dust — but we will look like the one who came from heaven.
15.50: Brothers, I am saying this because men in their physical form cannot enter the kingdom of God. That which can decay cannot have a share in what never dies.
15.51: Listen! I am telling you a secret: we all will not stay in death; we will all be changed.
15.52: We will be changed instantly, like the twinkle in someone's eye. That last trumpet will sound. Then people will rise from death, never to die again and we will be changed.
15.53: This decaying body must be dressed with immortality. This body, which can die, must be dressed with a body which can never die.
15.54: This body, which can be destroyed, will be replaced with a body which cannot be destroyed. This body, which can die, will be replaced with a body which can never die. Then the message which has been written will come true: " Victory has swallowed up death.
15.55: Where is your victory, O death? Where is your power to hurt, O death? "
15.56: Sin is death's power to hurt. Sin gets its strength from its relationship with the law of God.
15.57: But, thank God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, God gives us the victory!
15.58: So, you — to whom I give myself, for your good, expecting nothing in return — be firm and don't be moved. Always be doing something for the Lord. You must realize that your hard work for the Lord will not be without meaning.

16.1: You wrote me about the special collection for the saints. I have already given orders to the called out people in the Galatian area. Do the same thing they did:
16.2: every first day of the week each one of you must store something aside, saving up from what God has prospered you. There should be no special collections after I have come.
16.3: When I arrive, choose the men you want. I will send them to Jerusalem with letters of introduction. They will carry your gift.
16.4: Perhaps I should go too. If so, they will travel with me.
16.5: I will come to you after I travel through the Macedonian area. ( I am going that way. )
16.6: Maybe I will stay with you — even spend the winter there. Then you can send me on ahead to wherever I am going.
16.7: I don't want to see you as I am passing through, just for a short while. I hope to stay with you for a long time if the Lord allows this.
16.8: I will stay here in Ephesus until Pentecost day.
16.9: A very important opportunity has come for me to be effective, though many people are against me.
16.10: If Timothy comes to you, be sure that he has nothing to worry about while he is with you. Timothy does the Lord's work as I do.
16.11: None of you should make him feel as though he is not important. Send him on ahead with your blessing, so that he may come back to me. I am expecting him to come along with the brothers you choose.
16.12: You wrote me about Apollos, our brother. Many times I encouraged him and some other brothers to come to you. He didn't want to go so that he may go now. He will come when he has a chance.
16.13: Watch out! Stand firm in the faith! Be strong like men! Hold on tight!
16.14: All of you should give yourselves to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return.
16.15: You know Stephanas' family. They were the first converts in the Achaian area. They have given themselves completely to helping the saints. Brothers, I beg you
16.16: to put yourselves under people like them and everyone who likes to work together, under those who work hard for the Lord.
16.17: I was very happy when Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus arrived. These men make up for your not being here.
16.18: They made my spirit feel refreshed, as I'm sure they did yours too. You should give special recognition to men like these.
16.19: The called out people in the land of Asia send you their greetings. Aquila and Priscilla send you many greetings in the Lord. The called out people that meets in their house sends you greetings too.
16.20: All of the brothers send you greetings. You should greet one another with a holy kiss of friendship.
16.21: With my own hand I am writing my greeting — From Paul.
16.22: If anyone does not love the Lord, he should be condemned! Please, Lord, come!
16.23: May the help in time of need of our Lord Jesus be with you.
16.24: May my giving of myself, to all of you in Christ Jesus, be with all of you. Amen.

1.1: From Paul ( God wanted me be to a delegate of Christ Jesus. ) and from brother Timothy. To God's called out people in the city of Corinth and to all of the saints all over the Achaian area.
1.2: May help in time of need and peace come from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: Give praise to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. He is the Father of tender feelings, the God of all comfort.
1.4: He encourages us when we have any kind of trouble. This is why we are able to encourage people who are having all kinds of trouble. We use the help which God gives us!
1.5: Just as the sufferings of Christ overflowed into our lives, in the same way our help also overflows to others through Christ.
1.6: If we are having trouble, it is for your sake! We want you to receive comfort and be saved. If we receive comfort, it is for you! We want you to receive comfort. When you are encouraged, you will be able to endure the same kind of suffering we experience.
1.7: Our hope for you is firm. Because you share the sufferings, we know that you will also share in the comfort.
1.8: Brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the trouble we went through in the land of Asia. The burdens were heavier than we could carry; we thought we were not going to live anymore.
1.9: We felt we had been condemned to die. But something happened to make us put our hope upon God ( who raises people from death ) and not in ourselves.
1.10: God has rescued us from such life and death situations and He will rescue us in the future. We have placed all our hopes on Him. He will always rescue us
1.11: while you are working together, praying for us. Then many people will be thankful to God for His favor to us. This is an answer to the prayers of many people.
1.12: This is what makes us feel so good: our conscience is telling the truth. We have lived our lives in this world purely and with the kind of sincerity which comes from God, especially toward you. We lived by God's help in time of need, not human wisdom.
1.13: We are writing to you only what you can read and understand. I hope you will get a complete understanding
1.14: as you have understood parts of what we've said before. Then you can be proud of us, as we will be proud of you, on the Day when the Lord Jesus comes.
1.15: I was sure of this so I planned to come to you first. Then you would be helped twice.
1.16: I planned to visit you on my way to and from the Macedonian area. Then you could help me on my trip to the land of Judea.
1.17: When I make my plans, do you think I often change my mind? Do I plan in a human way, saying 'yes' when I mean 'no'?
1.18: God is dependable. Our message to you is not saying one thing and meaning something else.
1.19: Jesus Christ, the Son of God, was preached among you through us — Silas, Timothy, and myself. That message was not inconsistent! No, in Christ it was a definite 'yes'!
1.20: All of God's promises are " yes " in Christ! Through Christ we give glory to God by saying " Amen ".
1.21: God makes all of us — you and us — firm in Christ. God has chosen us.
1.22: He sealed us and gave the Holy Spirit as a guarantee in our hearts.
1.23: I call upon God as my Witness; He knows my motives: I didn't go back again to Corinth because I did not want to hurt you.
1.24: We are not trying to rule over your faith because you are standing by faith. No, we are working with you so that you will be happy.

2.1: I decided in my own mind that I would not visit you again with sadness.
2.2: Because if I make you sad, who will cheer me up? The ones whom I made sad?
2.3: Why did I write this letter? Because when I visit, I want you to make me feel happy, as you should, and not sad. I'm sure that all of you are happy when I am happy.
2.4: I wrote you from a troubled, heavy heart, with many tears. I didn't want to make you feel sad. No, I wanted to show you the great giving of myself to you, which I have for you.
2.5: I am not the only one that this person in your group has made sad — it's all of you. Well, some of you. ( I don't want to be too unkind. )
2.6: This man has suffered enough punishment from the whole group.
2.7: Now you should forgive and encourage this person so that he won't be overcome with too much sorrow.
2.8: I beg you to show him that you truly are giving yourselves to him, for his good, expecting nothing in return.
2.9: Why did I write you? To find out if you could pass this test: would you always obey?
2.10: If you forgive someone, then I forgive him too. Christ sees me do it. I forgive because you do, if there was anything to forgive in the first place.
2.11: Then Satan won't fool us. We know all about his tricks.
2.12: When I came to the city of Troas to tell the Good News about Christ, there was an open door for me in the Lord.
2.13: But I was still very worried because I couldn't find Titus, my brother. So I told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
2.14: Thank God! He always gives us the victory in Christ. God uses us to spread to all places the sweet smell of knowing Him.
2.15: To God, we are the pleasant smell of Christ among the people who are being saved and among those who are lost.
2.16: To one group, we are the smell of death; to the other group, the smell of life. Are we great enough for these things?
2.17: We are not like the many people who sell God's message. No, we speak sincerely before God in Christ — as men whom God has sent.

3.1: Are we beginning to pat ourselves on the back? Some people need letters of recommendation. We don't need letters like that, from you or to you; do we?
3.2: You are our letters! You are written on our hearts. Everyone knows you and can read you.
3.3: You are the result of our work. You are clearly a letter from Christ. It is not written with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God. It is not on stone tablets but on the tablets of human hearts!
3.4: This is the sort of confidence we have toward God through Christ.
3.5: It's not that we are so great, to think we can do anything on our own. No, our ability comes from God!
3.6: He made us able ministers of a new covenant, which is spiritual, not literal. The letter of the law kills, but the Spirit gives life!
3.7: The law was written on stones, but it came with such splendor that the sons of Israel could not continue looking at Moses' face, though that glory was fading away. And that was a ministry of death!
3.8: But how much more glorious will be the ministry of the Spirit?
3.9: Since the ministry which brought condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious will be the ministry which makes a person right with God?
3.10: Though the law was glorious, it is not bright when compared to a glory which is so much brighter today.
3.11: And the glory that lasts is greater than the glory that faded.
3.12: So we are very bold because we have such a hope.
3.13: We are not like Moses, who always wore a covering over his face, until the brightness faded away. He wanted to stop the sons of Israel from staring at it.
3.14: Their minds were closed. To this day when they read the Old Covenant, the covering is still there! It cannot be uncovered because it is removed only in Christ.
3.15: Even today, when they read the law of Moses, a covering lies upon their hearts.
3.16: But when someone " turns to the Lord, the covering is removed ".
3.17: The Spirit is " the Lord ". There is freedom wherever the Spirit of the Lord is.
3.18: All of us have uncovered faces; we reflect the same glory. It comes from the Spirit of the Lord. With one glory after another, we are being changed to look more like him.

4.1: That is why we don't give up. God has given us mercy. We have this ministry.
4.2: No, we put away secret things of which people are ashamed. We don't live by playing around with God's message or by using it in the wrong way. Instead, we make the truth plain, presenting ourselves to every person's conscience before God.
4.3: If our Good News is covered, it is covered to those who are lost.
4.4: The god of this world is among those people. They don't believe because he has blinded their minds. They cannot see the light of the Good News of the glorious Christ who is the image of God.
4.5: We are preaching that Christ Jesus is Lord. We are not preaching ourselves. Because of Jesus, we are only your slaves.
4.6: God has said, " From darkness let the light shine! " He made light shine in our hearts too. This brings us the light of knowing God's glory which can be seen in the face of Christ!
4.7: Why do we have this treasure in clay jars? To show that this superior power comes from God, not from us.
4.8: We are being squeezed — but we can still move. Sometimes we are in doubt — but we don't doubt the truth.
4.9: We are being chased — but God never abandons us. We are knocked down — but never knocked out.
4.10: We are always carrying the deadness of Jesus in our bodies so that, in our bodies, we may make Jesus' life obvious too.
4.11: Because of Jesus, those of us who are still alive are always being given up to die. Then the life of Jesus will be made clear in our dying flesh.
4.12: So death is active in us — but life is active in you.
4.13: This is written: " I believed, so I spoke. " Having that same spirit of faith, we also believe, and that is why we speak.
4.14: We know that God raised the Lord Jesus from death. He will also raise us to life with Jesus. He will present us, along with you, to God.
4.15: Everything happens for your good so that God's help in time of need will touch many more lives. They will be thankful and this will overflow for the glory of God.
4.16: That's why we never give up. Even though our physical bodies are wearing out, our spirits are getting younger every day.
4.17: The light troubles we now have will last only a short time. They are working out a far greater eternal glory for us, which is worth so much more than what we are suffering now.
4.18: We shouldn't look at things which can be seen. Instead, we should look for things which cannot be seen. What is seen is only temporary, but what is unseen lasts forever.

5.1: When the earthly " tent " in which we live is destroyed, we know that we have another building which comes from God — a house in the heavenly worlds, not man - made. It lasts forever.
5.2: That is why we groan, yearning to be clothed with our heavenly house.
5.3: Since we will be clothed with a body, we will not be a naked spirit.
5.4: While we are in our bodies now, we are groaning because we feel burdened. That doesn't mean we want to die; we only want a new life. Then eternal life will swallow up that which can die.
5.5: God made us for this very reason and He has given us the Spirit as a guarantee that we will live again.
5.6: Therefore, we are always cheerful. We know that, while we are at home in our physical bodies, we are not with the Lord — where home is.
5.7: We live by faith, not by seeing.
5.8: But we are cheerful; we would rather leave our bodies, and be at home with the Lord.
5.9: So whether we stay on earth or go home, we always want to please God.
5.10: All of us must appear in front of Christ's judgment bench. Then each person will receive good or bad as a reward — according to what he did while he was in his physical body.
5.11: We know what the awesome respect of the Lord really means. So we try to persuade people to live right. God knows all about us; I hope your consciences know us too.
5.12: Again we are not patting ourselves on the back in front of you. No, we are only giving you a good reason to be proud of us. Then you will have something to say to people who are proud of outward things and not proud of what is in the heart.
5.13: If we are crazy, then we are crazy for God! If we are in our right mind, then it is for your sake.
5.14: Christ's giving of himself to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, controls us. One man died for everyone. So everyone died. We are sure of that!
5.15: Christ died for everyone, so that people who are alive won't live only for themselves anymore. Instead, they will live for the one who died and came back to life for them.
5.16: So from now on, we really don't know a person by merely looking at his physical body. At one time we knew about Christ from a human viewpoint but we do not know him in that way anymore.
5.17: So if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. Old things have passed away. Listen, everything has become new.
5.18: Everything comes from God. He uses Christ to bring us back to Himself. God gave us the work of bringing people back to Himself.
5.19: When God was bringing the people of the world back to Himself in Christ, He was not counting their sins against them. God gave us the message about how He brings men back to Himself.
5.20: We are representing Christ. It is as though God is encouraging you through us. We beg you, for Christ's sake, come back to God!
5.21: Christ never sinned, but God caused him to become sin for us so that we could be made right with God in Christ.

6.1: As God's co - workers, you have received God's help in time of need. We beg you, don't waste it!
6.2: The Scripture says: " At the right time I listened to you. I helped you on the day of safety from danger. " Listen! Now is the right time. Listen! Now is the day of safety from danger!
6.3: We are always careful not to do anything which might hurt someone. We don't want anyone to blame the ministry.
6.4: Instead, in everything, we try to conduct ourselves as God's ministers: when we must endure much, when we are suffering, during hard times, when we are having problems,
6.5: when we are beaten, when we are in jail, during riots, while working hard, in sleepless night, when in fastings.
6.6: We try to do this with purity, with understanding, with patience, with kindness, with the Holy Spirit, with sincere giving of self to others for their good, expecting nothing in return,
6.7: with a true message, and with God's power. We have used the weapons of good to attack and to defend.
6.8: Through glory and disgrace, sometimes having a good reputation, and sometimes having a bad one — we are treated as men who fool people, but we tell the truth.
6.9: We are treated as if no one knows who we are, but we are well known. We are treated as if we are dying, but, look, we are still alive! We are treated as if we are beaten men, but we're not dead yet.
6.10: We are treated like men who are supposed to be sad, but we are always happy. We are treated as beggars, yet we make many people rich in faith. We are treated as men who own nothing, but we have everything!
6.11: We have spoken plainly to you people in Corinth. We opened wide our hearts.
6.12: We are not holding back our tender feelings from you. You are the ones who are holding back!
6.13: I am talking to you as if you were my children: open your hearts wide to us.
6.14: Don't be mismatched with unbelievers! How can right and wrong be partners? What do light and darkness share?
6.15: How can Christ and Satan agree? What does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?
6.16: How can God's temple exist next to false gods? We are the temple of the living God! It is as God said: " I will live in them and move among them. I will be their God. They will be my people. "
6.17: " 'So come away from them! Be separate! ' says the Lord. 'Don't touch what is not pure. Then I will accept you. ' "
6.18: " 'I will be your Father; and you will be my sons and daughters, ' says Almighty God. "

7.1: You to whom I give myself — since we have these promises, we should make ourselves clean from anything which might pollute the body or the spirit. Let us be completely holy, showing awesome respect for God.
7.2: Open up to us! We haven't done wrong to anyone; we ruined no one. We never took advantage of anybody.
7.3: I am not saying this to condemn you. I have told you before that you have a place in our hearts. We are together in life or death.
7.4: I have a lot of confidence in you. I'm very proud of you. Even though we have been through all kinds of trouble, I feel greatly encouraged and my joy is overflowing.
7.5: When we went into the Macedonian area, our bodies had no rest at all. We had all sorts of trouble. Outside, there were fights; inside, we were afraid.
7.6: However, God comforts people who are down; He comforted us when Titus came.
7.7: Not only that, we felt encouraged by the comfort you gave him. He told us about how much you yearned to see me, how deeply sorry you were, and about your enthusiasm for me. So I felt even happier.
7.8: Even though I made you sad with my letter, I am not sorry about it now. However, I could have regretted it. ( I see that that letter made you sad for a while. )
7.9: I am glad now, not because you were sad, but because you were sad enough to change your hearts! You became sad and that is what God wanted. So we didn't need to discipline you at all.
7.10: The kind of sorrow, which God uses, brings a change of heart that leads to safety from danger. There are no regrets. But the kind of sorrow in the world leads to death.
7.11: Look at what God's type of sorrow has produced in you! You are now eager. You wanted to defend yourselves. It made you upset. You were alarmed. You yearned to do something. You were excited. You wanted to make it right! You proved that you were innocent in every way in this matter.
7.12: So I did not write you because of the person who did wrong or because of the person who was wronged. It was to let you know how loyal you are to us before God.
7.13: That is why we are encouraged. Besides that, we are especially glad to see Titus happy. All of you made him feel very good.
7.14: I had bragged about you to him and you didn't let me down. Just as everything we told you was true, what we told Titus about you was also true.
7.15: He feels for you even more when he remembers that all of you obeyed. You welcomed him with awesome respect and trembling.
7.16: I am happy that I can be completely confident of you.

8.1: Now, brothers, we are going to tell you about the help in time of need which God has shown to the called out people in Macedonia:
8.2: they have suffered hard testing. However, even though they were very poor, they gave very generously. They were so happy.
8.3: I tell you the truth, they gave as much as they could — even more than they should — because they really wanted to.
8.4: They begged us again and again for the privilege of having a part in helping the saints in the land of Judea.
8.5: They did not do as we expected. No, the first thing they did was to give themselves to the Lord. Then they gave themselves to us to be used in whatever way the Lord wanted.
8.6: That is why we begged Titus to finish collecting your special gift of help in time of need. ( He was the one who started it. )
8.7: You are rich in everything: you have faith; you can tell God's message; you have a lot of knowledge; you are very eager to help; you give yourselves to us, for our good, expecting nothing in return. Now be rich with this special gift of help in time of need to them!
8.8: I am not giving this as an order. ( Others are eager to help too. ) I am only testing to see if your giving to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, is true.
8.9: You know the help in time of need of our Lord Jesus Christ. Even though he was rich, he became very poor for your sake. Why? So that you could become rich — because he was poor.
8.10: This is the advice I am giving; this is what's best for you. A year ago you were the first to do something — even the first to want to do something.
8.11: So finish doing it now! You planned it eagerly; be just as ready to complete it! Do whatever you can.
8.12: If someone is ready to give, God accepts what that person has, not what he doesn't have.
8.13: We don't want to make you suffer — just to give them some relief. Everyone should have the same amount.
8.14: At this time you have more than you need, while they are in need. Some day you may be in need and they will have more than they need. There should be a balance.
8.15: It is like this Scripture: " The man who gathered much did not have too much. And the man who gathered a small amount did not have too little. "
8.16: I thank God. He put the same eagerness in Titus' heart which I have for you.
8.17: When we asked Titus to help you, he welcomed it. He is enthusiastic. He is coming to you because he really wants to.
8.18: Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is respected among all of the called out people for preaching the Good News.
8.19: Not only that, he was appointed by the called out people to travel with us when we take this special gift of help in time of need. We will use this to give glory to the Lord. It shows how ready we are to help.
8.20: We want to stay away from any criticism of the way we use this generous gift.
8.21: We are trying to plan ahead for what looks right to men and to God.
8.22: Along with them, we are also sending our brother. We've often found him to be ready to help in many ways. But now, because he is so sure of you, he is even more enthusiastic.
8.23: I will say this for Titus: he is my partner. We work together for you. Our brothers are messengers of the called out people. They are Christ's glory.
8.24: So show your giving of self to others for their good, expecting nothing in return. Show why we are so proud of you. Then it will be clear to the other called out people.

9.1: I don't need to write you about helping the saints in the land of Judea.
9.2: Because I know you are ready, I have been bragging about you to the Macedonians: " The brothers in Achaia were prepared a year ago! " Your excitement has made most of them start giving.
9.3: But I am sending these brothers so that our pride in you about this matter will not be empty words. Then you will be prepared, as I was saying all along.
9.4: What if some Macedonians come with me? They might find that you are not prepared. Then we will be ashamed of you because we were so sure! You will be ashamed too.
9.5: Therefore I thought I must ask these brothers to come to you ahead of time. They can help collect the money which you promised long ago. Then as a true gift, it will be ready, not something I forced you to do.
9.6: Remember this: the person who plants only a few seeds will harvest very little, but the man who plants a lot of seeds will gather a great harvest.
9.7: Each person should give as he planned ahead of time in his heart. He should not be sorry that he gave or feels forced to give. God gives Himself to a cheerful giver for his good, expecting nothing in return.
9.8: God is able to give you everything you need. You will always have more than enough to do any good deed well.
9.9: It is like what this Scripture says: " God gives freely to the poor people. His being made right lasts forever. "
9.10: God gives seed to the man who plants, and He will give him bread to eat. God will also give you plenty of spiritual seed and make your being made right grow into a fine harvest.
9.11: He will make you rich in every way so that you may always be generous. This will cause the people to thank God for what came through us.
9.12: You are helping them. It is like a serving ministry which does two things: ( 1 ) it takes care of the needs of the saints; ( 2 ) many people will thank God, like an overflowing river.
9.13: When you help them, it is proof that you put yourself under Christ's authority and that you agree with his Good News. Sharing with them or anyone else shows that you are generous.
9.14: When they pray for you, they will yearn to see you because of God's help in time of need toward you.
9.15: Thank God for His gift — it is too much for words!

10.1: I, Paul, appeal to you through the gentleness and kindness of Christ. ( Some people say that I am humble when I am with you, and that I am bold when I am not with you. )
10.2: Please don't force me to be blunt with you when I come there. I'm quite sure I'll have to challenge those who think we live like people in this world.
10.3: We live in this world but we don't fight like people in this world.
10.4: For our fight we are not using weapons which come from this world. No, our weapons come from God. They are powerful enough to break down strong forts.
10.5: We break down false logic and anything which rises up against what we know is true about God. We capture every thought to make it obey Christ.
10.6: After you have obeyed completely, we are ready to punish anyone who has broken God's law.
10.7: You are looking only at the way things seem to be. If anyone is sure he belongs to Christ, he should think twice about himself. We belong to Christ just as much as he does!
10.8: The Lord gave us authority for building you up, not for tearing you down. Even if I take great pride in our authority, I won't let anyone put us down.
10.9: I don't want you to think I'm trying to scare you with letters.
10.10: Some people say, " Paul's letters are strong and heavy, but when he comes in person, he is weak. He is not a good speaker. "
10.11: Such a person should consider that what we say in letters, while absent, we will prove in deed when we are present!
10.12: We dare not take ourselves too seriously or compare ourselves with those people who pat themselves on the back. When they use themselves to measure by, and compare themselves with themselves, they are foolish.
10.13: But we will not boast beyond what God allows. Instead, we will stay within the limit which God has set for us; that includes you.
10.14: Since you were included, we didn't go too far when we came to you, bringing the Good News about Christ.
10.15: And we are not going too far, when we are proud of the hard work which others have done. As your faith grows, we hope that all of our work among you will increase.
10.16: We want to tell the Good News in areas beyond where you are. We don't want to brag about work done by another person in a different country.
10.17: " If anyone wants to be proud, let him be proud of the Lord. "
10.18: Who is approved? It is not the one who pats himself on the back. It is the one whom the Lord pats on the back!

11.1: I hope you'll put up with a little of my foolishness; you're already doing that.
11.2: I'm jealous for you with a jealousy that comes from God. I promised to present you as a pure virgin to one man — Christ.
11.3: With a clever trick the snake fooled Eve. I'm afraid that your minds might be polluted too. You might leave the simplicity and purity which is in Christ.
11.4: Someone might come preaching about another Jesus who is different from the Jesus we preached to you. You welcomed a different kind of spirit than you received before. How can you put up so easily with a good news that is different from the first one you accepted?
11.5: I think I am just as good as any of those " super " delegates!
11.6: I may use common words but I know what I'm talking about. We have always made this very clear to you.
11.7: I preached the Good News to you at no cost. Did I do wrong when I lowered myself to lift you up?
11.8: I " robbed " other called out people, taking pay from them, to help you.
11.9: While I was with you, when I needed something, I didn't ask any of you for anything. The brothers who came from the Macedonian area filled my needs. I never allowed myself to be a burden to you, and I never will.
11.10: The truth of Christ is in me; I'm proud of this. Nobody in the whole Achaian area can take that away from me!
11.11: Why? Because I do not give myself to you for your good, expecting nothing in return? God knows I do!
11.12: I will continue doing what I am doing. There are some " delegates " who are looking for a chance to brag that they are just like us. I want to cut off any chance of this happening.
11.13: These men are false delegates. They try to look like true delegates of Christ but they are lying about their work.
11.14: And it's no wonder because Satan himself can make himself look like an angel of light.
11.15: So it isn't any big thing when the servants of Satan try to look like servants of those being made right. However, Satan's servants will end up the same way they lived.
11.16: Again I'm saying, no one should think of me as a fool. But if you do, bear with me as you would a fool. Then I can brag a little as fools do.
11.17: When I confidently brag like this, I am not talking as the Lord would have it. I am only talking like a fool.
11.18: Many men are bragging in a human way. So I will brag too.
11.19: You are wise — you gladly put up with fools.
11.20: They make slaves of you. Anyone can take your money. Anyone can take advantage of you. Anyone can treat you as though you are not important. You will let anyone slap your face!
11.21: I'm ashamed to say it but we were too weak to do that. If someone dares to brag, I can too. ( I'm talking foolishly. )
11.22: Are they Hebrews? So am I! Are they sons of Israel? I'm one too! Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I!
11.23: Are they servants of Christ? ( I'm talking like a madman. ) I am more of a servant than they are! I have worked much harder than they have. I've been in jail more often than they have. I have been beaten more times than I can remember. Many times I've been close to dying.
11.24: On five different occasions the Jewish leaders whipped me 3# times.
11.25: Three different times I was beaten with rods. Once they tried to stone me to death. I was on three different ships that wrecked; once I was in the ocean for about 24 hours.
11.26: I'm always traveling. I'm in danger of floods, bandits, Jews, non - Jews, in danger in cities, in deserts, in the ocean, and in danger from false brothers.
11.27: I have worked so very hard. I've often gone without sleep, food, or drink. I have fasted many times. I've been cold and without enough clothes.
11.28: On top of everything else, every day I feel the pressure of my concern for all the called out people.
11.29: When someone is weak, I feel weak too. When someone falls into sin, it really upsets me.
11.30: If I must brag, I will brag about things which show how weak I am.
11.31: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus knows that I am not lying. ( He should be praised forever. )
11.32: The governor under King Aretas was watching the city of Damascus. His men were trying to arrest me.
11.33: But I was lowered in a basket through a window of the city walls. I got away from him.

12.1: It doesn't do any good but I must continue bragging. I will now move on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
12.2: I knew a man in Christ 14 years ago. This man was caught up to the third heaven. I don't know whether he was in his physical body or not — God knows.
12.3: But I know such a person. Again, I don't know if he was in or out of his physical body — God knows.
12.4: This man was caught up to Paradise. He heard things which cannot be re - told; a man is not allowed to tell such things to other men.
12.5: I will brag about such a man. I won't brag about myself — only about my weaknesses.
12.6: Even if I wanted to brag, I would not be foolish because I'm speaking the truth. However, I don't want to do that, or else someone might think more of me than he does when he sees me or hears me in person.
12.7: I've seen some very unusual revelations. God gave me something so that I would not become too proud — a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan. It always tortures me, stopping me from becoming too proud.
12.8: I begged the Lord about this three times. I wanted it to go away from me.
12.9: He said this to me: " My help in time of need is enough for you. Power is made perfect in weakness. " So I will be very happy to brag about my weaknesses so that the power of Christ will rest upon me.
12.10: This is why, for Christ, I can take pleasure in weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and disasters. Because when I am weak, that's when I am really strong.
12.11: I have become a fool but you forced me to do it. You should have been patting me on the back. Even if I am nothing, I'm just as good as any of those " super " delegates.
12.12: The signs of a true delegate have been done among you very patiently — proofs from God, miracles, and powers.
12.13: Did I treat you as if you were less important than the other called out people. No, I didn't burden you. Was that wrong? Please forgive me!
12.14: Listen, I'm ready to visit you for the third time; I won't be a burden. I want you, not your money! Parents should save up to help their children, not the other way around.
12.15: I will gladly spend my money and my energy for your souls. It seems that the more I give myself to you, for your good, expecting nothing in return, the less you give to me, for my good, expecting nothing in return.
12.16: Nevertheless, I've not been a burden to you. But am I a clever man? Did I use a trick to catch you?
12.17: I sent some men to you. Did I use any of them to take advantage of you?
12.18: I begged Titus to go to you and I sent the brother with him. Titus didn't take advantage of you, did he? We lived with the same attitude. We set the same example, didn't we?
12.19: Throughout this letter, have you been thinking that we are trying to defend ourselves to you? You to whom I give myself — we are doing everything to help build you up. We speak in Christ before God.
12.20: When I visit you, I'm afraid you will not be as I want to find you. Then I won't be as you want me to be! You might be jealous, angry, too proud, divided, in confusion, talking against one another, gossiping, or fighting.
12.21: When I visit you again, I'm afraid my God will humble me in front of you. I will cry over many people who have already sinned because they have not changed their hearts about the evil things they have done — indecency, unlawful sexual intercourse, and wild parties.

13.1: This is the third time I am coming to you. If someone is going to accuse me, " The testimony of two or three people " is true.
13.2: When I was with you the last time, I told you ahead of time. Now that I am not with you, I am warning you again: when I come there the next time, I will punish those people who have already sinned and all the others.
13.3: You are looking for proof that Christ speaks through me. Christ is not weak toward you; he is powerful among you.
13.4: Though Christ was nailed to the cross when he was weak, he now lives by the power of God! In Christ we are weak, but we will live with Christ for you by the power of God.
13.5: Test yourselves to find out if you are truly in the faith. Prove it to yourselves. Unless you fail, surely you know that Christ Jesus is among you.
13.6: I hope you know we are not failures.
13.7: We pray to God that you won't do something wrong. We are not trying to look like winners. No, we want you to do what is good, even though it looks as if we failed.
13.8: We can do nothing against the truth; we can only do something for the truth.
13.9: We are happy whenever we are weak while you are strong. And we are praying that you will be mature.
13.10: That is why I write these things while I am away from you. Then when I come, I will not need to be harsh, when I use the authority that the Lord gave me for building up, not for tearing down.
13.11: Finally, brothers, be glad! Try to be united. Warn each other, agree with each other. Be at peace. The God of peace and giving of Himself to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, will be with you.
13.12: Greet one another with a holy kiss of friendship.
13.13: All of the saints here are greeting you.
13.14: May the help in time of need of the Lord Jesus, the giving of God Himself to others - - for their good, expecting nothing in return - - and the sharing of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.

1.1: From Paul, a delegate, and from all of the brothers who are with me. I was not chosen by men to be a delegate; neither was I sent from men. No, it was through Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised Jesus from death. To the called out people in Galatia area:
1.2: [ no verse]
1.3: may God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ give to you help in time of need and peace.
1.4: Jesus gave himself for our sins so that we might escape from the evil in this world. This is what God our Father wanted.
1.5: To God be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
1.6: Not long ago, God called you through His help in time of need that came through Christ, but now I am surprised at you people! You are already turning away toward a different good news.
1.7: There is actually no other true good news. However, some people are disturbing you; they want to distort the Good News of Christ.
1.8: If we ourselves — or even an angel from heaven — tell you a different good news than the true Good News which we told you, then we should be condemned!
1.9: I said this before; I am saying it again: if anyone preaches a good news to you that is different from what you received, let that person be condemned.
1.10: Do you think I'm now trying to win men over? No! God is the One who I am trying to please. Am I trying to please man? If I were, I would not be a slave of Christ.
1.11: Brothers and sisters, I am letting you know that the Good News which I preached to you was not man - made.
1.12: I did not receive the Good News from men; no man taught it to me. No, Jesus Christ revealed the Good News to me.
1.13: You have heard about my past life in the Jewish faith. I violently persecuted God's called - out people. I tried to destroy them.
1.14: In the Jewish faith I was becoming a leader, doing better than most Jews my own age. I tried harder than anyone else to follow the traditions which came from our ancestors.
1.15: But God called me through His help in time of need. Even before I was born, He had special plans for me. God wanted me
1.16: to tell the Good News about Jesus to non - Jewish people. So He revealed His Son to me. I didn't receive advice or get help from any human being.
1.17: I didn't go up right away to see the delegates in Jerusalem. ( These men were delegates before I was. ) No, I went away to Arabia. Afterward I went back to the city of Damascus.
1.18: Three years later, I went up to Jerusalem to meet Peter and for 15 days I stayed with him.
1.19: I saw no other delegates — only Jacob, the brother of the Lord Jesus
1.20: God knows that the things which I am writing to you are true.
1.21: Later I went to the areas of Syria and Cilicia.
1.22: In Judea the called out people in Christ did not know my face.
1.23: They had only heard this about me: " This man used to persecute us but now he is preaching the same faith he once tried to destroy! "
1.24: They were praising God because of me.

2.1: After 14 years, I went with Barnabas up to Jerusalem again, and I took Titus along with me.
2.2: I went up because God showed me that I should go. I went to those men who were the leaders. When we were alone, I explained to them about the Good News which I preach to non - Jewish people so that my past work and the work I do now would not be wasted.
2.3: Titus was with me. Although he was not Jewish, these leaders did not force him to be circumcised.
2.4: It was very important for us to talk because some false brothers had secretly come into our group. Like spies, they came in to find out about the freedom which we have in Christ Jesus. They wanted to make us slaves to them.
2.5: But not for one moment did we give in to what those false brothers wanted! We wanted the truth of the Good News to continue with you.
2.6: Those men who seemed to be important did not change the Good News which I preach. ( It doesn't matter to me whether they were " important " or not; God treats all people alike. )
2.7: Those leaders saw that God had entrusted me with the work of telling the Good News to non - Jewish people, just as God had given Peter the work of telling the Good News to Jews.
2.8: God gave him the power to work as a delegate for Jewish people. God also gave me this power — for people who are not Jews!
2.9: Jacob, Peter, and John seemed to be the main leaders. They knew that God had given me help in time of need. So they accepted Barnabas and me. They said, " We agree. You should go to non - Jewish people. We will go to the Jews. "
2.10: They asked us to do only one thing: to remember to help the Jewish poor people. This was something I really wanted to do anyway.
2.11: Peter came to Antioch in Syria. Because he was wrong, I opposed him.
2.12: This is what happened: when Peter first came to Antioch, he always ate with non - Jewish people. But then some Jewish men were sent from Jacob. When they came, Peter stopped eating with those who were not Jewish and separated himself from them. He was afraid of the Jews who believed that all non - Jewish people must be circumcised.
2.13: Peter was two - faced. The other Jewish believers joined Peter. They were two - faced also. Even Barnabas was influenced by the things which those Jewish believers did.
2.14: I saw what they did. They were not following the truth of the Good News. So I spoke to Peter in such a way that all the other Jews could hear what I said: " Since you are a Jew but do not live as a Jew, why do you now force non - Jewish people to live as Jews? You live like non - Jewish people do. "
2.15: We Jews were not born non - Jewish or sinners; we were born as Jews.
2.16: We know that a person is not made right with God by following the law. Committing one's self to Jesus Christ is what makes a person right with God. So we made a commitment to Christ Jesus because we wanted to be made right with God. We are right with God because we made that commitment, not because of following the law. Nobody will ever be made right by following the law.
2.17: We Jews came to Christ to be made right with God. So it is clear that we were sinners too. Does this mean that Christ makes us sinners? No way!
