2.18: But I would truly be wrong to begin teaching again those things which I gave up.
2.19: I stopped living for the law. I died to the law so that I may now live for God. I died on the cross with Christ.
2.20: So the life which I now live is not really me — it is Christ living in me! I still live in my body, but I live by faith in the Son of God. He is the one who gave himself to me for my good, expecting nothing in return; he sacrificed himself for me.
2.21: This gift is from God and it is very important to me. Because if the law could have made us right with God, then Christ died for nothing!

3.1: You people in Galatia were told very clearly about the death of Jesus Christ on the cross. Why are you so foolish; you let someone trick you!
3.2: Tell me this one thing: how did you receive the Holy Spirit? Did you receive the Spirit by following the law? No! You received the Spirit because you heard the Good News and believed it.
3.3: You began your life in Christ with the Spirit. Are you trying to continue it by your own power? You are so foolish!
3.4: Many things have happened to you. Was it all a waste of time? I hope not!
3.5: Does God give you the Spirit because you follow the law? Does God work miracles among you because you follow the law? It is because you heard the Good News and believed it.
3.6: The Scriptures say the same thing about Abraham: " Abraham believed God and so God declared him a just man. "
3.7: So you should know that the true children of Abraham are those who have faith.
3.8: The Scriptures told what would happen in the future. These writings said that God would make non - Jewish people right — through their faith. The Good News was told to Abraham long ago: " Abraham, God will use you to bless all people on earth. "
3.9: All people who believe are blessed in the same way that Abraham was blessed for his faith;
3.10: but people who depend on following the law to make them right are under condemnation, because it is written, " A person must do everything which is written in the book of the law. If he does not always obey those things, then that person is under condemnation! "
3.11: So it is clear that no person may be made right with God by the law. The Scriptures say, " The person who is right with God by faith will live forever. "
3.12: The law is not based on faith. Instead, the law says, " A person who wants to find life by following these things must do the things the law says. "
3.13: The law put us under condemnation, but Christ took that condemnation away. He changed places with us; he put himself under that condemnation. It is written, " When a person's body is hung on a tree, it shows that the person has been condemned. "
3.14: Christ did this so that God's promised blessing to Abraham could be given to all people. This blessing comes through Christ Jesus. God wanted us to receive the promise of the Holy Spirit through faith.
3.15: Brothers, let me give you an example: a man writes a will. After the will is made legal, no one else may change that will or add to it, and no one can ignore it.
3.16: God made promises to Abraham and his descendant. God did not say " and to your descendants ". That would mean many people. But God said, " and to your descendant ". This means only one person — Christ.
3.17: This is what I mean: God made out a will to Abraham, promising to do the things which He told Abraham. The law came 430 years after the will was made but it did not change God's promise to Abraham.
3.18: Can following the law give us the things which God promised? If we could receive those things by following the law, then it is not God's promise which brings us those things. But God freely gave His blessings to Abraham through the promise He made.
3.19: Therefore what was the purpose of the law? The law was given to show people the difference between right and wrong. It continued until the special descendant of Abraham came. God's promise was about this descendant. The law was given through angels. The angels used Moses as a go - between to give the law to men.
3.20: ( A go - between is not needed when there is only one side; God is only one side. )
3.21: Therefore, does this mean that the law is against God's promises? If there were a law which could give men life, then we could truly be made right by following the law.
3.22: However, this cannot be true because the Scriptures showed that all people are bound by sin so that the promise would be given to people through faith — to those who believe in Jesus Christ!
3.23: Before this faith came, we were all held in check by the law. We had no freedom until God revealed to us the way of faith which was coming.
3.24: So the law was our trainer until Christ came so that we could be made right with God through faith.
3.25: The way of faith has come. Therefore we do not live under law anymore.
3.26: You were all immersed into Christ. So you were all clothed with Christ. You are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
3.28: Now in Christ there is no difference between Jew and non - Jew, between slave and free, between male and female. You are all the same in Christ Jesus.
3.29: You belong to Christ. Therefore you are Abraham's descendants. You receive all of God's blessings because of the promise which God made to Abraham.

4.1: I am telling you this: while the heir is still a child, he is no different from a slave. It does not matter that the heir owns everything
4.2: because, while he is a child, he must obey the people chosen to take care of him until the child reaches the age which his father set.
4.3: It is the same for us. We were once like little children, slaves to the standards of this world
4.4: but, when the right time came, God sent His Son. God's Son was born from a woman; he lived under the law.
4.5: God did this so that He could buy back the freedom of those who were under the law. God's purpose was to make us His children.
4.6: You are God's children. That is why God sent the Spirit of His Son into your hearts. The Spirit cries out, " Daddy, dear Father. "
4.7: So now you are no longer a slave — you are God's child, God's heir.
4.8: In the past you didn't know God. You were slaves to gods which were not real
4.9: but now you know the true God. Actually, it is God who knows you! So why do you turn back to those weak and useless standards which you followed before? Do you want to be slaves to those things again?
4.10: You are still observing special days, months, seasons, and years.
4.11: I am afraid for you. I am afraid that my work for you has been wasted.
4.12: Brothers, I too was once like you. So, please, become like me now. You were very good to me before.
4.13: Do you remember why I came to you the first time? It was because I was sick. That was when I preached the Good News to you.
4.14: My sickness was a burden to you but you didn't look down on me or make me go away. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel from God. You accepted me as if I were Christ Jesus himself!
4.15: Where is your happiness now? I tell you the truth: you would have plucked out your own eyes and given them to me, if that were possible.
4.16: Now have I become your enemy because I am telling you the truth?
4.17: Those people are working hard to persuade you to turn against us but this is not good for you. They want you to follow only them and no one else.
4.18: It is good for people to show interest in you but only if their purpose is always good. This is true whether I am with you or not.
4.19: My little children, again I feel pain for you such as a mother feels when she gives birth to her child. I will feel this until Christ is fully matured in you.
4.20: I wish I could be with you now. Then perhaps I could change the tone of my voice. I don't know what to do with you!
4.21: Since some of you people still want to be under the law of Moses, tell me, won't you listen to what the law says?
4.22: It is written that Abraham had two sons. The mother of one son was a slave woman. The mother of the other son was a free woman.
4.23: Abraham's son from the slave woman was born in the normal human way, but the son from the free woman was born because of the promise which God made to Abraham.
4.24: This true story is an example for us: the two women are like the two covenants between God and men. One covenant is the law which God set up on Mount Sinai. The people who are under this covenant are like slaves. The mother named Hagar is like that covenant.
4.25: So Hagar is like Mount Sinai in Arabia. She represents the city of Jerusalem today. This city is a slave and all of its people are slaves to the law,
4.26: but the heavenly Jerusalem, which is above, is like the free woman. This is our mother.
4.27: It is written: " Be happy, O woman who cannot have children! You never gave birth. Shout and cry out with joy! You never felt the pain of giving birth. The wife whose husband has left her will have more children than the wife who has a husband. "
4.28: One son of Abraham was born in the normal way. Abraham's other son, Isaac, was born by the power of the Spirit because of God's promise. My brothers, you are also children of promise just as Isaac was then. Ishmael persecuted Isaac. It is the same way now.
4.30: But what does the Scripture say? " Throw out the slave woman and her son! The son of the free woman will receive everything that his father has, but the son of the slave woman will receive nothing. "
4.31: Therefore, my brothers, we are not children of the slave woman. We are children of the free woman.

5.1: We have freedom now. Christ made us free. So stand firm; don't turn and go back into slavery.
5.2: Listen! I, Paul, am telling you this: if you allow yourselves to be circumcised, then Christ does you no good.
5.3: Again I warn every man: if you allow yourselves to be circumcised, then you must follow the entire law.
5.4: If you try to be made right with God through the law, then you are cut off from Christ — you have fallen from help in time of need!
5.5: But we have a true hope; we wait for it eagerly. We will be made right with God through the Spirit. How? By faith.
5.6: When a person is in Christ Jesus, it does not matter whether he is circumcised or not. The only thing which is important is faith — the kind of faith which works through giving yourself to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return.
5.7: You were running a good race. You were obeying the truth. Who persuaded you to stop?
5.8: That persuasion does not come from God who called you.
5.9: Be careful! " Just a little yeast makes the whole batch of dough rise. "
5.10: Somebody is disturbing you with different ideas. Whoever that person is, he will certainly be punished. I trust in the Lord that you will not believe those ideas.
5.11: Brothers, I still don't preach that people must be circumcised. If I did, why am I still being persecuted? Then the embarrassment of the cross would be neutralized.
5.12: I wish those people who are upsetting you would add castration to their circumcision!
5.13: Brothers, although God called you to be free, don't use your freedom as an excuse to do all of the things which your physical body wants. Instead, give yourselves to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return.
5.14: The entire law is made complete in this one command: " Give yourself to your neighbor for his good, expecting nothing in return, the same way you give to yourself. "
5.15: Be careful! If you continue hurting each other and tearing each other apart, you might completely destroy one another!
5.16: So I tell you: live by following the Spirit. Then you won't do the selfish and evil things which you want in your human nature.
5.17: The human nature wants things which are against the Spirit. The Spirit wants things which are against our human nature. These oppose each other. Because of this, you cannot do the things that you really intend to do.
5.18: But if you let the Spirit lead you, then you are not under the law.
5.19: Human nature does things which are wrong. These are clear: committing unlawful sexual intercourse, not being pure, having orgies,
5.20: worshipping false gods, practicing witchcraft, hating people, making trouble, being jealous, becoming too angry, being selfish, making people angry with each other, causing divisions,
5.21: envying others, murdering, getting drunk, having wild parties, and other such things. I warn you now as I warned you before: the people who do these things will not inherit God's kingdom.
5.22: But the Spirit produces: giving to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
5.23: gentleness, self - control. There is no law against things such as these.
5.24: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have nailed their own human nature to crosses, along with its feelings and selfish desires.
5.25: Since we get life from the Spirit, we should follow the Spirit.
5.26: We must not be conceited or make trouble for each other. Neither should we be jealous of one another.

6.1: Brothers, a person in your called out group might fall into a particular sin. You people who are spiritual should repair such a person with a gentle spirit. But watch yourself! You also might be tempted to sin.
6.2: Help carry each other's burdens. In this way you truly satisfy the " law " of Christ.
6.3: If someone thinks that he is important ( when he really is not ), he is only fooling himself.
6.4: A person should not compare himself with someone else. Each person should judge his own actions. Then he may take pride in what he himself has done.
6.5: Each person must shoulder his own responsibility.
6.6: The one who is learning about God's message should share all of the good things he has with the one who is teaching him.
6.7: Don't be fooled! You cannot mock God. A person harvests only the things which he plants.
6.8: If a person lives to satisfy his human nature, then his selfish ways will bring eternal death to him. But if a person lives to please the Spirit, he will receive eternal life from the Spirit.
6.9: We must never become tired of doing good. We will receive our harvest of eternal life at the right time. We must never give up!
6.10: Therefore when we have the chance to do good to people, we should do it, but we should give special attention to those who are within the family of believers of the faith.
6.11: I am writing this myself; look at the large letters I am using!
6.12: Some men are trying to force you to be circumcised. They do these things so that the Jewish people will accept them, fearing they will be persecuted if they follow only the cross of Christ.
6.13: These men who are circumcised do not obey the law themselves, but they want you to be circumcised so that they may brag about your flesh.
6.14: I hope that I will never brag about something like that! The cross of our Lord Jesus Christ is my only reason for bragging. Through the cross of Jesus my world has died and I died to the world.
6.15: For in Christ Jesus it does not matter whether a person is circumcised or uncircumcised. All that is important is being a new creation.
6.16: Peace and mercy to the people who follow this rule — to God's Israel.
6.17: So don't give me further trouble. I carry scars on my body which show that I belong to Jesus.
6.18: Brothers, may the help in time of need of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

1.1: From Paul. God wanted me to be a delegate of Christ Jesus. To the saints who live in the city of Ephesus, those who are faithful to Christ Jesus.
1.2: May help in time of need and peace come to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: Praise God! He is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. In Christ, God blessed us with every spiritual blessing in heaven.
1.4: In Christ, God chose us before the world began. He wanted us to be holy and spotless before Him in giving ourselves to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return.
1.5: God planned long ago that we become His own sons through Jesus Christ. This would please God; it is what He wanted.
1.6: We praise God for His glorious help in time of need that He gave us in His son. God gives Himself to His son, expecting nothing in return.
1.7: We have something in Christ - his blood has set us free. We have the forgiveness of sins! God's help in time of need is so rich!
1.8: It overwhelms us with all kinds of wisdom and understanding.
1.9: To us God made clear the secret of what He wanted. He was pleased to plan this in Christ.
1.10: God's plan is to bring everything together in Christ - in heaven and on earth - under Christ as Head. When the right time arrives, He will do this.
1.11: We were chosen in Christ. God planned this long ago for His purpose. He works out everything. God decides what He wants.
1.12: We were the first to pin our hopes on Christ. This happened so that we could become praise to God's glory.
1.13: You are in Christ too. You heard the true message, the Good News about your deliverance from sin. After you believed, you were sealed in Christ with the Holy Spirit whom God promised.
1.14: The Spirit is the guarantee that we will receive the inheritance. God will set His own people free for the praise of His glory.
1.15: I have heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus Christ and the giving to all the saints, for their good, expecting nothing in return.
1.16: So I never stop thanking God for you. I always mention you in my prayers.
1.17: I want the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, to give you insight and a wise spirit. Then you will know Him better.
1.18: I pray that the eyes of your heart will receive light. Then you will know the meaning of the hope of God's invitation. You will know the riches of His glorious inheritance among the saints.
1.19: You will know God's great power which is available to us who believe. It is like the exercising of His mighty strength
1.20: when He raised Christ from death and put him at His own right side in theheavenly world.
1.21: There Christ is far above any ruler, authority, power, lord or title which can be given, not only in this world but also in the next world.
1.22: God put everything under Christ's feet. God appointed him to be the Head over all things among the called out people.
1.23: This is Christ's body. It is the totality of Christ; he completes everything everywhere.

2.1: You were spiritually dead in your sins and violations.
2.2: In the past you lived in those things. You followed the evil ways of this world and the ruler of the power of the air - that evil spirit who is now working in those who disobey God.
2.3: We all used to live among people like that, with the evil desires in our human nature. We satisfied the impulses of our bodies and minds. We were like all other people - naturally deserving punishment.
2.4: However, God was rich in mercy because of His great giving to us, for our good, expecting nothing in return, which He had for us.
2.5: While we were spiritually dead in sins, God made us alive with Christ. ( You have been saved by God's help in time of need. )
2.6: And God raised us from spiritual death and seated us in the heavenly world with Christ Jesus.
2.7: God wanted to show the superior riches of His help in time of need for all time. He did this by using Jesus to be kind to us.
2.8: You have been saved by God's help in time of need through faith. Deliverance from sin does not come from you; it is God's gift.
2.9: It does not come from human effort. If that were true, someone could brag about earning it.
2.10: We are what God made. In Christ Jesus we have been created for doing good deeds. God prepared these good deeds long ago so that we could live by them.
2.11: Physically you are not Jewish. Those who have been physically circumcised called you " the uncircumcised ". Do you remember?
2.12: At that time you were without Christ. You were foreigners. You could not be part of Israel. You were strangers to the covenants of God's promise. You had no hope. You were in the world without God.
2.13: You used to be far away but now, in Christ Jesus, you have come near. This was made possible by the blood of Christ.
2.14: Christ himself is our peace. He has made Jews and non - Jews one. He used his own body to break down the barrier of hate which separated them.
2.15: Christ canceled the law which had commands in strict orders. He wanted to create one new man from two, making peace between them.
2.16: Then he could make them friends of God with one body through the cross. He used the cross to kill the hate.
2.17: When Jesus came, " He preached peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near. "
2.18: Because through Christ, both Jews and non - Jews have a way to get to the Father - by one Spirit!
2.19: So you are not strangers and visitors anymore. Instead, you are co - citizens with the saints and members of God's family.
2.20: You have been built on the foundation of the delegates and prophets. Christ Jesus is its most important stone.
2.21: The whole building is joined together in Christ. It becomes a holy temple sanctuary in the Lord Jesus.
2.22: In Christ you are being built up for God too, so that He may live in you by His Spirit.

3.1: This is why I, Paul, am Christ Jesus' prisoner for you non - Jews.
3.2: Surely you have heard about the plan of God's help in time of need which was given to me for you.
3.3: God used a revelation to make this secret clear. ( I wrote a little bit about it before. )
3.4: As you read this, you will be able to grasp my understanding of the secret of Christ.
3.5: People of other generations were not told this, but now it has been revealed to God's holy delegates and prophets by His Spirit:
3.6: Jewish people and non - Jewish people are now partners; they will inherit together. And through the Good News, they share God's promise in Christ Jesus.
3.7: I became a minister of this Good News. God's free help in time of need was given to me by exercising His power.
3.8: This help in time of need was given to me even though I am the least important of all the saints. God wanted to preach the riches without limit of Christ to non - Jewish people.
3.9: He wanted to teach everyone about the meaning of the secret plan. It was hidden in God a long, long time ago. ( He created everything. )
3.10: Why was it hidden? So that, through the called out people, His many kinds of wisdom could be made clear to rulers and powers in the heavenly world.
3.11: This happened for God's eternal purpose which He accomplished in Christ Jesus, our Lord.
3.12: In Christ and by believing in Christ, we have boldness and confidence to come near to God.
3.13: So I am asking you not to give up. I am suffering for you; this is glory for you.
3.14: This is why I bow down to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
3.15: Every family in heaven and on earth gets its name from the Father.
3.16: I pray that God will use His Spirit to give you power from the riches of His glory to make your inner being strong.
3.17: Then, through believing in Christ, he will live in your hearts. You will have your roots and foundation in giving yourselves to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return.
3.18: Then you and all of the saints will be able to completely understand the meaning of Christ's giving to others for their good, expecting nothing in return - how wide it is, how long it is, how high it is, and how deep it is. It goes beyond knowing, but you will know it. Then you will be filled with the totality of God.
3.20: Glory to God! He is able to do so much more than we can think of or ask for. God uses the power that is working in us.
3.21: Glory to God, among all the called out people He has, and to Christ Jesus for all generations forever and ever. Amen.

4.1: So I, the prisoner in the Lord Jesus, beg you to live as though you were worthy of God's invitation.
4.2: Be completely humble, gentle, and patient. Put up with one another by giving yourselves to one another, for his good, expecting nothing in return.
4.3: Try hard to keep the Spirit's unity; use peace to bind it together.
4.4: There is one body and one Spirit. You were called to one hope when God called you.
4.5: There is one Lord Jesus. There is one faith. There is one immersion.
4.6: There is one God. He is the Father of everyone. God is above everything, through everything, and in everything.
4.7: Each one of us has received God's help in time of need. Christ gave it by measure.
4.8: The Scripture says: " When he went up high, he captured everything. He gave gifts to men. "
4.9: ( When it says " he went up ", it could only mean that Christ came down to the lower parts of the earth.
4.10: The one who came down is the same one who went up - above all the heavens. He wanted to fill the universe. )
4.11: Christ appointed delegates, prophets, preachers, spiritual shepherds, and teachers
4.12: to prepare the saints for a ministry of service, for building up the body of Christ.
4.13: How long? Until we are all together. We must be united in our faith and knowledge of the Son of God. We must become like a full - grown man, reaching for the greatest potential of Christ.
4.14: Then we will not be little children anymore. The waves will not throw us back and forth. We won't be blown away by the winds of false teaching which clever men invent to trick people into following error.
4.15: When we speak the truth in giving ourselves to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, we will grow up into Christ in every way. He is the Head.
4.16: He is the source. The whole body is joined and held together with each joint that helps it. The whole body grows by giving itself to others and builds itself in us. Each part does its job.
4.17: I am telling the truth in the Lord Jesus: live no longer as the people of the world live. Their thinking is worthless.
4.18: Their minds have become dark. The life of God is foreign to them. They don't know about it because their hearts are stubborn.
4.19: When they lost all feeling of shame, they gave themselves over to sensuality, so that they could try every kind of unclean sex, wanting more and more of such things.
4.20: However, this is not the way you learned about Christ.
4.21: You heard about him. Then you were taught in him. ( The truth is in Jesus. )
4.22: You were taught to put away your old way of living. It will destroy you. Those evil desires can fool you.
4.23: You were taught to develop a new way of thinking.
4.24: You were taught to be clothed with a new personality like that of God. It was created with true justice and holiness.
4.25: Therefore put away lying. Let each one speak the truth to the other person. We are all parts of each other.
4.26: You are allowed to become angry, but don't sin. And don't let any day end without getting rid of your angry feelings.
4.27: Don't give the devil a chance.
4.28: The person who steals must not steal anymore. Instead, he must work hard, using his own hands to do good, so that he may have something to share with someone who needs it.
4.29: Don't let any mean word come out of your mouth. Instead, say something good to build up what is missing. Then it will be a blessing to those who hear it.
4.30: Don't make God's Holy Spirit sad. You were sealed with the Spirit for the Day of freedom.
4.31: May all bitterness, anger, grudges, yelling, and cursing - every kind of evil - be taken away from you.
4.32: Have tender feelings and be kind to one another. Forgive one another just as God, in Christ, forgave you.

5.1: Follow God, as children to whom He has given Himself, for their good.
5.2: Live a life of giving yourselves to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, just as Christ gave himself to us, for our good, expecting nothing in return. He gave himself for us. He was an offering and a sacrifice that smells sweet to God.
5.3: No type of impurity, unlawful sexual intercourse, or greed should be mentioned among you. That is not proper for saints.
5.4: You should not use obscene or foolish words. Dirty jokes are out of line. Instead, you should be thankful.
5.5: You can be sure of this one thing: no sexual sinner, no immoral or greedy person - he is the same as one who worships a false god - will have a share in the kingdom of Christ and God.
5.6: Don't let anyone fool you with empty words. This is why God's punishment is coming against people who will not obey.
5.7: So don't take part in these things with them.
5.8: In the past you were in darkness but now you are in light, in the Lord Jesus. Live like children of light
5.9: because the light produces all kinds of goodness, being made right, and truth.
5.10: Test everything to see if it would please the Lord.
5.11: Don't share in those deeds of darkness. They are not productive. Instead, prove that they are wrong.
5.12: The things which happen in secret are too shameful to talk about.
5.13: Everything that the light exposes will become clear.
5.14: Light makes everything clear. This song says: " Get up, you sleeper! Rise from death! and Christ will shine on you. "
5.15: Therefore, be very careful how you live. Don't live like foolish people; live like wise people.
5.16: Take advantage of every opportunity because these are evil times.
5.17: This is why you should not be fools. Instead, try to understand what the Lord wants.
5.18: Don't get drunk with wine; this leads to wildness. No, be filled with the Spirit.
5.19: Use psalms, songs of praise, and spiritual songs to talk to one another. Strum your heart and sing to the Lord.
5.20: Always thank God the Father for everything with the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
5.21: Submit yourselves to each other to show awesome respect for Christ.
5.22: Wives, you must subject yourselves to your own husbands as you do for the Lord.
5.23: A husband is to be the leader of his wife like Christ is the leader of the called out people. He is the savior of the body.
5.24: As Christ's people subject themselves to him, wives should subject themselves to their husbands in everything.
5.25: Husbands, give yourselves to your wives, for their good, expecting nothing in return, as Christ gave himself to those called out people, for their good, expecting nothing in return. He gave his life for them.
5.26: He used a washing of water through the word to make God's people holy.
5.27: He wanted to give to himself a glorious group of called out people that does not have stain or wrinkle or any such thing. Instead, he wanted them to be holy and spotless.
5.28: Husbands ought to give themselves to their wives, for their good, expecting nothing in return, as they do to their own bodies. The man who gives himself to his wife, for her good, expecting nothing in return, gives to himself, for his good.
5.29: No man ever hated his own flesh. No, he feeds it and takes care of it. Christ does the same thing for his called out people.
5.30: We are members of Christ's body.
5.31: The Scripture says: " This is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife. The husband and wife will become one flesh. "
5.32: This is a great secret. ( I am talking about the relationship between Christ and the called out people. )
5.33: Each one of you must give himself to his wife, for her good, expecting nothing in return, just as he gives to himself. And each wife must show respect for her husband.

6.1: Children in the Lord, obey your parents because this is right.
6.2: The first command with a promise is this: " You must show respect for your father and mother.
6.3: Then you will be fine. You will live a long time on the earth. "
6.4: Fathers, don't push your children to the point of rage. Instead, take care of them, using the Lord's warning and discipline.
6.5: Slaves, obey your human masters with awesome respect and trembling but sincerely, just as you would obey Christ.
6.6: Don't be a slave only while your master is looking, like slaves who only want to please men. Instead, from your inner being, do what God wants - as slaves of Christ.
6.7: Serve cheerfully, as if it were for the Lord Jesus and not for men.
6.8: Each one of you knows that if a slave or free man does something good, the Lord Jesus will give him a reward for doing that.
6.9: Masters, treat your slaves the same way. Don't try to scare them. You know that the Lord Jesus is in heaven. He is their Lord and your Lord. God treats everyone the same.
6.10: Last of all, be clothed with the Lord Jesus and the power of his strength.
6.11: Put on all of God's armor. Then you will be able to stand against the evil tricks of the devil.
6.12: Our fight is not against men. No, it is against rulers, against authorities, against world powers of this darkness, and against evil spiritual beings in the heavenly world.
6.13: This is why you must take up all of God's armor. Then when the time for battle comes, you will be able to resist; and after you have fought your best, you will stand.
6.14: So stand firm, using truth as a belt around your waist. Put on the chest plate of being made right.
6.15: With shoes on your feet, be ready to tell the Good News about peace.
6.16: And along with everything else, take up faith for a shield. With this, you will be able to put out all the burning arrows of the evil one.
6.17: Take the helmet of deliverance from sin; and take the sword of the Spirit. ( This is the word of God. )
6.18: Pray with the Spirit at all times. Use all kinds of prayers and requests. Be on guard! Always pray for all the saints.
6.19: Pray for me too! Then, when I open my mouth to speak, the message will be given to me. With boldness I will make clear the secret of the Good News.
6.20: I am a representative in chains for this good news. Pray that I will speak boldly about it as I should.
6.21: Tychicus, my dear brother and faithful servant in the Lord Jesus, will tell you all about things here. Then you will know what is happening to me and what I am doing.
6.22: That is why I sent him to you. Then you will learn about how we are. He will encourage your hearts.
6.23: Peace to the brothers there and the giving of ourselves to you — for your good, expecting nothing in return —with faith from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
6.24: May help in time of need, that never stops, be with all those people who give themselves to our Lord Jesus Christ, for his good, expecting nothing in return.

1.1: From Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus. To all of the saints - including the overseers and servants - in Christ Jesus, who live in the city of Philippi.
1.2: May help in time of need and peace come to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: Every time I think of you, I thank my God.
1.4: In all prayers for all of you, I always pray with joy.
1.5: You shared in preaching the Good News from the very first day until now.
1.6: I feel sure of this one thing: the One who began a good work among you will continue it until it is finished, when Christ Jesus comes.
1.7: I have you in my heart. So it is right for me to feel like this about all of you. Whether I am in chains or giving a defense of the Good News and confirming it, all of you share with me in this help in time of need.
1.8: My God knows that I am telling the truth: with the tender feelings of Christ Jesus I yearn for all of you.
1.9: This is what I am praying for: I want your giving to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, to overflow more and more, with a more full knowledge and all insight.
1.10: Then you will be able to test what is best so you will be pure and without guilt when Christ comes.
1.11: You will be filled with what being made right produces through Jesus Christ for the glory and praise of God.
1.12: Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that the things which have happened to me have really helped the Good News to go forward.
1.13: So the fact that I am in chains for the cause of Christ has become clear to the whole palace guard and to all the other soldiers.
1.14: And, because of my chains, most of the brothers in the Lord have become more confident. They dare to speak the message with almost no fear.
1.15: Some people are preaching Christ with motives of jealousy and bickering, but others preach with a good heart.
1.16: They do it in giving themselves to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, knowing that I am ready to defend the Good News.
1.17: But some preach Christ from selfish ambition, not sincerely. They think they can cause trouble for me while I am in prison.
1.18: So what? The only important thing is that Christ is being preached! I am happy about this, whether it comes from true or false motives. Yes, and I will be happy in the future too,
1.19: because I know I will be delivered. You are praying and the Spirit of Jesus Christ is also helping.
1.20: I am hoping and expecting that I will never be ashamed. Instead, may I have all courage so that my body will be used to make Christ more important now and always, whether I am alive or whether I die.
1.21: Because to me living is Christ, and dying is even better.
1.22: But suppose I go on living in my body? This could mean productive work. Which should I choose? I don't know.
1.23: I am torn between living and dying. I have a strong desire to die and be with Christ. That would be so much better for me,
1.24: but staying alive is more important for your sakes.
1.25: Being sure of this, I now know that I will stay on. I will continue with all of you so that you may grow and have a happy faith.
1.26: Then when I come to you again, you will be proud of me and this will overflow in Christ Jesus.
1.27: Live as though you were worthy of the Good News. I might come and visit you but if I don't get there, I want to hear good things about you - that you stand firm with one spirit, with one heart, fighting for the faith of the Good News.
1.28: Don't let those who are against you scare you. This will show them that they will lose but you will be saved. This comes from God.
1.29: You not only have the privilege of believing in Christ, but also the privilege of suffering for Christ.
1.30: You saw the struggle I have had and you hear about the one I'm having now. Now you have the same thing.

2.1: Are you encouraged in Christ? Are you comforted by his giving to you, for your good, expecting nothing in return? Do you share with the Spirit? Do you have any tender feelings or compassion for others?
2.2: Make me truly happy; I want you to agree among yourselves and to have the same giving for one another, for their good, expecting nothing in return. Be united in your life and mind.
2.3: Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceited pride. Instead, humbly treat others better than yourselves.
2.4: Look for what is important to others, not just what is important to you.
2.5: Have the same attitude among you that Christ Jesus had:
2.6: though Christ was divine by nature, he did not think that being equal with God was something to be grasped.
2.7: Instead, he emptied himself, taking on the very nature of a slave. He became like human beings appearing in human form.
2.8: He humbled himself. He obeyed though it meant dying, even dying on a cross!
2.9: So God made him the most important. God gave him a name that is above every name.
2.10: God wanted every knee to bow when the name of Jesus is mentioned; those in the heavenly world, on earth, and under the earth.
2.11: And every tongue will confess that " Jesus Christ is Lord " for the glory of God the Father.
2.12: So - you to whom I give myself - you have always obeyed when I was with you, but it is even more important that you obey while I am gone. Work out your own deliverance from sin with awesome respect and trembling,
2.13: because God is the One who is working in you. How? He causes you to want to do what pleases Him.
2.14: Do everything without complaining or arguing about it.
2.15: Then you will be pure and innocent. You will be God's children, spotless in the middle of a dishonest, evil generation of people. You will shine among them like stars in the universe.
2.16: Hold out the message of life. Then when Christ comes, I can boast that my past work was not wasted, or the work I do now either.
2.17: No, even if it is true that I am poured out like a drink offering for the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad. I am happy for all of you.
2.18: You should be happy for the same reason. Be happy with me!
2.19: In the Lord Jesus, I hope to send Timothy to you soon. Then I will be cheered up when I find out about what is happening with you.
2.20: Timothy is the only one who has the same attitude I have. He really cares about what happens to you.
2.21: Everyone else looks out for himself - not for the things of Jesus Christ -
2.22: but you know that Timothy has passed the test. Timothy has served with me for the Good News as a son working for his father.
2.23: So I hope to send him whenever I see how things go here.
2.24: I am sure in the Lord that I will come soon too.
2.25: But I think I need to send back Epaphroditus, my brother, co - worker, and fellow - soldier. He is your messenger and he has helped me with whatever I needed.
2.26: He yearns for all of you. He feels depressed because you heard that he was sick.
2.27: He was so sick that he almost died! However, God gave him mercy, and not just him but me too! I would have become more and more sad.
2.28: So I am very eager to send Epaphroditus. When you see him again, you will be happy. And I will not feel so sad.
2.29: Welcome him in the Lord with great joy. Give glory to men like him.
2.30: For Christ's work, Epaphroditus almost died. He risked his life to make up for what was missing in your service to me.

3.1: Last of all, my brothers, be happy in the Lord. It does not bother me to write the same things to you again inasmuch as it is safety for you.
3.2: Watch out for dogs. Watch out for men who do evil. Watch out for mutilators.
3.3: We are the true circumcision, not they. We worship in God's Spirit. We boast in Christ Jesus. Our trust is not based on flesh!
3.4: I could trust in flesh. If someone thinks he can trust in the flesh, I have more reason to do that:
3.5: I was circumcised eight days after I was born. I come from the people of Israel. I am from the tribe of Benjamin. My Hebrew parents gave me a Hebrew education. I learned the law as a Pharisee.
3.6: I tried so hard that I even persecuted the called out people. I had the law " of being made right " - I felt no guilt.
3.7: The things which I used to think were good for me are now worthless to me because of Christ.
3.8: Not only that, I think everything is worthless except what is so much more valuable - knowing Christ Jesus, my Lord. I have thrown everything else away because of him. It's all worthless! I want to have Christ.
3.9: I want to be in him, not having " my " right way ( the kind that comes from the law ) but having the " being made right " which comes through believing in Christ ( the kind of " being made right " which comes from God based on faith ).
3.10: Then I will know Christ and the power he had when he came back to life. I want to share in Christ's suffering and become like him when he died, that
3.11: somehow I may reach the resurrection from death.
3.12: I have not yet made the resurrection my own. And I have not already become perfect but I press on to win what Christ Jesus won for me.
3.13: Brothers, I don't think I have already won it, but I'm doing one thing: I am reaching out - forgetting about what is behind me.
3.14: I am pressing on toward the goal to win the prize to which God called me. It is above in Christ Jesus.
3.15: Those who are spiritually mature will think like this but if you think in a different way, God will reveal this to you.
3.16: However, we should live by the same standard we have followed until now.
3.17: Brothers, be like me! We gave you a good example. Pay attention to the people who follow it.
3.18: Because - as I was often telling you and I am now saying this with tears - many people are living as enemies of the cross of Christ!
3.19: They will end up in hell. Their god is their stomach. Their glory is in their shame. They think only about earthly things,
3.20: but we are citizens of heaven. We are expecting the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, to come from heaven.
3.21: Using the power that allows him to put everything under his control, Christ will change our wretched bodies to be like his glorious body.

4.1: So, my brothers - you to whom I give myself - I yearn for you. You are my crown and joy. Stand fast in the Lord!
4.2: Euodia and Syntyche, I beg you, agree with one another in the Lord.
4.3: Yes, I am asking you, faithful Syzygus, help these women. They both fought next to me for the Good News. Clement and my other co - workers did too. Their names are in the Book of Life.
4.4: Rejoice in the Lord. Again I say, rejoice!
4.5: Show a gentle spirit to everyone. The Lord is near.
4.6: Don't worry about anything. Instead, let God know what you are asking for in prayer. Tell Him all about what you want. And be thankful.
4.7: God's peace, which goes far beyond all human understanding, will guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.
4.8: Finally, brothers, think about good things and things that will bring praise - whatever is true, noble, right, pure, lovely, and honorable.
4.9: Practice the things you learned from me, received from me, heard from me, or saw in me. The God of peace will be with you.
4.10: I am very happy in the Lord that, after all this time, you are still concerned about me. You were always concerned but you didn't have the chance to give.
4.11: I am not saying this because I need something now. I have learned to be satisfied in any situation.
4.12: I know what it is to go without and I know what it is to have plenty. At all times I have learned the secret of being full or going hungry, of having plenty or very little.
4.13: I can do anything - by the One who gives me the power.
4.14: But it was good of you to share with me in my troubles.
4.15: When I left the Macedonian area after the Good News first came to them, not one called out group of people helped ( in giving or receiving things ). You were the only ones - and you Philippians know this!
4.16: Even while I was in the city of Thessalonica, time and again when I needed help, you sent something to me.
4.17: I am not looking for gifts. I only want to see " credit " added to your account.
4.18: I have gotten everything; it is more than enough. I have plenty since I received the things you sent with Epaphroditus. It is an acceptable sacrifice, a sweet smell that pleases God.
4.19: My God will fill all of your needs with His wealth in glory in Christ Jesus.
4.20: Give glory to our God and Father forever and ever. Amen.
4.21: Greet every holy person in Christ Jesus. The brothers here with me send you their greetings.
4.22: All of the saints here greet you, especially those in Caesar's household.
4.23: May the help in time of need of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

1.1: From Paul ( God wanted me to be a delegate of Christ Jesus. ) and from Timothy, our brother.
1.2: To the saints and faithful brothers and sisters in Christ in the city of Colossae. May help in time of need and peace come to you from God our Father.
1.3: For you we thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. ( We are always praying. )
1.4: We have heard about your faith in Christ Jesus and the giving to the saints, for their good, expecting nothing in return,
1.5: because of the hope that is hidden away in heaven for you. You heard about this hope long ago in the true message - the Good News.
1.6: It came to you as it is now all over the world. It is producing fruit and increasing its influence. It has been doing the same thing among you ever since you first heard and learned about God's help in time of need in the truth.
1.7: You learned it from Epaphras, our co - slave, to whom I give myself. He is a faithful slave of Christ for us.
1.8: He has also told us about your giving to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, in the Spirit.
1.9: Since the day we heard about you, we haven't stopped praying for you. We ask that you may be filled with the knowledge of what God wants, with all kinds of wisdom and spiritual understanding.
1.10: We want you to live as if you were worthy of the Lord Jesus. Please him in every way. Produce the fruit of good deeds. Grow in your knowledge of God.
1.11: Be strong! Have all the strength of His glorious power. Then you will be able to endure anything. You will learn patience with joy.
1.12: Give thanks to the Father who entitled you to have a part of what saints will receive. The saints are in the light.
1.13: He rescued us from the power of darkness and moved us into the kingdom of His Son to whom He gave Himself.
1.14: We have freedom in Christ through his blood: the forgiveness of sins.
1.15: Christ is the image of the unseen God. Christ is the firstborn of all of the creation
1.16: because in Christ everything was created - everything in the heavenly world and everything on earth, things that can be seen and things which cannot be seen; thrones, lords, rulers, and powers. Everything was created through Christ and for Christ.
1.17: Christ is before everything, and everything holds together in Christ.
1.18: Christ is the Head of the body, the called out people. Christ is the Source, the first one to rise from death so that he could be first in everything
1.19: because it pleased God to have the totality live in Christ
1.20: and, through Christ, to bring everything back to Him. God used the blood of the cross of Christ to make peace with everything on earth and everything in the heavenly world.
1.21: In the past you did evil things. You were strangers and enemies of God in your mind.
1.22: But now Christ's physical body has brought you back to God through death. He wanted to present you holy, spotless, and without guilt before Him.
1.23: But you must stay rooted and grounded in the faith. Don't be moved away from the hope of the Good News that you heard. It was preached to every person under heaven. I, Paul, am a minister of this Good News.
1.24: I am happy even though I am now suffering for you. Christ did not finish the suffering. I am completing the suffering which was left over. I am doing this in my body for Christ's body, the called out people.
1.25: I was made a minister of that people by God's plan which was given to me for your sakes. God wanted me to complete His message.
1.26: This is the secret that was kept hidden from generations and for ages but now it has been made clear to God's saints.
1.27: God wanted them to make clear the meaning of the glorious riches of this secret in people who are not Jewish. The secret is - Christ in you; he is the hope of glory.
1.28: We preach Christ. We use every kind of wisdom to teach and warn every person. We want to present every person to God perfect in Christ.
1.29: This is what I am working for. Using all the energy that he exercises so powerfully in me, I am struggling to do this.

2.1: I want you to know how hard I have fought for you and for the people of the town of Laodicea and for all of those who have not met me face to face.
2.2: Then their hearts will be encouraged and bound together with giving to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return. They will have all the riches of complete understanding, knowing God's secret - Christ.
2.3: All of the treasures and hidden wisdom are found in Christ.
2.4: I am telling this so that no one will fool you with false reasonings.
2.5: Even though I am physically not there with you, I am with you in spirit. It makes me feel happy when I see how orderly and how strong your faith in Christ is.
2.6: So continue living in Christ, just as you did when you accepted Christ Jesus as Lord.
2.7: Be rooted and built up in him. Be firm in faith, as you were taught. Overflow with thankfulness.
2.8: Be careful! Don't let anyone capture you with philosophy or misleading theories that can fool you. These come from human tradition and worldly standards, not from Christ!
2.9: The totality of divinity lives embodied in Christ.
2.10: You are completed in Christ. He is above every ruler and authority.
2.11: In Christ you were circumcised with a non - human circumcision. With Christ's circumcision you stripped away sins of the human nature.
2.12: You were buried with Christ by immersion. You were also raised with Christ through believing in the power of God who raised Christ from death.
2.13: When you were spiritually dead in your sins and your human nature was not circumcised, God brought you back to life with Christ. He forgave all of our sins.
2.14: God wiped away the written code with its strict orders. It was negative; it was against us. He took it out of the way. He nailed it to his cross.
2.15: After God stripped away the power of the rulers and authorities, He showed this openly, using the cross to show His victory over them.
2.16: So don't let anyone condemn you for what you eat or drink, or a religious festival, or the new moon holiday, or Sabbaths.
2.17: These are only a shadow of the future; Christ is real.
2.18: Don't let anyone who likes to act " humble " and to worship angels disqualify you from the race. He talks in detail about what he has " seen ". His unspiritual mind makes him boastful for no real reason.
2.19: He is not holding onto the Head. The whole body grows the way God made it grow, held together by its joints and ligaments, getting its support from the head.
2.20: If you truly died with Christ, leaving behind the standards of the world, why are you living as if you were still in the world? You are making strict rules:
2.21: " Don't handle it! "; " Don't taste this! "; " Don't touch that! "
2.22: None of these things will last after they have been used for a while. They are human commands and teachings.
2.23: These things look like there is wisdom behind them. They have forced worship, false humility, and harsh treatment of the human body but they don't help control physical desires at all!

3.1: So since you were raised with Christ, search for things that are above, where Christ is sitting at God's right side.
3.2: Think about things that are above, not things on the earth.
3.3: Since you have died, your life has been hidden away with Christ in God.
3.4: When Christ ( your life ) appears, then you will appear with him in glory too.
3.5: So kill the earthly parts: unlawful sexual intercourse, that which is dirty, lust, evil desire, and greed. ( Greed is the same thing as worshipping a false god. )
3.6: Because of these things, God's punishment will come upon people who will not obey.
3.7: In the past you used to live that way!
3.8: But now you must put away all of those things: anger, grudges, feelings of hate, cursing, and filthy words.
3.9: Do not lie to one another. Strip away that old personality along with its habits.
3.10: Put on the new personality, which is being renewed, by learning to be like the image of its Creator.
3.11: Here there are no Greeks or Jews, no circumcision or uncircumcision, no foreigners, no Scythians, no slaves or free men. Christ is everything and in everything.
3.12: So clothe yourselves with tender feelings, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience like God's chosen - saints to whom He gives Himself, for your good, expecting nothing in return.
3.13: Put up with one another. If someone has a problem with somebody else, forgive each other as the Lord forgave you.
3.14: Add the giving of yourselves to others to all of these things. This binds them all together in perfect unity.
3.15: Let the peace of Christ direct your hearts. God called you in one body to peace. Be thankful.
3.16: Let the teaching of Christ live among you in an abundant way. Use all wisdom to teach and warn one another with psalms, songs of praise, and spiritual songs, singing to God with your hearts.
3.17: Everything you say or do should be done by the authority of the Lord Jesus. Thank God, the Father, through Christ.
3.18: Wives, subject yourselves to your husbands. This is what the Lord wants.
3.19: Husbands, give yourselves to your wives for their good, expecting nothing in return. Don't be bitter with them.
3.20: Children, in everything obey your parents. This is pleasing to the Lord.
3.21: Fathers, don't make your children bitter or they will give up.
3.22: Slaves, in everything obey your human masters. Don't serve them only when they are looking, like slaves who are trying to please men. Instead, serve with a sincere heart, showing respect for the Lord.
3.23: Whatever you do, work at it; really try hard as if it were for the Lord, not men.
3.24: Be a slave to Christ, the master. You know you will receive a reward from the Lord; it will be an inheritance.
3.25: Anyone who does wrong will be paid back for his wrong. And to God everyone is the same.

4.1: Masters, treat your slaves well and fairly. Remember, you have a Master in heaven too.
4.2: Continue in prayer. Be alert. Be thankful.
4.3: Pray for us too. Pray that God will give us an opportunity to share the word, to talk about the secret of Christ. That is why I am tied up in chains.
4.4: I want to make the message clear, as I should.
4.5: Live wisely in front of outsiders. Take advantage of every opportunity.
4.6: Your message should always be beautiful, flavored with salt. You should learn how you must answer each person.
4.7: Tychicus will tell you all of the news about me. He is our brother, faithful slave and co - slave in the Lord, to whom we give ourselves.
4.8: That is why I sent him to you. Then you will find out everything that is happening to us. He will encourage your hearts.
4.9: With him is Onesimus, the dear, faithful brother. He is one of your own number. They will tell you everything that is happening here.
4.10: Aristarchus, my cellmate, greets you. Mark, the cousin of Barnabas, greets you too. You have already received instructions about him. If he comes to you, welcome him.
4.11: Jesus ( the one called Justus ) sends his greetings. These are the only Jews who are my co - workers in the kingdom of God here. They have been very helpful to me.
4.12: Epaphras greets you. He is one of your own and a slave of Christ Jesus. He is always wrestling in his prayers for you. He wants you to stand complete, totally sure of everything that God wants.
4.13: I'll tell you the truth about him: he works very hard for you and the believers in the towns of Laodicea and Hierapolis!
4.14: Luke, the doctor to whom I give myself, greets you. Demas does too.
4.15: Greet the brothers in Laodicea. Greet Nympha and the group that meets in her home.
4.16: After this letter has been read to all of you, see that it is read to the called out group in Laodicea. Then you can read the letter which they received.
4.17: Tell this to Archippus: " Be sure that you finish the work you received in the Lord! "
4.18: I write this with my own hand: " Greetings from Paul. Remember my chains. " May help in time of need be with you.

1.1: From Paul, Silas, and Timothy. To the called out people of the Thessalonians in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ. Help in time of need and peace to you.
1.2: We always thank God for all of you. We continually mention you in our prayers.
1.3: Before our God and Father, we remember the effort that came from your faith, the hard work that came from your giving of yourselves to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, and your endurance which comes from the hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.
1.4: Brothers and sisters, God gives Himself to you, for your good, expecting nothing in return. You know He has chosen you.
1.5: How did our good news come to you? It came not only with talk but also with power, the Holy Spirit, and with much conviction. You know how we lived among you for your sake.
1.6: You copied us and the Lord Jesus. Even during much suffering, you accepted the message with the joy that comes from the Holy Spirit.
1.7: So you became an example to all of the believers in the areas of Macedonia and Achaia.
1.8: The Lord's message rang out from you. The news about your faith in God has gone out too. Not only did it go to Macedonia and Achaia, it went everywhere! We don't have to talk about it,
1.9: because people tell us about how we came in among you and how you turned away from false gods to God. Now you are serving the true, living God
1.10: and waiting for His Son to come from heaven. Jesus, whom God raised from death, will rescue us from the punishment that is coming from God.

2.1: Brothers, you know that our stay among you was fruitful.
2.2: Before we arrived there, as you know, we had suffered and had been insulted in the city of Philippi. But with our God's help, we dared to tell you God's Good News, even when some people strongly opposed us.
2.3: Our plea does not come from false, impure, or tricky motives.
2.4: No, we talk like men who have been tested by God. He trusted us with the Good News. We don't talk like men who are trying to please men. No, God tests our hearts.
2.5: In the past you know we never used flattery. We didn't try to look good to get your money. God knows this is true!
2.6: We were not looking for glory from men — not from you nor anyone else.
2.7: As Christ's delegates, we could have been hard on you, but we were gentle among you, like a mother taking care of her children.
2.8: We gave ourselves to you for your good, expecting nothing in return. It was a pleasure to share with you not only God's Good News, but also our lives. You had become precious to us.
2.9: Brothers, do you remember our hard work? We were exhausted. We worked night and day; we didn't want to be a burden to you while we preached God's Good News to you.
2.10: We were pure, being made right, and without guilt among you believers. You know it and God knows it!
2.11: You know that we treated each one of you as a father treats his own children.
2.12: We encouraged you, comforted you, and told you to live your lives worthy of God who called you into His kingdom and glory.
2.13: This is why we continually thank God: when you received God's message that you heard from us, you accepted it as the true message of God, not as a human message. It is working in you believers.
2.14: Brothers, you became imitators of God's called out people which are in Christ Jesus in the land of Judea. Your own countrymen make you suffer in the same way that the Judeans make them suffer.
2.15: They killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets. They drove us out. They are not pleasing God and they are against all men.
2.16: They try to stop us from talking to non - Jewish people to keep them from being saved. They are always piling up their sins. God's punishment has finally come upon them.
2.17: Brothers, we were forced to leave you for a short time. ( This was in body, not in spirit. ) With a strong desire, we tried very hard to see you face to face.
2.18: Several times even I, Paul, wanted to come to you but Satan stopped us.
2.19: What are we hoping for? What would make us happy? What is the crown we will take pride in before our Lord Jesus when he returns? It is you!
2.20: You are our glory, our joy.

3.1: We decided to stay behind alone in Athens. But, when we could wait no longer,
3.2: we sent Timothy. He is our brother and God's co - worker for the Good News of Christ. We wanted him to help your faith and make you strong.
3.3: We didn't want anyone to be shaken by these troubles. You know that we must be ready for this.
3.4: When we were with you, we told you ahead of time: " We are about to be persecuted. " And, as you know, it happened.
3.5: That is why I couldn't wait any longer; I sent Timothy to find out if your faith was strong. The Tempter could have tempted you and our hard work would have been wasted.
3.6: But Timothy has just now come back from you to us. He has told us the news about your faith and giving of self to others for their good, expecting nothing in return; that you always have good memories of us and yearn to see us, just as much as we want to see you.
3.7: Brothers, this is why your faith encouraged us, even though we are in trouble and suffering.
3.8: If you stand in the Lord, we feel alive now.
3.9: We cannot thank God enough. Can we repay our God for all of the happiness we have before Him because of you?
3.10: Day and night we are praying very hard that we will see your faces and supply anything that is missing in your faith.
3.11: May God Himself, our Father, and our Lord Jesus prepare a way for us to come to you.
3.12: May the Lord make your giving of self to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, grow and overflow to one another and everyone else, just as ours does toward you.
3.13: May the Lord make your spirits strong, without guilt, and holy before God, our Father, when our Lord Jesus returns with all his saints.

4.1: Finally, brothers, we gave you instructions about how you must live to please God. You are living that way now. We are asking — yes, begging you in the Lord Jesus to do even more!
4.2: You know some of the instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
4.3: This is what God wants: You must be holy. Stay away from unlawful sexual intercourse.
4.4: Each one of you should know how to control his own body, with holiness and honor.
4.5: This should not be with a lustful desire, like people of the world who don't know God.
4.6: No one should take advantage of or cheat his brother. The Lord will punish those who do such things, as we told you before and warned you.
4.7: God did not call us to be unholy, but to be holy.
4.8: So the person who rejects this is not rejecting man, but God. God gives His Holy Spirit to you.
4.9: We don't need to write you about loving your brothers. God has already taught you how to give yourself to one another, for his good, expecting nothing in return;
4.10: you are doing this to all the brothers throughout Macedonia. Brothers, we beg you, to do this even more!
4.11: Try to live a quiet life. Mind your own business. Work with your own hands, as we told you.
4.12: Then outsiders will respect the way you live. You will not be dependent on anyone.
4.13: Brothers, I want you to know the truth about the people who have already died. Then you will not be sad like others who have no hope.
4.14: Since we believe that Jesus died and came back to life, through him, in the same way, God will bring along with Jesus those who have died.
4.15: We are telling you the Lord's teaching: when the Lord Jesus returns, we — who are still alive on earth — will not go ahead of those who have already died.
4.16: The Lord himself will come down from heaven with a command, with the voice of the angel leader, and with the sound of God's trumpet. The dead people in Christ will be the first to rise from death.
4.17: Then we who are still alive on earth will be gathered up with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will always be with the Lord.
4.18: Therefore comfort one another with these words.

5.1: Brothers, we don't need to write you about dates and times
5.2: because you know very well that the Day of the Lord will come suddenly, like a robber in the night.
5.3: People will say, " Things are peaceful and safe. " That's when destruction will suddenly hit them. It will be like when the birth pain comes to a pregnant woman. They won't be able to run away.
5.4: But, brothers, you are not in the dark. That Day will not surprise you as a robber does.
5.5: All of you are sons of light and sons of daytime. We do not belong with the night or darkness.
5.6: So we should not be asleep like others are. No, we should be awake and alert.
5.7: Sleepers sleep at night; drinkers get drunk at night.
5.8: But since we belong to the day, let us be self - controlled, putting on faith and giving ourselves to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, as a chest - plate, and the hope of safety from danger as a helmet.
5.9: God did not plan for us to be punished, but to have safety from danger through our Lord Jesus Christ.
5.10: Whether we are awake or asleep, Christ died for us so that we will live together with him.
5.11: So comfort one another. Continue building each other up, just as you are doing now.
5.12: Brothers, we beg you to respect those who are working hard among you. They are leading you in the Lord and warning you.
5.13: Because of their work, treat them with the greatest honor in giving of self to others for their good, expecting nothing in return. Be at peace with one another.
5.14: Brothers, we beg you, warn those who are lazy. Comfort people who are afraid. Help the weaker ones. Be patient with everyone.
5.15: Be sure that no one pays back wrong with a wrong. Instead, always try to do good to one another and to everyone.
5.18: Thank God at all times. This is what God wants for you in Christ Jesus.
5.19: Don't put out the fire of the Spirit.
5.21: Test everything; keep what is good.
5.22: Stay away from every kind of evil — even from what looks like evil.
5.23: The God of peace Himself will make you completely holy. May He keep your spirit, soul, and body whole without guilt until our Lord Jesus Christ comes.
5.24: And he will come! God is the One who calls you. He is faithful.
5.26: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss of friendship.
5.27: Before the Lord, I order you to have this letter read to all the brothers.
5.28: May the help in time of need of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

1.1: From Paul, Silas, and Timothy. To the called out people of the Thessalonians in God our Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.2: May help in time of need and peace come to you from God, our Father, and from the Lord, Jesus Christ.
1.3: We should always thank God for you, brothers and sisters. We really should, because your faith is growing fast. The giving of yourselves to everyone among you, for his good, expecting nothing in return, is also becoming stronger.
1.4: So among God's called out people, we are proud of you. You are going through persecutions and troubles. We tell them how you still believe and endure.
1.5: This shows that God's judgment is right. You are suffering for the kingdom of God. So you are worthy of it.
1.6: God is fair. He will give trouble to those who make trouble for you.
1.7: But to those of you who are having trouble, He will also give you — and us — rest! The Lord Jesus will be revealed from heaven with his powerful angels.
1.8: He will come with a flaming fire. He will punish the people who do not acknowledge God and those who don't obey the Good News of our Lord Jesus.
1.9: They will be punished with eternal destruction — away from the Lord and from the glory of his strength.
1.10: Jesus will come so that his saints may give him glory. His coming will mean splendor unimaginable. On that day you will be there too, because you believed our story.
1.11: This is why we always pray for you. Our God called you; we want Him to make you worthy of that! May God also accomplish in a powerful way all of the good you want to do and every action that comes from your faith.
1.12: In this way, the name of our Lord Jesus will be honored by you and you will be honored by him. All this was made possible by the help in time of need of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

2.1: Our Lord Jesus Christ is coming. And we will be gathered together with him. But, brothers, we beg you
2.2: not to allow your minds to be alarmed or quickly upset. Perhaps some spirit, message, or letter said, " The Day of the Lord has already come! " We sent no such letter.
2.3: Don't let anyone fool you like that because " the falling away " must come first. The lawless man, the son of destruction, will be revealed then.
2.4: He will be against everything that people worship or think is divine. He will lift himself above all of these things. He will even sit in God's temple sanctuary, claiming that he is God.
2.5: Surely you remember when I was still with you that I always told you these things.
2.6: And now, you know what is holding the lawless man back — he must be revealed at the proper time.
2.7: Lawlessness is already working in secrecy. Someone is holding it back. Until that changes, nothing will happen.
2.8: Only then will the lawless man be revealed. The Lord Jesus will kill him with a blast from his mouth. When Jesus comes with splendor, Jesus will destroy him.
2.9: The lawless man will come with Satan's power. He will use all kinds of false powers, proofs, and miracles.
2.10: There will be every kind of evil to fool the people who are being destroyed. Why? Because they did not give themselves to the truth expecting nothing in return, so that they could be saved.
2.11: This is why God sends them a deceiving power so that they will believe the lie.
2.12: Then all people who did not believe the truth will be condemned. They enjoyed sin.
2.13: But we should always thank God for you, brothers. The Lord gives himself to you, for your good, expecting nothing in return. God planned for you to be saved. You are His first crop. You believed the truth, and the Spirit made you holy.
2.14: Using our Good News, God called you into this. He wanted you to have the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
2.15: So, brothers, stand firm! We have spoken to you and written a letter. Hold onto the things we taught you.
2.16: Our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our Father will encourage your hearts and make you strong in every good word and deed. He gave Himself to us for our good, expecting nothing in return and, with help in time of need, gave us eternal comfort and good hope.
2.17: [ no verse]

3.1: Finally, brothers, pray for us. Pray that the Lord's message will spread fast and be honored just as it was with you.
3.2: Pray that we will be rescued from unfair, evil men. Not all people are of the faith.
3.3: But the Lord is faithful; He will protect you from the evil one. The Lord will make you strong.
3.4: We trust the Lord that you are doing — and will do — the things we instructed you to do.
3.5: May the Lord guide your hearts into God's giving of Himself to you, for your good, expecting nothing in return, and the endurance of Christ.
3.6: Brothers, by the authority of the Lord Jesus Christ, we order you to withdraw from any brother who is a lazy person, a troublemaker. He is not living the way we taught you to live.
3.7: You know how you ought to act — like us! We were always busy among you.
3.8: We never ate the food of anybody, unless we paid for it! No, night and day we worked hard to the point of exhaustion. Why? So we wouldn't be a burden to any of you.
3.9: We have the right to be paid but we wanted to be an example for you to follow.
3.10: Even when we were with you, we gave you this order: " If a person doesn't want to work, then don't let him eat! "
3.11: We hear that some men among you are living lazy lives; they are not working. Instead, they keep other people from working.
3.12: By the Lord Jesus Christ, we order — even beg — you people, " Get to work! Quietly earn your own living. "
3.13: Brothers, never get tired of doing good.
3.14: If someone won't obey our teaching in this letter, give him notice. Don't associate with him! Then he will feel ashamed.
3.15: Don't think of him as an enemy; warn him as you would a brother.
3.16: May the Lord of peace Himself always give you peace in every way. May the Lord be with all of you.
3.17: This is the way I write: " Greetings from Paul! This was with my own hand. " It is my signature on every letter.
3.18: May the help in time of need of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.

1.1: From Paul. I am a delegate of Christ Jesus. God our Savior and Christ Jesus, our hope ordered this.
1.2: To Timothy, my true son in the faith. May God, our Father, and Christ Jesus, our Lord, give you help in time of need, mercy, and peace.
1.3: While I was traveling to the Macedonian area, I urged you to stay in the city of Ephesus. Some men there are teaching a different teaching. I want you to order them to stop doing this.
1.4: They should not hold onto myths or endless lists of ancestors. These cause arguments. They are not helping God's plan which comes by faith.
1.5: Giving yourself to others, for their good, expecting nothing in return, is the real reason for this command. It comes from a pure heart, a good conscience, and honest faith.
1.6: Some of them have wandered away. They are lost in empty talk.
1.7: They want to be teachers of the law, but they don't understand what they are talking about or the things they are so sure of.
1.8: We know that the law is good if a person uses it rightly.
1.9: We also know this: the law was not made for a good man but for people who are lawless, rebels, ungodly, sinners, unholy, not religious, father - killers, mother - killers, murderers,
1.10: sexual sinners, homosexuals, slave traders, liars, and those who break promises. These and other things are against the healthy teaching
1.11: as found in the glorious Good News of the blessed God which He trusted to me.
1.12: I am thankful to Christ Jesus our Lord who gave me power. He thought I was faithful so he appointed me for this work.
1.13: In the past I said evil things against God. I was a persecutor and a man of violence. But I received mercy because, when I was an unbeliever, I didn't know what I was doing.
1.14: Then the help in time of need of our Lord came upon me like a flood, with the faith and the giving of self to others for their good, expecting nothing in return, which are in Christ Jesus.
1.15: This statement is something you can trust; it is worth complete acceptance: " Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners. " I am the worst one
1.16: but, because of this, I received mercy. Christ Jesus wanted to show all his patience in me, the worst sinner. This was an example for those who were about to believe in him for eternal life.
1.17: Give honor and glory forever and ever to the eternal King who cannot die or be seen, the only God. Amen.
1.18: Timothy, my son, I give you this instruction. It is like the prophecies which were made earlier about you. Use them to fight the good fight.
1.19: Hold onto the faith and a good conscience, which some people have rejected. They wrecked their faith, like a ship at sea.
1.20: Some of them are Hymenaeus and Alexander. I gave them to Satan so that they could be corrected and not say evil things against God anymore.

2.1: First of all, I beg you to pray for all people. Ask for things. Speak for them. Be thankful to God for them.
2.2: Pray for kings and all those who have authority so that we may lead peaceful, quiet lives. We want to be godly and serious.
2.3: This is good and acceptable before God, our Savior.
2.4: God wants all men to be saved and to begin understanding the truth.
2.5: There is one God. There is one go - between between God and men — the man Christ Jesus.
2.6: Christ gave himself for everyone. He was the price. That was God's proof given at the right time.
2.7: This is why I was made a preacher, a delegate, ( I speak the truth; I'm not lying. ) and a teacher of people who are not Jewish. I teach about faith and truth.
2.8: Everywhere I want men lifting up holy hands to pray. No anger. No arguing.
2.9: In the same way, I want the women to dress modestly. They should use good sense and be proper, avoiding fancy hairdos and gold, or pearls, or expensive clothes.
2.10: Instead, use good deeds to be beautiful. Do what godly women think is right.
2.11: A woman must learn quietly and with all submission.
2.12: I don't allow a woman to teach a man nor rule over him. No, she should be quiet.
2.13: Adam was made first. Eve was made next.
2.14: Also, Adam was not seduced; the woman was. She fell into sin.
